2.en:
**I have heard thee.** This verse is a parenthetical comment on the reception of divine grace (v. 1). It constitutes an urgent appeal to men to seek reconciliation with God lest they receive the grace of God in vain. The quotation is from the LXX of Isa. 49:8 (see comment there). Isaiah looks forward to the “day of salvation” as the time of the Messiah. Paul here recognizes that the prophecy has been fulfilled in Christ. The first advent of Christ ushered in an era that is favorable to salvation (see DA 37). So long as Christ intercedes for sinners the “day of salvation” will continue.
**Succoured.** That is, helped.
**Accepted time.** That is, a time when repentant sinners will be received (see on Isa. 49:8).
**Day of salvation.** That is, the time during which the light of probation lingers (see John 12:35). Eventually the day of mercy will close, and when it does there will be no second chance for those who have spurned God’s grace. Men often procrastinate because they think the day of salvation will continue indefinitely, that temporal matters require first consideration, that pleasure must be pursued, that it will be easier to repent and believe tomorrow than it is today. They forget that the only time man has for salvation and for victory over any sin is the present moment, and that victory postponed becomes defeat. Delay is both foolish and dangerous. Life may be cut short; deterioration of mind and body may make attention to spiritual things difficult or impossible. The heart may be fatally hardened and the desire for salvation lost; the Holy Spirit may cease to strive. Procrastination is ultimately equivalent to rejection.
2.zh:
因為他說：在悅納的時候，我應允了你；在拯救的日子，我搭救了你。看哪！現在正是悅納的時候；現在正是拯救的日子。

**在悅納的時候。**指悔改的罪人被接納的時候（見賽49:8註釋）。
**我應允了你。**本節補充說明了領受上帝的恩典（1節），強烈呼籲人能與上帝和好，免得徒受上帝的恩典。引文系七十士譯本的賽49:8（見該節註釋）。以賽亞展望“拯救的日子”為彌賽亞的時期。保羅在這裡承認預言應驗在基督身上。基督第一次降臨開創了有利於得救的時代（見《歷代願望》37頁）。只要基督為罪人代求，“拯救的日子”就必繼續。
**在拯救的日子。**就是在寬容之燈依然點亮的時候（見約12:35）。恩典的時期終將結束。那時棄絕上帝恩典的人就再也沒有機會了。人常常拖延，以為拯救的日子是無限延伸的，而暫時的事需要優先考慮，必須追求快樂，明天悔改相信總比今天容易。他們忘記了人得救和戰勝罪惡的唯一時間就是現在；拖延勝利就是失敗。拖延是愚蠢而危險的。壽命可能縮短。體力和智力的衰退會使人難以或不可能關注屬靈的事物。心地也可能剛硬得不可救藥。得救的願望喪失了。聖靈不再感動他。拖延最終等於拒絕。
**搭救。**就是幫助。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《福山寶訓》第151頁；《拾級就主》第34頁；《證言》卷二第102頁；《證言》卷五第635頁；《證言》卷九第129頁。

15.en:
**Concord.** Gr. sumphōnēsis, “concord,” “agreement.” Concerning the related word sumphōnia see on Luke 15:25. Between Christ and Satan there is utter discord.
**Belial.** Gr. Belial, a transliteration from the Heb. beliya‘al, “worthless one” (see on Deut. 13:13; Judges 19:22; 1 Sam. 2:12). However, textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the reading Beliar. The reading Belial appears only in few late manuscripts and probably entered KJV by way of the Latin Vulgate. Here the word is a personification for Satan, representing the worthlessness and emptiness of the things by means of which he seeks to attract and lure men into sin. It is also used of the followers of Satan (Deut. 15:9, margin; 1 Sam. 25:25; 30:22; Ps. 41:8, margin). Christ and Belial are the opposing leaders in the great controversy between righteousness and unrighteousness (Rev. 12:7–9; cf. ch. 20:7–9). Sin is not an abstract thing. Back of all that is true, holy, and righteous are the supernatural forces of the universe led by Christ. Back of all that is evil and worthless are the supernatural forces of darkness led by Satan. All the world is lined up behind one or the other (1 Peter 5:8–9; Rev. 12:11).
Man’s choice between these two world rulers must be clear and decided. Christ is the Prince of light (John 1:9; 8:12). His followers are called the children of light (Matt. 5:14; John 12:36; Eph. 5:8). They walk in the light, and their destiny is the city of light, where there is no darkness at all (John 12:35, 36; 1 Thess. 5:4, 5; 1 John 1:5–7; Rev. 22:5). Satan is the prince of darkness (Col. 1:13). His followers are the children of darkness (John 3:19; Eph. 5:11). They walk in darkness now, and their destiny is eternal darkness (Matt. 22:13; 25:30; 2 Peter 2:17; 1 John 1:6; Jude 13).
15.zh:
基督和彼列（彼列就是撒但的別名）有什麼相和呢？信主的和不信主的有什麼相干呢？

**彼列。**Belial，希伯來詞beliya`al的音譯，“沒有價值的人”（見申13:13；士19:22；撒上2:12註釋）。有文本為Beliar。該詞在這裡指撒但，表示撒但企圖用無價值、虛空的事物吸引誘惑人犯罪。也用來指撒但的隨從（申15:9旁註；撒上25:25；30:22；詩41:8邊注）。基督和彼列是義和不義大斗爭中對立的領袖（啟12:7-9；參啟20:7-9）。罪惡並不是抽象的。在所有真實，聖潔和公義的事物背後，是基督所領導的宇宙超自然力量。在所有邪惡無價值的事物背後，是撒但所領導的黑暗超自然勢力。全世界的人都列在一方或另一方（彼前5:8-9；啟12:11）。
人在這兩位世界統治者之間的選擇必然是明確的。基督是光明之君（約1:9；8:12）。祂的信徒被稱為光明之子（太5:14；約12:36；弗5:8）。他們行在光中。他們的前途是光明之城。那裡毫無黑暗（西1:13）。撒但是黑暗之君（西1:13）。他的隨從者是黑暗之子（約3:19；弗5:11）。他們行在黑暗中。他們的命運是永遠的黑暗（太22:13；25:30；彼後2:17；約壹1:6；猶13）。
**相和。**sumphōnēsis，“一致”，“協議”。其相關詞sumphōnia見路15:25註釋。基督和撒但之間絕不相會妥協。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第330頁；《證言》卷一第279，289，408頁；《證言》卷二第168，344頁；《證言》卷四第187頁；《證言》卷五第52，340頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–16節）**。《先祖與先知》第563頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–18節）**。《證言》卷五第431頁。

14.en:
**Be ye not.** Literally, “do not become.” Chapters 6:14 to 7:1 constitute an extended parenthesis such as occurs often in the writings of Paul. It consists of a warning against any and every kind of association with unbelievers that would place Christians in situations where they find it difficult or impossible to avoid compromising principle. This prohibition includes the marriage relationship (see on ch. 7:1), but is by no means restricted to it. The admonition of this parenthetical passage was probably suggested to Paul’s mind by his counsel in ch. 6:12, 13, not to be narrowhearted and exclusive. If so, his purpose was to leave the Corinthians no reason for concluding that they were to be so largehearted as to enter into intimate fellowship with unbelievers. The fact that v. 14 begins with the words “do not become” indicates that Paul was thinking primarily of the future, rather than of the past.
**Unequally yoked.** Gr. heterozugeō, “to yoke in unequal partnership.” The prefix hetero– here denotes persons of a different kind (cf. on Matt. 6:24). In view of the fact that Paul is addressing the Corinthian church members as Christians, the others referred to are non-Christians. The principle here stated is similar to that of Ex. 34:16; Deut. 7:1–3; cf. Lev. 19:19; Deut. 22:10; Phil. 4:3. So great is the difference in ideals and conduct between Christians and non-Christians, believers and unbelievers, that to enter into any binding relationship with them, whether in marriage, in business, or otherwise, inevitably confronts the Christians with the alternatives of abandoning principle or enduring difficulties occasioned by differences in belief and conduct. To enter into such a union is to obey God and to bargain with the devil. Separateness from sin and sinners is explicitly set forth throughout the Scriptures (Lev. 20:24; Num. 6:3; Heb. 7:26; etc.). No other principle has been more strictly enjoined by God. Throughout the history of God’s people the violation of this principle has inevitably resulted in spiritual disaster.
**With unbelievers.** To those who do not accept Christ as their Saviour, and His teachings as their standard of belief and conduct, the ideals, principles, and practice of Christianity are foolishness (1 Cor. 1:18). By reason of their outlook on life, unbelievers often find it most difficult to tolerate a pattern of conduct that tends to restrict their own ways of living, or implies that their concepts and practices are evil or inferior. Paul does not forbid all association with unbelievers, but only such association as would tend to diminish the Christian’s love for God, to adulterate the purity of his outlook on life, or to lead him to deviate from a strict pattern of conduct. Christians are not to shun their relatives and friends, but to associate with them as living examples of applied Christianity and so win them to Christ (1 Cor. 5:9, 10; 7:12; (10:27). The decisive question is, Does the Christian choose to associate with the unbeliever because of a fondness for the ways of the world, or because of a sincere desire to be a blessing to the unbeliever and to win him to Christ? A second question, and one of no less importance to the Christian himself, is, Whose influence is likely to prevail, that of Christ or that of the evil one? When it comes to a binding relationship such as marriage, however, the Christian who truly loves the Lord will under no circumstances unite with an unbeliever, even in the pious and otherwise commendable hope of winning him to Christ.
Almost without exception disappointment is the result of a course of action contrary to the wise counsel here set forth by the apostle. Those who choose to heed this counsel may expect in a special way to enjoy God’s favor, and will find that He has something in store for them far surpassing any plans they might have had for themselves.
**What fellowship?** By a series of five rhetorical questions (vs. 14–16) Paul contrasts the irreconcilable and mutually exclusive opposition between the yoke of Christ and that of the world. Every union in which the character, beliefs, and interests of the Christian lose anything of their distinctiveness and integrity, is hereby prohibited. A Christian cannot afford to enter into any connection with the world that calls for compromise. The line of demarcation is clearly defined between (1) righteousness and unrighteousness, (2) light and darkness, (3) Christ and Satan, (4) faith and infidelity, (5) the temple of God and the temple of idols.
14.zh:
你們和不信的原不相配，不要同負一軛。義和不義有什麼相交呢？光明和黑暗有什麼相通呢？

**你們……原不。**林後6:14至7:1是一大段插入語。這種結構在保羅的書信中經常出現。它包括警告基督徒不要與不信的人結交，因為這會使他們難以甚至無法避免在原則上妥協。這一禁令包括婚姻的關係（見林後7:1註釋），但不限於婚姻關係。這段插入的警告可能暗示了保羅林後6:12,13勸勉的思想，即不要狹隘和排外。若是這樣，他的目的就是不讓哥林多信徒有理由認定他們應該心胸寬廣到與不信之人親密結交。事實上14節開頭的“原不”，說明保羅所想的主要是將來，而不是過去。
**和不信的。**不接受基督為救主，不以祂的教訓為他們信仰與行為，以及基督教的理想，原則和實踐的標準，這樣做乃是愚蠢的（林前1:18）。不信的人由於其人生觀，往往很難容忍那約束他們生活方式、暗示他們的觀念和作法是錯誤或低劣的行為模式。保羅沒有禁止他們與不信之人的所有結交，只是禁止那種會減少基督徒對上帝的愛，在純正的人生觀中摻入雜質，或使他們偏離純正行為方式的交往。基督徒不是要避開他們的親友，而要與他們交往，作為應用基督教的典範，爭取他們歸向基督（林前5:9,10；7:12；10:27）。關鍵的問題是，基督徒選擇與不信的人交往，是因為喜愛世人的方式呢？還是誠心要將福氣帶給不信的人，爭取他們歸向基督呢？第二個問題對於基督徒本身也很重要，就是誰的影響佔上風，是基督還是那惡者？但是在涉及婚姻結合這樣的關係時，真正愛主的基督徒決不會與不信的人結合，即使抱著誠心爭取對方歸向基督的良好願望。
凡與使徒本段的明智勸勉背道而馳的人，結果毫無例外都是失望。而那些選擇留意這勸勉的人，則能以特殊的方式享受上帝的悅納，並發現為他們所儲備的東西，遠遠超過他們所能為自己打算的。
**不相配。**heterozuge，“負軛不般配”。前綴hetero-在這裡指不同種類的人（參太6:24）。鑑於保羅是寫信給以哥林多教會的基督徒，另一等人就是指非基督徒了。這裡所闡明的原則與出34:16；申7:1-3；參利19:19；申22:10；腓4:3相似。基督徒和非基督徒，信和不信的人之間在觀念和行為上的區別非常大。與他們建立任何關係，無論是婚姻、生意或其他關係，基督徒都無可避免地會面臨放棄原則，忍受信仰和行為的差異所造成分歧的可能性。進行這樣的結合，就會悖逆上帝，與魔鬼妥協。聖經一貫清楚地教導我們要與罪和罪人分離（利20:24；民6:3；來7:26等）。上帝所囑咐的原則，沒有比這更嚴格的了。從上帝子民的整個歷史中可以看出，違背這項原則必然導致屬靈的災難。
**有什麼相交呢。**保羅用連續五個反問句（14-16節），說明了基督之軛和屬世之軛的不可協調性和相互排斥性。任何結合若使基督徒的品格，信仰和旨趣喪失其獨特性和完整性，都屬禁止之列。基督徒不可與世人建立起任何需要妥協的關係。以下的界限是非常分明的：一，義和不義；二，光明和黑暗；三，基督和撒但，四，信和不信；五，上帝的殿和偶像的殿。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《拾級就主》第38頁；《佈道論》第617頁；《懷愛倫傳略》第321頁；《先祖與先知》第175頁；《證言》卷一第200頁；《證言》卷二第44，689頁；《證言》卷四第504，505頁；《證言》卷七第108頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–15節）**。《基督教育原理》第476頁；《傳道良助》第392頁；《先知與君王》第58頁；《給傳道人的證言》第271頁；《證言》卷二第48頁；《證言》卷三第248頁；《證言》卷四第346頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–16節）**。《醫療佈道論》第45頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–18節）**。《基督教育原理》第499，533頁；《服務真詮》第404頁；《證言》卷三第373頁；《證言》卷五第13，364頁；《證言》卷六第195頁；《證言》卷八第223頁。

16.en:
**Agreement.** Or, “assent,” “consent” (Luke 23:51). There can be no alliance between Christ and Satan, between the true God and false gods, between Christianity and heathenism. Paul declares that an alliance between believers and unbelievers is equally inconceivable.
**Ye are the temple.** See on 1 Cor. 3:16, 17; 6:19, 20.
**I will dwell.** Quoting from Lev. 26:11, 12 Paul draws an analogy between the Jewish Temple and the Christian church. The Temple at Jerusalem was built for the glory of Jehovah, was honored by the glory of His presence, in the Shekinah, and was His dwelling place (1 Kings 6:12, 13; cf. Ex. 25:8; 29:43–45; Heb. 8:1, 2). The church is composed of those who have been born into Christ (Heb. 3:6; 12:23). They constitute the body of Christ (Col. 1:24), who is the head (Eph. 1:22). He purposes to dwell in them as He did in the Temple of old (1 Cor. 3:16, 17; 6:19, 20); but how can He do so if they are in “agreement”with idols?
**Be their God.** This formula, “I will be their God, and they shall be my people,” occurs commonly throughout the OT, and constitutes a declaration of the covenant relationship into which God purposed to enter with Israel of old (see on Hosea 1:9, 10, and now purposes to enter with His people today.
16.zh:
神的殿和偶像有什麼相同呢？因為我們是永生神的殿，就如神曾說：我要在他們中間居住，在他們中間來往；我要作他們的神；他們要作我的子民。

**相同。**“贊成”，“同意”（路23:51）。基督和撒但之間，真神和假神之間，基督徒和異教徒之間不可能結盟。保羅說，信與不信的人結盟是無法想象的。
**我們是永生上帝的殿。**見林前3:16,17；6:19,20註釋。
**我要在他們中間居住。**保羅引用利26:11,12，將猶太人的聖殿與基督教會進行對比。耶路撒冷的聖殿是為耶和華的榮耀而建造的，被祂臨格的榮光所尊榮，是祂的居所（王上6:12,13；參出25:8；29:43-45；來8:1,2）。教會是由重生歸入基督的人所組成（來3:6；12:23）。他們構成基督的身體（西1:24）。基督是頭（弗1:22）。祂願意住在他們中間，就像古時住在聖殿中一樣（林前3:16,17；6:19,20）。但是如果他們與偶像“相同”， 祂又怎能住在其中呢？
**作他們的上帝。**《舊約》中經常出現“我要做他們的上帝，他們要作我的子民”的說法，表達了上帝願意與古代以色列人立約（見何1:9,10的註釋）。現在祂也願意與祂今天的子民立約。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第161，311頁；《教育論》第258頁；《傳道良助》第254頁；《服務真詮》第146頁；《給傳道人的證言》第388頁；《論福利工作》第130頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–18節）**。《基督教育原理》第480頁；《給傳道人的證言》第272頁。

17.en: **Wherefore come out.** Paul here combines various OT passages such as Isa. 52:11–12; Jer. 51:6, 45. The historical reference is to the departure of captive Israelites from ancient Babylon, which Paul here refers to as an illustration of the separation of God’s people from the world and from spiritual Babylon (see on Rev. 18:4). Upon their return from captivity the Jews were charged not to carry back with them anything savoring of pagan idolatry. Similarly, spiritual Israel is charged to “touch not the unclean thing” (see on Isa. 52:11, 12).
17.zh:
又說：你們務要從他們中間出來，與他們分別；不要沾不潔淨的物，我就收納你們。

保羅在這裡把幾處《舊約》經文結合起來，如賽52:11-12，耶51:6,45。在歷史上是指被虜的以色列人從古巴比倫出來。保羅這裡是指上帝的兒女與世界和屬靈的巴比倫中分離（見啟18:4註釋）。猶太人從被虜之地迴歸時，奉命不要帶回任何具有異教偶像崇拜色彩的東西。同樣，屬靈的以色列人也奉命“不要沾不潔淨的物”（見賽52:11,12註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《健康勉言》第291，589頁；《基督教育之研究》第328頁；《早期著作》第242頁；《基督教育原理》第311，483，501頁；《給青年人的信息》第313頁；《先祖與先知》第458頁；《救贖的故事》第60頁；《論節制》第119頁；《證言》卷一第242，279，288，405，503頁；《證言》卷二第48，125頁；《證言》卷三第126，458頁；《證言》卷四第577，583頁；《證言》卷六第95，147頁。

1.zh:
我們與神同工的，也勸你們不可徒受他的恩典。

**同工。**合作的原則對於個人的屬靈成就和基督徒服務的成功是很重要的。上帝需要人自願的合作（《歷代願望》535頁）。人行善的能力完全取決於他與上帝合作的程度（參約5:19,30；《歷代願望》297頁）。基督的傳道人和工人不是要靠著自己的力量和智慧來工作。上帝沒有讓他們採用自己的策略或資源。基督與祂使者之間的這種合作非常緊密而持久，以致“他們能作成全能者的事工”（《歷代願望》327頁）。基督不只是一個觀察者，僅僅在觀望。祂積極參與他們的一切工作（腓2:12,13；參來1:14）。
**徒。**沒有任何積極的目的（參賽55:10,11）。重要的是人接受恩典和持續領受恩典的方式（見太13:23；徒2:41註釋）。
徒受上帝的恩典包括：
一. 忽視它。持續疏忽會使我們的心聽不到上帝的聲音。一本旅行指南對於不認真查閱、不隨從其中指示的鹵莽遊客來說，是沒有價值的。
二. 曲解它用來遮掩罪惡（羅6:1,15）。一些人提出沒有聖經依據的觀點，認為上帝的恩典取消了祂的律法（見羅3:31註釋），作為任意妄為、不順從上帝的藉口（來10:29）。
三. 摻入人的觀念和方法。當人設法藉著拘泥律法的細節在上帝面前賺取功勞時，就徒受了祂的恩典（羅6:14,15；加2:21；5:4；弗2:8,9）。
四. 只從理智上接受，沒有帶到生活中去，沒有給心靈帶來潔淨，使人完全熱切地順從上帝的道。理解卻不應用，就像是研究食物的成分卻不吃一樣（太7:20-24）。
除了第一步稱義之外沒有任何進步，就是徒受上帝的恩典，沒有任何用處。啟動水泵運行是必要的，但啟動本身並不是目的。同樣，上帝賜下恩典使悔改的罪人稱義，是為了使他繼續領受恩典，幫助他過無罪的生活。靠恩稱義只是基督徒生活的開始。
**受。**dechomai，這裡指“欣然領受”，“悅納”，“擁抱”。但在理智上接受上帝的恩典，有可能得不到其好處。基督用撒種在石頭地和荊棘中的比喻說明了這條真理（見太13:5-7註釋）。儘管哥林多信徒曾接受保羅以前的勸勉，與上帝和好，但這還不夠。他們個人的得救還沒有完成。當人與上帝和好時，他的基督徒生活才剛剛開始；他剛與上帝建立了新的關係。在和好的那一刻，他們的確處在得救的狀態中。他們靠上帝的恩典得稱為義。但基督的福音不只是赦免過去的罪，還指望品格的改變，其目標是罪惡無法侵入的生命（見羅6:5-16；林後1:22；3:18註釋）。先是領受上帝的恩典，獲得稱義，接著還要不斷領受恩典，達到成聖。
**恩典。**見羅3:24註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一第381，432頁；《證言》卷六第297頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–4節）**。《服務真詮》第116頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–10節）**。《基督教育原理》第533頁。
1.en:
**Workers together.** The principle of cooperation is vital to personal spiritual accomplishment and to success in Christian service. God does not dispense with man’s voluntary cooperation (DA 535). Man’s capacity for good is completely dependent upon the measure of his cooperation with the divine (cf. John 5:19, 30; DA 297). Christian ministers and workers are not to attempt to labor in their own strength or wisdom, and God does not leave them to their own devices, or to their own resources. This cooperation between Christ and His ambassadors is to be so close and continuous that “they are enabled to do the deeds of Omnipotence” (DA 827). Christ is more than an observer, simply looking on; He is an active partner in all that they do (Phil. 2:12, 13; cf. Heb. 1:14).
**Receive.** Gr. dechomai, here, “to receive favorably,” “to approve,” “to embrace.” It is possible to give mental assent to the grace of God and yet not be benefited by it. This truth Christ illustrated by the seed that feel on stony ground and among thorns (see on Matt. 13:5–7). Even though the Corinthians had responded to Paul’s earlier exhortations and had been reconciled to God, this was not enough. The work of their salvation, individually, was not yet complete. The Christian life has only begun when men are reconciled to God and thereby enter upon a new relationship with Him. It is true that at the moment of reconciliation they are in a saved state. They stand justified by the grace of God. But the gospel of Christ includes much more than the forgiveness of past sins; it envisions, as well, a transformation of character whose goal is a life into which sin does not enter (see on Rom. 6:5–16; 2 Cor. 1:22; 3:18). The initial reception of God’s grace, which brings justification, is to be followed by a continuous reception of grace, which produces sanctification.
**Grace.** See on Rom. 3:24.
**In vain.** That is, without its having served any useful purpose (cf. Isa. 55:10, 11). The important thing is the way man receives grace, and continues to receive it (see on Matt. 13:23; Acts 2:41).
God’s grace is received in vain— 1. When it is neglected. Persistent inattention may deafen the heart to God’s voice. A guidebook for a journey is of little value to a man who blunders along without studying it or following its instructions. 2. When it is perverted by using it as a cloak for sin (Rom. 6:1, 15). The unscriptural argument that God’s grace abrogates His law (see on Rom. 3:31) is advanced by some as an excuse for doing as they please instead of obeying God (see Heb. 10:29). 3. When it is adulterated with human ideas and methods. Men receive God’s grace in vain when they seek to earn merit before God by a punctilious legalism (Rom. 6:14, 15; Gal. 2:21; 5:4; Eph 2:8, 9). 4. When it is received only by the intellect and is not taken into the life; when it does not purify the heart and lead to full and eager obedience to the Word of God. Comprehension without application is like studying food chemistry but neglecting to eat (Matt. 7:20–24).
If there is no advancement beyond the first step of justification, the grace of God has been received in vain. It has served no useful purpose. It is sometimes necessary to prime a pump in order to start it operating, but the priming is not an end in itself. In the same way, God imparts grace to justify the repentant sinner, but only in order to place him in a position where he can receive continuing grace to help him live above sin. Justification by grace is but the beginning of the Christian life.

3.zh:
我們凡事都不叫人有妨礙，免得這職分被人毀謗；

**妨礙。**直譯為“絆倒的機會”。保羅渴望履行自己的職責（參第1節），使人沒有理由因他而拒絕上帝的恩典。所以他自己的生活必須與他所傳的福音完全一致。保羅在3-10節例舉了他的生活與他的信息一致的證據。他使哥林多信徒沒有理由責備他這個傳道人。
**職分。**有文本為“我們的職分”。保羅在這裡所到自己作為基督使者的工作。他經受患難辛勞，研究傳講上帝的道，避免任何引起敵意的機會（林前8:13；10:32,33；腓2:15；帖前2:10；5:22；參10:16）。但在哥林多有一些人生氣了。傳道服務不得罪人似乎是不可能的。一些人連真理和聖潔也反感；人聽了耶穌的道，也曾對祂動怒（約6:60,61,66）。對於其他人而言，任何對罪惡或錯誤的警告都會冒犯他們。但是對於真正的基督徒來說，福音使者決不會表現出驕傲、不敬、狂妄、不良習性或行為、無禮或粗俗而冒犯他們。
只要有可能，福音的執事就要“與眾人和睦”（羅12:18）。但耶穌和保羅無論走到哪裡都會引起敵意。耶穌來“不是叫地上太平，乃是叫地上動刀兵”（太10:34），並警告說“人的仇敵，就是自己家裡的人”（36節）。沒有哪一個基督徒比基督遭遇更多的敵人。祂的門徒則被指責為“攪亂天下的”（徒17:6）。在各世代中，上帝的僕人總會無可避免地遭遇衝突。基督徒的美德和上帝公義的標準常常妨礙人的罪中之樂。而惡人則喜歡控告那些警告他們惡行的人。沒有一個傳道人可以指望忠實地傳講真理而不得罪那些因真理而暴露出生活中罪惡的人。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《傳道良助》第60頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–10節）**。《使徒行述》第369頁；《傳道良助》第60頁。
3.en:
**Offence.** Literally, “an occasion for stumbling.” Paul aspires so to conduct his ministry (cf. v. 1) as to give men no excuse, on his account, for rejecting the grace of God. It is therefore imperative that his own life shall be in complete harmony with the gospel he preaches. In vs. 3–10 Paul lists evidences that his life is in harmony with his message. He has given the Corinthians no reason to blame him as a minister.
**Ministry.** Textual evidence may be cited (cf. p. 10) for reading “our ministry.” Paul here speaks of his own service as an ambassador for Christ. He had suffered, labored, studied, and ministered the Word so as to avoid giving any occasion for offense (1 Cor. 8:13; 10:32, 33; Phil. 2:15; 1 Thess. 2:10; 5:22; cf. 10:16). Nevertheless, there were a number in Corinth who had taken offense. It would perhaps be impossible to preach and to act so that none would be offended. To some, even truth and holiness give offense; men who listened to Jesus were offended at Him (John 6:60, 61, 66). To others, any warning against sin or error gives offense. But to true Christians, the gospel ambassador will give no offense by manifestations of pride, irreverence, aloofness, questionable habits or practices, discourtesy, or vulgarity.
As far as possible, the gospel minister should “live peaceably with all men” (Rom. 12:18), yet both Jesus and Paul stirred up enmity wherever they went. Jesus “came not to send peace, but a sword” (Matt. 10:34), and warned that a “man’s foes shall be they of his own household” (v. 36). No Christian has ever encountered more enemies than Christ, and His disciples were charged with having “turned the world upside down” (Acts 17:6). In every age God’s servants have found conflict unavoidable. Christian virtue and God’s standard of righteousness often stand in the way of men’s sinful pleasures, and wicked men are prone to charge as disturbers those who sound a warning against their evil ways. No minister can hope to preach the truth faithfully without offending men whose lives are thereby shown to be wrong.

4.zh:
反倒在各樣的事上表明自己是神的用人，就如在許多的忍耐、患難、窮乏、困苦、

**表明自己。**保羅再次提出他在這封書信中經常談起的薦信問題（林後3:1-3；4:2；5:12；10:12,13,17,18）。他曾清楚地區分真薦信與假薦信。他在林後6:3-10中介紹了自己的職分，指出他個人的行為和他為基督所受的辛勞和苦難。真薦信是由行為，而不是由言語構成的。
**忍耐。**hupomone，“堅定”，“堅貞”，“容忍”，“耐心等待”（參路8:15；21:19）。
**患難。**thlipsis，“壓迫”，“窮困”，“艱難”，直譯是“擠壓”，“壓力”（參1:4,8；2:4；4:17等）。
**窮乏。**anagkai，“災難”，直譯是“緊張的壓力”。
**困苦。**stenochōriai，“不幸的災難”，“極端痛苦”，直譯是“狹隘的空間”。該詞表達極端需要的狀態，遭到包圍，無路可走。保羅在這裡指極端困難，似乎無法解脫的情況，如以色列民面對紅海時（出14:1-12）。
4.en:
**Approving ourselves.** Paul again takes up the problem of commendation, which he refers to frequently in this epistle (chs. 3:1–3; 4:2; 5:12; 10:12, 13, 17, 18). He has sought to make a clear distinction between the right type of commendation and that which is false. In ch. 6:3–10 he commends his own ministry, pointing to his personal conduct and to his life of labor and suffering for Christ. True commendation consists of deeds, not words.
**Patience.** Gr. hupomonē, “steadfastness,” “constancy,” “endurance,” “patient waiting” (cf. Luke 8:15; 21:19).
**Afflictions.** Gr. thlipsis, “oppression,” “distresses,” “straits,” literally, “pressings together,” “pressures” (cf. chs. 1:4, 8; 2:4; 4:17; etc.).
**Necessities.** Gr. anagkai, “calamities,” literally, “tight pressings.”
**Distresses.** Gr. stenochōriai, “dire calamities,” “extreme afflictions,” literally, “narrow spaces.” This word depicts a state of extreme and pressing need, in which one is hemmed in, as it were, with no room left in which to move. Paul here refers to extremely difficult and seemingly impossible situations such as the Israelites faced at the Red Sea (Ex. 14:1–12).

5.zh:
鞭打、監禁、擾亂、勤勞、警醒、不食、

**鞭打。**或“擊打”。見太10:17；林後11:24,25註釋。
**擾亂。**akatastasiai，“混亂”，“騷亂”，“動亂”。參路21:9。保羅和他的同伴常常是這些“擾亂”的對象，被控是騷亂的製造者。使徒在這種情況下是非常危險的。他們在彼西底的安提阿（徒13:50），在路司得（徒14:8-19），帖撒羅尼迦（徒17:5），哥林多（徒18:12），以弗所（徒19:23-41）和耶路撒冷（徒21:28-31；23:7-10）都有這樣的遭遇。
**勤勞。**可能指保羅辛勞地製作帳篷和從事傳道工作（林前3:8；4:12；15:58；帖前2:9；帖後3:8）。
**警醒。**或“不眠”（徒16:24,25；20:7,31）。
**不食。**可能既指主動的節食（徒9:9；徒13:2；徒14:23），也指窮困或其他因素造成的飢餓（林後11:9,27；腓4:10-12）。
5.en:
**Stripes.** Or, “blows,” “beatings.” See on Matt. 10:17; 2 Cor. 11:24, 25.
**Tumults.** Gr. akatastasiai, “disorders,” “disturbances,” “confusion.” The same word is translated “commotions” in Luke 21:9. Paul and his companions were frequently the objects of these “tumults,” and were usually accused of starting them. Under such circumstances the apostles were in extreme danger. Such experiences befell them at Antioch in Pisidia (Acts 13:50), at Lystra (ch. 14:8–19), at Thessalonica (ch. 17:5), at Corinth (ch. 18:12), at Ephesus (ch. 19:23–41), and at Jerusalem (chs. 21:28–31; 23:7–10).
**Labours.** Probably a reference to Paul’s toil at tentmaking and the labors attending upon his ministry (1 Cor. 3:8; 4:12; 15:58; 1 Thess. 2:9; 2 Thess. 3:8).
**Watchings.** Or, “sleeplessness” (Acts 16:24, 25; 20:7, 31).
**Fastings.** Probably including both voluntary abstinence from food (Acts 9:9; Acts 13:2; Acts 14:23) and hunger resulting from poverty or other circumstances (2 Cor. 11:9, 27; Phil. 4:10–12).

6.zh:
廉潔、知識、恆忍、恩慈、聖靈的感化、無偽的愛心、

**廉潔。**保羅已列舉了他傳道工作中所遇到的許多困難（參林後4:8-11；11:23-27）。現在他開始講述積極的道德和屬靈品質，作為基督教傳道士生活的特徵，並證實他作為基督使者的使命。這些積極的品質使他能堅強地忍受所遭遇的侮辱，逼迫和貧困。靠著上帝的恩典，這些經歷使他的品格更加成熟，高尚和純潔。保羅在這裡無疑指純潔的動機和行為，身體和心靈的清潔。純潔是進行無可指責服務的首要條件（參林後11:2；帖前2:10；彼前3:2；約壹3:3；見太5:8註釋）。
**知識。**指天國的知識，包括聖經所啟示的全部神聖真理。真宗教決不依靠無知發展。每一個基督徒所肩負最嚴肅的責任之一，就是清楚而全面地瞭解聖經所展示的福音。見路1:77；11:52；林前1:5註釋。
**恆忍。**makrothumia，“忍耐”，“恆心”，“堅忍”，“忍受”。恆忍的品質使傳道人能長期忍受有時在未來的信徒和反對真理的人身上所遇到的錯誤，失敗和愚昧。
**恩慈。**chrēstotēs，“美德”，“正直”，“良善”（見羅3:12註釋）。知識本身會引起人驕傲和自負（林前8:1-3）。許多自稱明白真理的基督徒，只會劇烈地爭論，卻不能為信仰做辯護。他們無法平心靜氣和與觀點不同的人討論真理。基督的傳道人尤其需要防止這種非基督化的傾向。特別是在遭到迫害，汙衊，或信徒的貶低時，一定要百倍警惕，保守自己的心。
**聖靈的。**聖靈是培養這一切美德的積極動力（加5:22,23）。離開了聖靈，也會在某些程度上，至少在表面上擁有這些美德，但決不完全。
**愛心。**agape（見太5:43,44註釋）。福音傳道士最偉大的品質就是這個最重要和聯絡全德的聖靈果子（見林前13註釋）。關於“愛人不可虛假”，見羅12:9註釋。沒有這種品質，基督的使者就會變得剛硬，冷淡，自滿和挑剔。沒有愛就沒有純潔和能力。
6.en:
**Pureness.** Thus far Paul has listed the difficulties attendant upon his ministry (cf. chs. 4:8–11; 11:23–27). Now he sets forth those positive moral and spiritual qualities that must characterize the life of the Christian minister in particular and validate his commission as an ambassador for Christ. These positive traits enable him to endure with fortitude the insults, persecution, and privation that circumstances impose upon him. By God’s grace these experiences mature, ennoble, and refine his character. Here Paul no doubt refers to both pure motives and pure conduct, to chastity of both mind and body. Purity is a primary requisite of a blameless ministry (cf. 2 Cor. 11:2; 1 Thess. 2:10; 1 Peter 3:2; 1 John 3:3; see on Matt. 5:8).
**Knowledge.** That is, of the kingdom of heaven, and including the entire field of divine truth revealed in the Bible. True religion does not thrive on a diet of ignorance. One of the most solemn duties incumbent upon every Christian is to gain a clear and comprehensive insight into the gospel as set forth in the Book of God. See on Luke 1:77; 11:52; 1 Cor. 1:5.
**Longsuffering.** Gr. makrothumia, “patience,” “perseverance,” “steadfastness,” “endurance.” The quality of long-suffering enables the minister to bear long with the faults, failings, and dullness sometimes encountered in prospective converts, and often in those who oppose the truth.
**Kindness.** Gr. chrēstotēs, “moral goodness,” “integrity,” “kindness” (see on Rom. 3:12). Knowledge by itself leads to pride and intolerance (1 Cor. 8:1–3). Many professed Christians who claim to know the truth find it impossible to defend the faith except by passionate arguments. They cannot speak for the truth without becoming angry with those who disagree. The Christian minister, particularly, needs to guard against this unchristian tendency. Especially in the midst of persecution, under false accusation, or when his converts do not seem to appreciate him as they should, he must watch his own spirit with close vigilance.
**By the Holy Ghost.** The Holy Spirit is the active agency in cultivating all these virtues (Gal. 5:22, 23). It is possible to possess these traits in some degree, superficially at least, apart from the Holy Spirit, but never in their fullness.
**Love.** Gr. agapē (see on Matt. 5:43, 44). The crowning characteristic of the gospel minister is this chief and all-pervading fruit of the Spirit (see on 1 Cor. 13). For comment on “love unfeigned” see on Rom. 12:9. Without this quality the ambassador of Christ becomes hard, cold, self-complacent, and censorious. Purity and power are impossible without love.

7.zh:
真實的道理、神的大能；仁義的兵器在左在右；

**真實的道理。**見約1:14；8:32註釋。對傳道人最嚴格的要求就是不增不減地如實宣傳真理。真誠的最終檢驗，就是在生活和言行上表現真理。上帝是真理（詩31:5；耶10:10）。真理是永恆的，正如上帝是永恆的（詩100:5；146:6）。基督道成肉身是真理的完美啟示（約14:6）。要殷勤追求真理。以真理為重生（雅1:18）和成聖（約17:17）的手段和和日常行為的楷模（約叄3,4）。只把真理當作理智的觀念來接受，就沒有什麼價值（約3:21；約壹1:6）。因為全心全意地接受真理，意味著完全順從上帝所啟示的全部旨意。持有和實行真理乃是真基督徒的標誌（見太7:21-27註釋）。
**大能。**dunamis，“力量”，“能力”，“遺傳的力量”。真理和大能是相輔相成的。上帝的真理如果沒有上帝的能力就沒有實際的價值。只是大能卻沒有真理，就會導致壓迫。真理和大能都來自上帝，都必須受愛的控制（見林後5:14註釋）。宗教信仰唯一有效的權威就是本著上帝之道闡述真理，藉著上帝的大能應用在生活中，並處在上帝之愛的控制之下。
**仁義的兵器。**保羅用戰爭的比喻來描寫基督徒的命運（弗6:11-17）。披帶基督的全副軍裝就是披帶祂的義。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《早期著作》第273頁；《今日的生活》第94頁；《先知與君王》第111，725頁；《證言》卷二第446頁。
7.en:
**Truth.** See on John 1:14; 8:32. No more exacting requirement is made of the minister than the proclamation of truth without diminishing from, or adding to, it. To be the embodiment of truth, in life, in word, in deed, constitutes the ultimate test of genuineness. God is truth (Ps. 31:5; Jer. 10:10), and truth is eternal as God is eternal (Ps. 100:5; 146:6). Christ incarnate was the full and perfect revelation of truth (John 14:6). Truth must be sought for diligently and made a means of regeneration (James 1:18) and sanctification (John 17:17), and a pattern for daily conduct (3 John 3, 4). Truth is of little value when entertained as an intellectual concept only (John 3:21; 1 John 1:6), for the wholehearted acceptance of truth means complete obedience to all of God’s revealed will. The possession and practice of truth is the mark of a true Christian (see on Matt. 7:21–27).
**Power.** Gr. dunamis, “strength,” “ability,” “inherent power.” Truth and power are complementary. The truth of God without the power of God has no practical value. Power alone, without truth, leads to oppression. Truth and power both come from God, and both must be under the control of love (see on ch. 5:14). The only valid authority for religious belief is truth as set forth in the Word of God, applied to the life by the power of God, and held under the control of His love.
**Armour of righteousness.** Paul uses the figure of warfare to describe the lot of the Christian (Eph. 6:11–17). To be clothed with the panoply of Christ’s armor is to be clothed with His righteousness.

8.zh:
榮耀、羞辱，惡名、美名；似乎是誘惑人的，卻是誠實的；

8-10節是一系列的對比（參林後4:8-10）。即使不是全部，其大部分也是保羅的親身經歷，同哥林多教會最近的危機有關。保羅對這些時常變化的環境所作出的反應，證明他勝任福音執事的工作。他保持忍耐和勇敢，因此總是有良好的結果。
他既受人尊重（加4:14），也受人侮辱和詆譭（林前4:11-13）。但他總是以基督的精神來應付，並順從祂的命令（太5:38-42；路6:22；10:16；加1:10）。哥林多的假使徒曾誹謗他。還有人藐視保羅的講道和他的職分，說他是騙子（林後2:17；4:2；見11:22）。對於保羅而言，這只是為他提供了與基督的苦難有份的機會（腓3:10；參太5:11；彼前4:14）。保羅和他的同工沒有藉著表現出怨恨和自高而冒犯人。
8.en:
**Honour and dishonour.** Verses 8–10 set forth a series of paired contrasts (cf. ch. 4:8–10). Most, if not all, of these experiences had come to Paul in connection with the recent crisis in the Corinthian church. His reaction to these changing circumstances commend him as a minister of the gospel. He remained patient and courageous, and thus good always resulted.
On the one hand, he had been honored by men Gal. 4:14), and on the other, dishonored and discredited (1 Cor. 4:11–13). But he always replied in the spirit of Christ and in harmony with His commands (Matt. 5:38–42; Luke 6:22; 10:16; Gal. 1:10). The false apostles at Corinth had spoken evil of him. There were still some who held Paul’s preaching and ministry in contempt and spoke of him as an impostor (2 Cor. 2:17; 4:2; see on ch. 11:22). For Paul, this only provided an opportunity for fellowship with Christ in His sufferings (Phil. 3:10; cf. Matt. 5:11; 1 Peter 4:14). Paul and his companions gave no offense, either by showing resentment or by self-exaltation.

9.zh:
似乎不為人所知，卻是人所共知的；似乎要死，卻是活著的；似乎受責罰，卻是不至喪命的；

**似乎不為人所知。**即模糊不清。保羅可能指自己沒有薦信（林後3:2）。相比之下，猶太派人士（見林後11:22註釋）卻自以為了不起。同樣，世人也不認識我們的主（約1:10）。連祂的兄弟也沒有認出他。祂的同鄉只以祂為“木匠的兒子”（太13:55）。屬靈的盲目使當時的人沒有認出耶穌的真實身份。各時代的基督徒也是這樣（約16:33；約壹3:1,13）。世人崇尚基於出身、財富、智慧和地位的偉大和能力，卻不重視基於聖潔和謙卑的偉大。基督徒要有受人曲解，誤會，嘲笑和迫害的思想準備，因為世人不理解他們的生活、經驗、原則、抱負和昐望（林前2:14）。
**人所共知的。**就是得到誠心的人所承認和尊重。
**似乎要死。**在世人看來，保羅也許快要死了。但在屬靈的眼光看來，他卻擁有永生（約壹5:11,12）。他仇敵昏花的眼光看他的苦難是上帝不悅和懲罰的證據。但保羅以屬靈的眼光享受與基督同受苦難（腓3:10），並看到上帝對他大愛的憑據（林前11:32；來12:6；啟3:19）。
**受責罰。**或“懲罰。”見林後4:9註釋。
9.en:
**As unknown.** That is, obscure. Possibly Paul refers to his lack of credentials (ch. 3:2). In contrast, the Judaizers (see on ch. 11:22) considered themselves men of distinction. Likewise, the world knew not our Lord (John 1:10). Even His brothers failed to recognize Him. His fellow townsmen knew Him only as “the carpenter’s son” (Matt. 13:55). Spiritual blindness hid the real Jesus from the eyes of His generation. So it is with Christians in every age (John 16:33; 1 John 3:1, 13). The world acclaims greatness and power based on ancestry, wealth, intellectual greatness, and position, but greatness based on holiness and humility receives little recognition. Christians must be prepared for misrepresentation, misunderstanding, scorn, and persecution, because their life, experience, principles, ambitions, and hopes are meaningless to the natural man (1 Cor. 2:14).
**Well known.** That is, recognized and respected by men of sincerity.
**As dying.** To the secular eye Paul was perhaps at the point of death, but to the spiritual eye he had possession of eternal life (1 John 5:11, 12). His sufferings appeared to the dim vision of his opponents as evidence of God’s displeasure and punishment, but with spiritual insight, Paul enjoyed fellowship with Christ in His sufferings (Phil. 3:10), and discerned evidences of God’s great love for him 1 Cor. 11:32; Heb. 12:6; Rev. 3:19).
**Chastened.** Or, “chastised.” See on ch. 4:9.

10.zh:
似乎憂愁，卻是常常快樂的；似乎貧窮，卻是叫許多人富足的；似乎一無所有，卻是樣樣都有的。

**似乎憂愁。**保羅似乎只有憂愁的理由。但他認為憂愁和喜樂並不是互相排斥的，因為他知道如何在患難中喜樂。他即使有理由憂愁，仍因上帝天意的引導而高興。這種態度反應了基督的精神（羅12:12；腓4:4,11；來2:10-18）。基督教不僅在考驗時支持人，而且賜人歡樂勝利的精神，使人心中充滿信心和盼望。（賽61:3）。
保羅勝利的精神或許在《腓立比書》中得到了最好的詮釋。那捲書的中心詞就是“喜樂”。但保羅在寫《腓立比書》時，是身陷監獄，遭人拋棄，孤獨一人，又面臨立即處死的危險。真正的基督徒總能在良好的心態，純潔高尚的意念，上帝的悅納和同胞的得救中保持喜樂（來12:2）。無論他蒙召要忍受什麼，他都已學會了滿足（腓4:11）。知足常樂的人生是基督徒與生俱來、不可剝奪的權利。得救脫離罪惡的權勢和撒但的手，“靠著愛我們的主……得勝有餘”（羅8:37），被“拯救到底”（來7:25）──這一切足以成為喜樂幸福人生的理由。
**貧窮。**指“虛心”（見太5:3註釋）。在世人看來，保羅確實是貧窮的。但在屬靈的眼光看來，他是富足的。他喪失了一切（林前4:11；腓3:7,8；4:12）。物質上的貧窮，常常是基督徒的選擇和命運。耶路撒冷的信徒自願交出自己地上的財產（徒2:44,45；3:6；5:1-3）。生活不能憑外表來評價。上帝的國不是眼所能見的。人真正的富足不在於持有，而在於施給（見箴11:24註釋）。他們因基督測不透的豐富而富足（賽55:1,2；徒20:35；林後8:9；弗3:8；提前6:18）。他們因把天國的福分傳授與別人而富足（賽58:6-14）。
**樣樣都有。**信徒在基督裡繼承和擁有萬有（太5:5；16:25；19:29；可10:28-30；羅8:17；林前3:21-23；啟3:21）。福音使人富足，給人帶來崇高的思想，宗旨，盼望、上帝的交往，純潔的心靈，和諧的身心，和享受上帝所造萬有的能力。見太6:24-34註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》第68頁；《救贖的故事》第313頁。
10.en:
**As sorrowful.** Paul seems to have cause for nothing but melancholy. For him, however, sorrow and joy are not mutually exclusive alternatives, for he knows how to be glad in the midst of tribulation. He rejoices in God’s providential leading, even when he has cause for sorrow. This attitude reflects the mind of Christ (Rom. 12:12; Phil. 4:4, 11; Heb. 2:10–18). Christianity not only sustains the soul in the hour of trial but imparts the spirit of joyful triumph and fills the mind with assurance and hope. (Isa. 61:3).
Paul’s spirit of triumph is perhaps best set forth in the book of Philippians, whose key word is “rejoice.” Yet when he wrote that book Paul was in prison, deserted, alone, and in danger of immediate execution. The true Christian can always rejoice in a good conscience, in a pure and noble mind, in divine favor, and in the salvation of his fellow men (Heb. 12:2). He has learned to be content, whatever he may be called upon to endure (Phil. 4:11). A life of contentment and joy is the Christian’s inalienable birthright. To be delivered from the power of sin and the hands of Satan, to be “more than conquerors through him that loved us” (Rom. 8:37), to be saved “to the uttermost” (Heb. 7:25)—all this is cause enough for a life of joy and happiness.
**Poor.** That is, “poor in spirit” (see on Matt. 5:3). To the secular eye, Paul was poor indeed, but to the spiritual eye he was rich. He had suffered the loss of all things (1 Cor. 4:11; Phil. 3:7, 8; 4:12). It has generally been the choice and lot of Christians to remain poor in material things. Believers at Jerusalem willingly surrendered their earthly wealth (Acts 2:44, 45; 3:6; 5:1–3). Life cannot be estimated by appearances. As far as God’s kingdom is concerned, things are not what they seem. Men become truly rich, not by keeping, but by giving (see on Prov. 11:24). They are made rich with the unsearchable riches of Christ (Isa. 55:1, 2; Acts 20:35; 2 Cor. 8:9; Eph. 3:8; 1 Tim. 6:18). They become rich by conferring Heaven’s blessings on others (Isa. 58:6–14).
**Possessing all things.** In Christ the believer becomes heir and possessor of all things (Matt. 5:5; 16:25; 19:29; Mark 10:28–30; Rom. 8:17; 1 Cor. 3:21–23; Rev. 3:21). The gospel enriches men with noble thoughts, high purposes, elevating hopes, divine fellowship, purity of heart, harmony of being, the ability to enjoy all that God has made. See on Matt. 6:24–34.

11.zh:
哥林多人哪，我們向你們，口是張開的，心是寬宏的。

**哥林多人哪。**在兩封書信裡，保羅只有在這裡稱他們為“哥林多人”。他呼籲他們回應他的愛，像他待他們那樣待他。
**我們向你們，口是張開的。**保羅對哥林多信徒是直言無隱的，該說什麼，就說什麼。這是他們瞭解的。
**心是寬宏的。**保羅在與他們相處，勸勉和責備他們，面對他們的問題和批評時，總是暢所欲言的。在任何時候，即使在此時，保羅也沒有向他們隱瞞他內心深處的想法和感受。他一直說話坦率，毫無保留（參太12:34；羅10:10）。他的心總是充滿對他們的愛。即邊現在，他仍想念他們，渴望他們愛的回應。他以寬宏的心懷、基督的精神面對他們的一切批評。
11.en:
**Ye Corinthians.** Here alone in his two epistles does Paul address the Corinthians by name. He appeals to them to reciprocate his love, to deal with him as he has dealt with them.
**Our mouth is open.** Paul was keeping nothing back from the Corinthians. He would say what there was to say, that they might know the facts.
**Our heart.** In all his dealings with them, in his exhortations and rebukes, in the face of their problems and criticism, Paul has been speaking out of the abundance of his heart. At no time, even to the present moment, has he avoided expressing his inmost thoughts and feelings to them. All along he has spoken openly and without reserve; he has kept nothing back (cf. Matt. 12:34; Rom. 10:10). His heart has always been full of love for them, and even now he yearns for them and for their loving response. He has met all their criticisms in the spirit of Christ, with largeness of heart.

12.zh:
你們狹窄，原不在乎我們，是在乎自己的心腸狹窄。

**狹窄。**或“受限制”，“限於狹小地帶”，“壓縮”。保羅對他們的愛決不狹隘。缺乏體諒的決不是他。哥林多信徒在他的心中的位置並不小。但是顯然有些哥林多信徒在感情上對他很狹隘。
**心腸。**指心，肺，肝，上腸道等。古人認為身體的這個部位是情感所在處（腓1:8；2:1）。在保羅和哥林多信徒人的關係中，不論存在什麼不愉快的不理想的事，保羅和他同伴們的心中都不存在狹隘的觀念。
12.en:
**Straitened.** Or, “restricted,” “confined in a narrow place,” “compressed.” Paul’s love for them is in no way contracted. If there had been a lack of sympathetic understanding, it was not on his part. The Corinthians do not have a narrow place in his heart, but apparently some of them had scanty room for him in their affections.
**Bowels.** That is, the heart, lungs, liver, upper intestines, etc. This region of the body was considered by the ancients to be the seat of the affections (Phil. 1:8; 2:1). Whatever there may have been that was unpleasant and undesirable in the relations between Paul and the Corinthians, it did not exist in the hearts of Paul and his companions.

13.zh:
你們也要照樣用寬宏的心報答我。我這話正像對自己的孩子說的。

保羅把哥林多信徒看作他屬靈的孩子（林前4:14,15）。作為他們屬靈的父親，他向他們傾注了充足的父愛。作為回報，他希望得到他們的愛。難道他們不願擴大心胸為他留出一席之地嗎？若是這樣，他們之間的一切問題都解決了；所有的意見也都消除了（參加4:12；帖前2:11）。
13.en: **For a recompence.** Paul considers the Corinthian believers his spiritual children (1 Cor. 4:14, 15), and as their spiritual father he has poured upon them a full measure of paternal love. In return, he longs for their love. Will they not enlarge their hearts enough to make room for him? To do so will be to solve all the problems and to remove all the ill feelings between them (cf. Gal. 4:12; 1 Thess. 2:11).

18.zh:
我要作你們的父；你們要作我的兒女。這是全能的主說的。

**父。**18節也是將幾處《舊約》經文結合而成（撒下7:8,14；賽43:6；耶31:19）。參林後6:18；見太6:9註釋。
**兒女。**成為上帝的兒女，是上帝賜給從聖靈所生之人的最高特權（見約1:12-13；3:3,5；約壹3:1,2註釋）。上帝在這裡應許作祂兒女的父親，和他們的供應者，保護者，安慰者，引導者和拯救者。雖然人是被接納為上帝兒女的，但這個過程也被稱為新生（約1:12,13；3:3,5）。
信徒相信基督的結果，就是上帝之靈超自然的運作，創造了新的屬靈生命，使人成為上帝的兒女。這種父子關係與人間的父子關係一樣真實和重要。在耶穌作上帝兒子的生活中，我們看到了這種關係的完美典範。我們有權利成為天父的兒女（見路2:49；約1:14；4:34；8:29註釋）。這個關係的關鍵是愛，其結果是順從信靠。父親的重要品質是愛的權威。兒女的重要品質是信靠和順服。沒有這些品質，就無法體驗真正的父子關係（羅8:9,10；林後7:1；約壹1:1-7）。上帝希望這些品質實現在每一個基督徒的生活中。
**全能的。**這個上帝的稱呼經常出現在《啟示錄》中（啟1:8等），強調了林後6:17,18應許的確實和偉大。參該詞希伯來語的對應詞（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷一171頁）。7:1結束了保羅在6：14節所開始的思路（見該節註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《健康勉言》第590頁；《今日的生活》第83，86，98頁；《證言》卷二第593頁；《證言》卷四第624，653頁；《證言》卷五第348，368頁；《證言》卷六第190頁；《證言》卷七第226頁；《證言》卷八第177頁；《證言》卷九第188，287頁。
18.en:
**A Father.** Verse 18 consists of another mosaic of ideas gathered from different passages of the OT (2 Sam. 7:8, 14; Isa. 43:6; Jer. 31:9). Compare 2 Cor. 6:18; see on Matt. 6:9.
**Sons and daughters.** The privilege of becoming the adopted sons and daughters of God is the supreme privilege He accords those who are born of the Spirit (see on John 1:12–13; 3:3, 5; 1 John 3:1, 2). God here promises to act the part of a father to those who become His children, to be their provider, protector, counselor, guide, and deliverer. Although men become sons of God by adoption, the same process is also spoken of as a new birth (John 1:12, 13; 3:3, 5).
As a result of the believer’s faith in Christ the supernatural operation of the Spirit of God creates new spiritual life, which makes the man a son of God. This Father-son relationship is as real and vital as the human relationship used to illustrate it. In the life of Jesus as the Son of God we have a perfect example of the relationship it is our privilege to bear to our heavenly Father as His sons (see on Luke 2:49; John 1:14; 4:34; 8:29). The key to this relationship is love, and its result is obedient trust. The essential quality of fatherhood is loving authority, as that of sonship is trust and obedience. Without these qualities there can be no true fatherson experience (Rom. 8:9, 10: 2 Cor. 7:1; 1 John 1:1–7). God intends that they shall be a reality in the life of every Christian.
**Almighty.** A divine title also used here and frequently in the book of Revelation (Rev. 1:8; etc.). This title here emphasizes the certainty and the greatness of the promise of 2 Cor. 6:17, 18. Compare the Hebrew equivalent (see Vol. I, p. 171). Chapter 7:1 completes the sequence of thought which Paul began in ch. 6:14 (see comment there).

21.en:
**Made him to be sin.** That is, God treated Him as if He were a sinner, which He was not (see DA 25). The truths stated in v. 21 are among the most profound and significant in all the Bible. This verse sums up the plan of salvation, declaring the absolute sinlessness of Christ, the vicarious nature of His sacrifice, and man’s freedom from sin through Him. See on John 3:16.
**Knew no sin.** How Jesus could come to this world as a human being and “in all points” be “tempted like as we are, yet without sin” (Heb. 4:15) is an unfathomable mystery. He never committed sin, in word, in thought, or in deed. Throughout the entire course of His life He kept Himself from sin in every way. Here on earth He lived a holy, undefiled, and pure life, ever conscious of being in harmony with the Father’s will (John 8:46; 14:30; 15:10; Heb. 7:26; see Additional Note on John 1; see on Luke 2:52). Christ, the Sinless One, took sinful humanity to His warm heart of love and experienced the temptations that beset us without being in the least degree overcome by them. He “identified Himself with sinners” (DA 111). When, on the cross, Jesus came to the hour for which He had entered the world (John 8:20; 12:23, 27; 13:1; 17:1; 18:37), He was “offered to bear the sins of many” (Heb. 9:28) and became the “Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world” (John 1:29).
The guilt of the sins of the world was reckoned to Him as if it were all His own (Isa. 53:3–6; 1 Peter 2:22–24). “He was numbered with the transgressors” (Mark 15:28). Christ became identified with sin; He took it to Himself in a real sense and felt the horror of separation from God.
**The righteousness of God.** See on Rom. 5:19. As our sins were reckoned to Christ, as if they were His, so His rightheouness is reckoned to us as if it were ours.
21.zh:
神使那無罪（無罪：原文是不知罪）的，替我們成為罪，好叫我們在他裡面成為神的義。

**使使那無罪……成為罪。**上帝看待祂如罪人，但祂並不是（見《歷代願望》25頁）。21節中所闡述的真理是聖經中最為深奧最有意義的真理之一。本節歸納了救贖的計劃，宣佈基督絕對無罪，祂作為祭牲的替人受死，以及人藉著祂得以脫離罪惡。見約3:16註釋。
**不知罪。**耶穌怎樣來到這個世界成為人，“凡事受過試探，與我們一樣。只是祂沒有罪”（來4:15），這是深不可測的奧秘。祂在思想和言行上從來沒有犯罪。祂的一生在各方面都遠離罪惡。祂在世界上過聖潔無暇的純潔生活，始終想到與祂父的旨意保持和諧（約8:46；14:30；15:10；來7:26；見《約翰福音》第一章補充註釋；見路2:52註釋）。無罪之主基督以溫暖的愛心取了有罪的人性，經歷了我們所遭遇的試探，卻絲毫沒有被試探所勝。祂“將自己與罪人視同一體（《歷代願望》111頁）。當祂在十字架上，為那一刻來到世界上的時候（約8:20；12:23,27；13:1；17:1；18:37），祂“被獻，擔當了多人的罪孽”（來9:28）成為“上帝的羔羊，除去世人罪孽的”（約1:29）。
世上罪人的罪都歸到了祂身上，好像是祂自己的（賽53:3-6；彼前2:22-24）。“祂被列在罪犯之中”（可15:28）。基督與罪惡視同一體，在真實的意義上承擔罪孽，感受與上帝隔絕的恐懼。
**上帝的義。**見羅5:19註釋。正如我們的罪歸與基督身上，就像是祂的罪，祂的義也歸於我們，就像是我們的義
**懷愛倫註釋**。《安息日學訓言》第89頁；《基督教育之研究》第22頁；《基督教育原理》第272頁；《今日的生活》第11頁；《醫療佈道論》第27頁；《救贖的故事》第225頁；《證言》卷一第482頁；《證言》卷二第212頁；《證言》卷三第372頁；《證言》卷五第229頁；見約1:14懷愛倫註釋。

19.en:
**To wit.** In modern English, “namely,” or “that is to say.”
**God was in Christ.** A clearer rendition of the Greek of the first clause would be, “God was reconciling the world unto Himself in Christ [or “through Christ”].” Men must realize that although it was the Son who died on the cross, He died so as “the Lamb of God” (John 1:29).
**Reconciling the world.** The entrance of sin had set men at enmity with God, and it was the purpose of Christ in coming to this world to win back the affection and loyalty of men toward God.
**Not imputing.** Or, “not reckoning,” “not counting.” The trespasses are there on the record, charged against those who committed them, but divine mercy and justice have found a way to deal with the offenders as though they were not guilty. Sin is a debt (Matt. 6:12) for which the sinner must someday render an account (cf. Matt. 25:19). But God will not impute sin to those who have been reconciled to Him through Christ (Ps. 32:2).
**Trespasses.** See on Matt. 6:14.
**Committed unto us.** Here is further proof of the love of God and of His willingness to forgive. The message of reconciliation has been deposited, as it were, in the minds and hearts of all who accept it for themselves, for distribution to others.
**Word.** See on John 1:1.
19.zh:
這就是神在基督裡，叫世人與自己和好，不將他們的過犯歸到他們身上，並且將這和好的道理託付了我們。

**就是。**“即是”。
**上帝在基督裡。**或“藉著基督”。人必須認識到聖子死在十字架上是作為“上帝的羔羊”（約1:29）。
**叫世人與……和好。**救恩的計劃不是讓上帝與人和好，而是讓世人與祂和好。罪的進入使人與上帝為敵，基督來到這個世界的目的就是要挽回人對上帝的情感和忠誠。
**不將……歸到。**過犯是記錄在案，指控犯罪之人的。但上帝的憐憫和公義已找到一種方法來對待犯罪的人，就像他們是無罪的一樣。罪就是債（太6:12）。罪人總有一天要交帳的（參太25:19）。但是上帝不再把罪歸給那些已經藉著基督與祂和好的人（詩32:2）。
**過犯。**見太6:14註釋。
**將……託付了我們。**這進一步證明了上帝的愛和祂願意赦免。和好的信息彷彿已存在接受的人心中，好分給別人。
**道理。**見約1:1註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第762頁；《教育論》第28頁；《善惡之爭》第417，502頁；《先祖與先知》第64，366頁；《拾級就主》第13，35頁；《證言》卷五第739頁；【 SDA6.1102】。

18.en:
**All things.** That is, all of the “new” things of v. 17 in particular, and thus also the new ministry (chs. 3:6; 4:1) and the new discernment of character (ch. 5:16). God is the source of them all.
**Reconciliation.** Gr. katallagē, “exchange,” “reconciliation,” “restoration to favor.” In Rom. 5:11 the same word is translated “atonement” (see comment there). In the NT it denotes a return to favor with God (see Rom. 5:1, 10; Col. 1:20). The idea of reconciliation to God implies that in the past God and man enjoyed a state of fellowship, that there now exists a state of separation (Rom. 8:7), that God has taken the initiative to terminate this state, and that it is therefore again possible for man to enjoy fellowship with God.
Reconciliation involves no change on God’s part, for God never changes (Mal. 3:6; James 1:17; cf. Heb. 13:8). It is not God who needs to be reconciled to man, but man who needs to be reconciled to God (see 2 Cor. 5:18–20; Eph. 2:16; Col. 1:20–21). There has never been enmity on God’s part. Men sometimes conceive of God as a stern judge, angry with sinners, hard to be placated, unmerciful, ready to condemn. This characterization misrepresents Him and is an affront to Him. Christ did not have to go to the cross in order to appease God, but as a demonstration of His love. God did not demand the death of His Son, but gave Him out of a heart of infinite love (John 3:16; 1 John 4:9; see on Rom. 3:25). On the other hand, God cannot set aside His law and avert the consequences that follow its violation without denying His own character, of which His law is an expression. God has always hated sin. He cannot, in fairness, treat good and evil alike. The atonement does not change the law; it changes the enmity that resulted from its violation. Reconciliation removes the enmity by means of a substitutionary fulfillment of the law’s requirements.
18.zh:
一切都是出於神；他藉著基督使我們與他和好，又將勸人與他和好的職分賜給我們。

**一切。**特指林後17節的“新”事物，因此也是指新的職分（林後3:6；4:1）和新的品格辯識力（林後5:16）。上帝是這一切的源泉。
**和好。**katallage，“交換”，“和解”，“恢復喜愛”。參羅5:11。該詞在《新約》中表示重獲上帝的悅納（見羅5:1,10；西1:20）。與上帝和好的概念暗示上帝和人原來有密切的關係，現在處於分離的狀態（羅8:7）。上帝採取主動，結束了這一狀態，使人重享與祂的親密關係。
和好並不涉及上帝一方的改變，因為上帝是永不改變的（瑪3:6；雅1:17；參來13:8）。不是上帝需要與人和好，而是人需要與上帝和好（見林後5:18-20；弗2:16；西1:20-21）。上帝一方從來就沒有敵意。人有時視上帝為嚴厲的法官，生罪人的氣，不肯和解、沒有憐憫，喜歡懲罰。這樣的表述誤解了並公然侮辱了上帝。基督不是為了平息上帝的怒氣而被迫釘十字架的，卻是為了表顯上帝的愛。上帝並沒有要求祂的兒子死，而是出於無限的愛心賜下了祂（約3:16；約壹4:9；見羅3:25註釋）。另一方面，上帝不會將祂的律法放在一邊，改變違犯律法的結果，從而否定祂的律法所表顯的祂的品性。上帝一向憎恨罪惡。按公平的原則，祂不會對善與惡一視同仁。贖罪並不改變律法。它改變的是違背律法所產生的敵意。和解的工作通過為人履行律法的要求而消除敵意。

10.en:
**For we must.** The conjunction “for” connects this verse with what has gone before. Anticipation of being called upon to stand before God on the great judgment day was one of Paul’s reasons for seeking so earnestly to be found acceptable before God. Faithfully and selflessly he purposed to discharge the trust committed to him as an ambassador for Christ. Those for whom the solemnity of that day has reality will ever be diligent and serious in seeking to make God first and to please Him in their daily lives.
The final judgment is necessary to the vindication of God’s character and justice (Ps. 51:4; Rom. 2:5; 3:26). In the present earthly state the best of men are often most afflicted, while the worst of men may prosper (Ps. 37:35–39; cf. Rev. 6:9–11). The character of God requires that in the end it shall be well with them that do good, and ill with them that do evil. This state of affairs does not now exist, and therefore there must be a day when the wrongs of the present time are made right. It is also necessary in order that Christ may triumph over the prince of darkness and his followers (Isa. 45:23; Rom. 14:10, 11; Phil. 2:10; GC 666–671), and that Christ may take to Himself that which He has purchased with His own blood (Heb. 2:11–13; cf. John 14:1–3).
**Appear.** Gr. phaneroō, “to make manifest,” “to make visible,” “to make known,” “to show openly,” “to make public.” This word occurs nine times in 2 Corinthians. On that great day men will not only put in an appearance at the bar of justice, but will stand revealed as to what manner of persons they are. The secrets of their lives will be made bare (Eccl. 12:14; Rom. 2:16; 1 Cor. 4:5). All will have a fair hearing (cf. Jude 15). No man will be judged in his absence, or by proxy (Rom. 14:12; cf. James 2:12, 13).
**Judgment seat.** Gr. bēma, “a raised platform,” from which a formal Roman trial was conducted. Christ is to be the final judge (Matt. 11:27; John 5:22–27; Acts 17:31; 1 Peter 4:5). He is particularly fitted for this task. He is the world’s Creator and its Redeemer. It is a most awesome thought that our Saviour is to be our judge. He took upon Him the nature of those who will come before His bar of justice (Phil. 2:6–8), those whose destiny He will decide. He suffered every temptation to which they have been subjected (Heb. 2:14–17; 4:15). He stood in man’s place. In Christ divine wisdom is combined with human experience. His understanding and insight are infinite (Heb. 4:13). In Christ the righteousness of God has been united with that of a perfect Man. In His role as “Judge of all,” God the Father is united with Christ (Heb. 12:23, 24), and is seen by John the revelator upon a “great white throne” at the end of the thousand years (Rev. 20:11, 12).
**Receive.** Gr. komizō, “to receive as a reward,” “to care for,” “to carry away.” Good or bad, men’s deeds are recorded in heaven (Eccl. 12:13, 14; cf. Eph. 6:8; Col. 3:25; 1 Tim. 6:19).
**In his body.** That is, in this life (see on v. 6). Obviously, probation is here limited to man’s existence in this present world and terminates with the dissolution of the body (v. 1).
**According to.** A man’s deeds will be compared with the great standard of conduct, the law of God (Eccl. 12:13, 14; Rom. 2:12, 13; James 1:25; 2:10–12). In the final judgment there will be no vague standard of righteousness, and thus no chance to escape a just recompense by a belated appeal to divine mercy (Gal. 6:7; Rev. 22:12).
10.zh:
因為我們眾人必要在基督臺前顯露出來，叫各人按著本身所行的，或善或惡受報。

**因為我們眾人。**“因為”一詞承上啟下。保羅誠懇地追求在上帝面前蒙悅納的原因之一，就是預期在審判的大日要被召站在祂面前。保羅作為基督的使者，決心忠誠無私地履行所交託他的職責。凡認識到審判之日嚴肅性的人，必時常殷勤認真地尋求把上帝放在第一位，在日常生活中討祂喜悅。
最後的審判對於認識上帝的品格和公義是非常必要的（詩51:4；羅2:5；3:26）。在現實的世界中，最好的人往往受苦最多，最壞的人卻興旺發達（詩37:35-39；參啟6:9-11）。上帝的品格要求在末日行善的得到賞賜，作惡的得到報應。這種狀態現在並不存在，所以必有一天，現今的錯誤要得到糾正。基督要戰勝黑暗之君及其隨從者（賽45:23；羅14:10,11；腓2:10；《善惡之爭》666-671頁），接納祂自己的血所買來的人（來2:11-13；參約14:1-3），也必須這麼做。
**臺。**bēma，“高臺”，是羅馬正式舉行審判的地方。基督將成為終審法官（太11:27；約5:22-27；徒17:31；彼前4:5）。祂特別適合擔任這個職務。祂是世界的創造主和救贖主。一想到我們的救主將成為我們的法官，我不禁肅然起敬。祂曾取了那些將要到祂臺前受審之人的本性。他們的命運將由祂來決定。祂凡事受過試探，與他們一樣（來2:14-17；4:15）。祂站在人的位置上。在基督裡上帝的智慧與人的經驗結合在一起。祂有無限的理解力與觀察力（來4:13）。在基督身上，上帝的公義與完美人性合而為一。在“審判眾人”的工作中，父上帝與基督一同進行（來12:23,24）。蒙啟示的約翰曾看見一千年結束時，上帝在“白色的大寶座”上（啟20:11,12）。
**顯露。**phaneroo，“顯示”，“表露”，“宣揚”，“公佈”，“展示”。該詞在《哥林多後書》中出現九次。在那大日，人不僅來到審判臺前，而且顯露出他們的本來面目。他們生活中的秘密將公開（傳12:14；羅2:16；林前4:5）。所有的人都將得到公正的審判（參猶15）。沒有人會在缺席或代理的情況下受審（羅14:12；參雅2:12,13）。
**按著。**人的行為要與那行為的偉大標準、上帝的律法進行對照（傳12:13,14；羅2:12,13；雅1:25；2:10-12）。在最後的審判中，公義的標準不是模糊的。再呼籲上帝憐憫就太晚了。人沒有機會躲避公義的報應（加6:7；啟22:12）。
**本身所行的。**即今生的行為（見第6節）。寬容時期顯然只限於人在今生生存之時，隨著人的死亡而結束（第1節）。
**受報。**komizo，“接受”，“關心”，“帶走”。人的行為不論善惡都記錄在天上（傳12:13,14；參弗6:8；西3:25；提前6:19）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第716頁；《論節制》第143頁；《證言》卷一第123頁；《證言》卷二第312頁；《證言》卷四第84，384頁；《證言》卷五第34，483，510頁；《證言》卷六第89頁；《證言》卷七第218頁。

17.en:
**In Christ.** Paul’s favorite definition of what it is to be a Christian. When he became a Christian he was baptized “into Jesus Christ” (Rom. 6:3), and the new life he lives henceforth is centered in Christ (John 15:3–7). He is joined to Christ and wholly subject to His life, power, influence, and word. Paul’s whole life moves in a new, spiritual sphere. Nothing is exempted.
Only “in Christ” can a sinner find acceptance with God (Phil. 3:9) and sustenance for living the new life (John 15:4, 5; Gal 2:20). The joys and sorrows, triumphs and sufferings, of life are all “in Christ” (Rom. 14:17; Phil. 3:9, 10). Even death is robbed of its sting, for those who “die in the Lord” are blessed (Rev. 14:13). Christianity elevates every human experience and obligation into a new relationship, designated by the term “in Christ.”
**Creature.** Gr. ktisis, “creation,” “thing created,” “creature.” For a man to be constrained by the love of Christ to live no longer unto self but unto God, to judge men no longer by appearance but by the spirit, to know Christ according to the spirit and not according to the flesh, he must be created a new being. To transform a lost sinner into a “new creature” requires the same creative energy that originally brought forth life (John 3:3, 5; Rom. 6:5, 6; Eph. 2:10; Col. 3:9, 10). It is a supernatural operation, altogether foreign to normal human experience.
This new nature is not the product of moral virtue presumed by some to be inherent in man, and requiring only growth and expression. There are thousands of so-called moral men who make no profession of being Christians, and who are not “new” creatures. The new nature is not merely the product of a desire, or even of a resolution, to do right (Rom. 7:15–18), of mental assent to certain doctrines, of an exchange of one set of opinions or feelings for another, or even of sorrow from sin. It is the result of the presence of a supernatural element introduced into a man, which results in his dying to sin and being born again. Thus are we created anew in the likeness of Christ, adopted as sons and daughters of God, and set on a new path (see Eze. 36:26, 27; John 1:12, 13; 3:3–7; 5:24; Eph. 1:19; 2:1, 10; 4:24; Titus 3:5; James 1:18). Thus we are made partakers of the divine nature and are granted possession of eternal life (2 Peter 1:4; 1 John 5:11, 12). The new believer is not born a full-grown, mature Christian; he first has the spiritual inexperience and immaturity of infancy. But as a son of God he does have the privilege and opportunity to grow up into the full stature of Christ (see on Matt. 5:48; Eph. 4:14–16; 2 Peter 3:18).
**Become new.** See on Rom. 6:4–6. Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the omission of the words “all things,” the last clause of v. 17 thus reading “they are become new.”
17.zh:
若有人在基督裡，他就是新造的人，舊事已過，都變成新的了。

**在基督裡。**這是保羅最喜歡的基督徒定義。他成為基督徒時，就受洗“歸入耶穌基督”（羅6:3），此後，他的新生活就以基督為中心（約15:3-7）。他與基督聯合，完全服從祂的生命，能力，影響和話語。保羅的整個生活都在新的屬靈氣氛中進行，沒有例外。
罪人只有“在基督裡”才能蒙上帝悅納（腓3:9）並維持新生命（約15:4,5；加2:20）。生活中的喜樂與哀傷、勝利與患難都是“在基督裡”的（羅14:17；腓3:9,10）。連死亡的毒鉤也被奪走了，因為“在主裡面而死的人”是有福的（啟14:13）。基督教將人的一切經驗和責任都提高到了一種新的關係，就是“在基督裡”。
**新造的人。**ktisis，“創造，”“受造之物”。當一個人被基督的愛所激勵，不再為自己而是為上帝而活，看人不再憑外貌，而是憑內心，認識基督是根據心靈而不是根據肉體時，他就是一個新造的人。把淪喪的罪人變成一個“新造的人”，同樣需要最初帶來生命的創造之能（約3:3,5；羅6:5,6；弗2:10；西3:9,10）。這是超自然的工作，與人普通的經驗截然不同。
這種新的本性不像一些人所想象的，是人遺傳美德的產物，只需要發展和表現出來就行了。成千上萬所謂有道德的人，並不承認自己是基督徒。他們不是“新”造的人。新的品性不只是出於行義的願望或決心，在理智上贊同某些教條，把某一套觀點或情感換成另一套，甚至出於由罪而生的哀傷。它是超自然能力進入人心的結果，使人向罪死，獲得重生。於是我們就成為像基督的新造之人，被接納為上帝的兒女，走上新的道路（見結36:26,27；約1:12,13；3:3-7；5:24；弗1:19；2:1,10；4:24；多3:5；雅1:18）。我們就這樣與上帝的性情有份，獲得永生（彼後1:14；約壹5:11,12）。新信徒一開始並不是發育成熟的基督徒。他起先在屬靈上是缺乏經驗而不成熟的。但他作為上帝的兒女，有權利和機會長成基督滿足的身量（見太5:48；弗4:14-16；彼後3:18註釋）。
**都變成新的了。**見羅6:4-6註釋。有文本在本句前還加上“凡事”。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第476頁；《教育論》第172頁；《基督教育原理》第264頁；《善惡之爭》第461頁；《懷愛倫傳略》第40頁；《服務真詮》第492頁；《今日的生活》第26頁；《拾級就主》第57頁；《成聖的人生》第55頁；《證言》卷一第32頁；《證言》卷二第294頁；《證言》卷四第625頁；《證言》卷五第650頁；《證言》卷八第84頁。

7.en:
**We walk.** That is, live, as Christians in this present life (Rom. 6:4; 8:1, 4; 13:13; 1 Cor. 7:17; Gal. 5:16; Eph. 2:2, 10).
**By faith.** Paul’s confidence in the resurrection (vs. 6, 8) has faith for its basis (see on ch. 4:18). In this life the apostle walks by faith, as in the life to come he will walk by sight.
**Sight.** Gr. eidos, “external appearance,” “form,” “shape.” Eidos refers to the thing which is seen, not to the faculty of seeing (cf. Luke 9:29, “fashion”; John 5:37). We believe in the Lord without having seen Him. Until the time when we do see Him face to face our manner of life as Christians rests on our belief in the unseen. There are two worlds, the visible and the invisible, which would be one except for the entrance of sin. A person walks by sight when he is under the influence of the material things of time, but he walks by faith when he is under the influence of things eternal. The decisions of the unregenerate man are made, his conduct determined, by external appearances. But the Christian has so firm a conviction regarding the realities of the eternal world that he thinks and acts by faith, in the light of things visible only to the eye of faith (see on Matt. 6:24–34; 2 Cor. 4:18). Those who walk by sight instead of by faith thereby express doubt concerning the invisible realities and the promises of God. By faith the kingdom of God becomes a living reality, here and now. Faith comes by “hearing,” and “hearing by the word of God” (see on Rom. 10:17). See on Heb. 11:1, 6, 13, 27, 39.
7.zh:
因我們行事為人是憑著信心，不是憑著眼見。

**行事為人。**指基督徒的現實生活（羅6:4；8:1,4；13:13；林前7:17；加5:16；弗2:2,10）。
**憑著信心。**保羅相信復活（第6,8節）是有根據的（見林後4:18註釋）。使徒在今生憑著信心行事為人，就像在來生憑著眼見生活一樣。
**眼見。**eidos，“外貌”，“形式”，“形狀”。Eidos指看得見的事物，而不是指視力（參路9:29“面貌”；約5:37）。我們沒有看見主就相信祂。在我們面對面見祂以前，我們基督徒的生活方式在於我們相信那看不見的。有兩個世界，看得見的和看不見的。若沒有罪惡的侵入，這兩個世界本是一個。當一個人受暫時的物質所影響時，他就憑著眼見行事為人。但當他受永恆的事物所影響時，他就憑著信心行事為人。未悔改之人所做的決定，他所採取的行動，乃是依據外貌。但是基督徒堅信永恆的現實，根據只有信心的眼睛才能看見的事物，憑著信心而思想行事（見太6:24-34；林後4:18註釋）。所以那些只憑眼見而不憑著信心行事為人的人，會對上帝的應許和看不見的事物表示懷疑。憑著信心，上帝的國度現在就變成活的現實。“信道是從聽道來的，聽道是從上帝的話來的”（見羅10:17註釋）。見來11:1,6,13,27,39註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第51頁；《佈道論》第64頁；《今日的生活》第342頁；《先知與君王》第175頁；《證言》卷二第339頁；《證言》卷三第14頁；見羅5:1懷愛倫註釋。

20.en:
**We are ambassadors.** Gr. presbeuō, literally, “to be older,” and thus “to be an elder,” “to be ambassador.” This characterizes the ambassador as one distinguished by dignity and experience, and therefore vested with authority. Christ’s ambassadors become such by virtue of prior attachment to Him and to His cause (see on Acts 14:23). They are distinguished for their fidelity (1 Cor. 4:1, 2; 1 Tim. 1:12), their zeal, their personal understanding of and experience with the great truths of the gospel, and their diligence in study, in prayer, in soul winning, and in building up the church. There is no greater dignity or honor than that of being an ambassador for Christ and the kingdom of heaven.
**As though God.** It is the ambassador for Christ who speaks “the word of reconciliation” (v. 19). God speaks to men through His ambassadors, even as He reconciled the world to Himself through Christ. For a discussion of God’s interest in sinners see Isa. 1:18; Jer. 44:4; Eze. 33:11; Hosea 11:8.
**In Christ’s stead.** Literally, “for Christ,” that is, on behalf of Christ. The Christian ambassador is in no sense a substitute for Christ, but simply the one through whom reconciliation is effected. He is in no sense a priestly mediator, for there is only “one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus” (1 Tim. 2:5). Reconciliation has already been provided in Christ. The minister is simply the agent by whom “the word of reconciliation” (2 Cor. 5:19) is proclaimed to others. He is not the creator or dispenser of it. He leads men and women into the presence of God, where they experience reconciliation for themselves. His task is to convince men that God has provided reconciliation in Christ. Each believer thus has access to, and deals directly with, God (Rom. 5:1; Eph. 2:13, 16–18; 3:12; Heb. 4:14–16).
**Be ye reconciled.** God is the author and dispenser of reconciliation, men are the recipients. Men cannot reconcile themselves to God by lamentation over past sins, by performing arduous service, or by practicing certain prescribed ceremonies. They receive reconciliation simply by repenting of their sins and accepting the gift of divine mercy.
20.zh:
所以，我們作基督的使者，就好像神藉我們勸你們一般。我們替基督求你們與神和好。

**我們作基督的使者。**presbeuo，直譯為“年長”，因此有“作長老”，“作使者”的意思。該詞賦予使者尊貴練達，擁有權威的特徵。這是因為基督的使者先獻身與基督和祂的聖工（見徒14:23註釋）。他們因忠誠（林前4:1,2；提前1:12）和熱心，個人對福音偉大真理的理解和體驗，以及勤於學習、祈禱、救人、建設教會而顯得出色。沒有比作基督和天國的使者更尊嚴的了。
**就好像上帝。**基督的使者傳講“和好的道理”（19節）。上帝藉著祂的使者向人說話，就像祂通過基督叫世人與自己和好。關於上帝關心罪人，見賽1:18；耶44:4；結33:11；何11:8。
**替基督。**基督的使者不可能取代基督，而只是幫助使和解生效。他不是祭司式的中保，因為“在上帝和人中間，只有一位中保，乃是降世為人的基督耶穌”（提前2:5）。在基督裡已經提供了和解。傳道人只是媒介，向他人傳講“和好的道理”（林後5:19）的，而不是和好的作者和施與者。他帶領人到上帝面前自己與祂和好。他的任務就是使人相信上帝已經在基督裡提供了和解。每一個信徒就這樣可以接近上帝，直接與祂交往（羅5:1；弗2:13,16-18；3:12；來4:14-16）。
**求你們與……和好。**上帝是和好的作者和施與者，人是領受者。人不能靠哀嘆過去的罪，進行辛苦的服務，遵守某些規定的禮節而與上帝和好。他們得到和解只能通過悔改自己的罪，接受上帝慈憐的恩賜。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第441，510頁；《早期著作》第64頁；《先祖與先知》第580頁；《證言》卷一第431頁；《證言》卷二第102，336，342，705頁；《證言》卷四第229，393，523頁；《證言》卷六第427頁；見林前3:9懷愛倫註釋。

1.zh:
我們原知道，我們這地上的帳棚若拆毀了，必得神所造，不是人手所造，在天上永存的房屋。

**我們原知道。**是憑信心，而不是憑經驗。保羅在這裡解釋了第4章盼望的理由是基督復臨時復活的確實性。復活是通往永恆世界的門戶，因此是保羅熱切盼望的目標。耶穌也曾表達了有關祂所教導真理的確實性（參約3:11；4:22）。
**我們這地上的帳棚。**關於“地上的帳篷”，保羅還說到“住在身內”時“與主相離”（第6節），並且“嘆息”直到他“地上的帳棚”拆毀（第1節），擁有“天上的房屋”（第2節）。製作帳棚的人（見徒18:3），很自然將人體與帳棚進行比較。帳棚和身體有若干相似之處：兩者的材料都是從地上來的，是暫時性的，容易毀壞。帳棚是暫時的住所，隨時都可能被拆卸搬走。約1:14的直譯是當基督道成肉身，“支搭帳棚”住在我們中間（見該處註釋）。彼得也將人體比作帳棚（見彼後1:13,14）。
**必得。**保羅堅信復活的有福盼望（林前15:20），所以他把將來的“房屋”說成是已經擁有的。他的目光注視那些尚看不見的事物（林後4:18）。他天上“房屋”與地上“房屋”一樣真實。《希伯來書》第11章所列的信心英雄同樣接受上帝的應許，並把它們當作已經實現了的。保羅有天上“房屋”的資格和權利，所以他毫不猶豫地宣稱已經擁有。
**上帝所造。**保羅還把“上帝所造”的房屋稱作“天上的房屋”（第2節），“不是人手所造”，而是“永存的”（第1節）。他把擁有這房屋稱作“穿上”它（第2節），“與主同住”時就“離開身體”（第8節）。有些人認為這“房屋”就是約14:2的“住處”。但如果是指天上真實的住宅，那麼地上的房屋也是指真實的住宅了。但這顯然不是作者的意思。多數解經家認為保羅這裡指的是“屬靈的身體”，是在復活時賜給信徒的（見林前15:35-54）。他稱他“地上的房屋”為“帳棚”，天上的“家”為“房屋”。一個是暫時的居所，另一個是永恆的。復活聖徒的身體將像他們的復活的主（路24:36-43；腓3:21）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷六第214頁。
1.en:
**For we know.** That is, by faith, not by experience. The word “for” makes ch. 5 a continuation of the theme of ch. 4. Here Paul explains that the reason for the hope stated in ch. 4 is the certainty of the resurrection at the second coming of Christ. The resurrection is the gateway to the eternal world, and hence the objective of Paul’s earnest desire. Jesus expressed the same assurance regarding the truths He taught (cf. John 3:11; 4:22).
**Our earthly house of this tabernacle.** Literally, “our earthly tent-house.” With reference to his “earthly house.” With reference to his “earthly house” Paul also speaks of being “absent from the Lord” while he is “at home in the body” (v. 6), and of groaning until his “earthly house” is “dissolved” (v. 1) and he takes possession of his “house which is from heaven” (v. 2). To compare the human body with a tent was natural for a tentmaker (see Acts 18:3). Tent and body are alike in several respects: the materials of which both are made come from the earth, both are temporary in nature, and both are easily destroyed. A tent is but a transient dwelling place, and may be taken down and moved at any time. Literally, according to John 1:14, Christ “tented” among us when He assumed a human body at the time of His incarnation (see comment there). Peter similarly compares the human body to a tent, or “tabernacle” (see 2 Peter 1:13, 14).
**We have.** Paul’s confidence in the blessed hope of the resurrection (1 Cor. 15:20) is so certain that he speaks of his future “house” as a present possession. His eyes are fixed on things that are, as yet, “not seen” (2 Cor. 4:18). His heavenly “house” is no less real to him than his earthly “house.” The heroes of faith named in Hebrews 11 similarly accepted God’s promises and acted upon them as though they were present realities. Paul has the title and the right to his heavenly “house” and does not hesitate to claim it as his.
**Building of God.** Paul also speaks of his “building of God” as a “house which is from heaven” (v. 2), and of its being “not made with hands” but “eternal” (v. 1). He speaks of taking possession of that house as being “clothed upon” with it (v. 2), and of being “ absent from the body” when he is “present with the Lord” (v. 8). Some have identified this “building” with the “mansions” of John 14:2. But if reference is to literal heavenly mansions, then the earthly house should also refer to literal earthly houses. But this is obviously not what the writer has in mind. Most Biblical expositors agree that Paul here refers to the “spiritual body” given to the believer at the time of the resurrection (see on 1 Cor. 15:35–54). He speaks of his “earthly house” as a “tent,” and of his heavenly “house” as a “building.” One is a temporary dwelling place, the other permanent. The bodies of the resurrected saints will resemble that of their resurrected Lord (Luke 24:36–43; Phil. 3:21).

2.zh:
我們在這帳棚裡歎息，深想得那從天上來的房屋，好像穿上衣服；

**我們在這帳棚裡嘆息。**將來的生活對於保羅來說非常現實。所以他焦急地期待把今生換成來生。他知道榮耀的身體正等著他，他嘆息渴望擁有它（羅7:24；8:23-25）。
**從天上來的。**見第1節註釋。
**好像穿上衣服。**ependuo，“穿上”。保羅現在把房屋或帳棚的比喻與衣服的比喻結合起來。他絕對相信復活和上帝的應許，所以對來生的喜愛遠遠超過今生。保羅希望把他必朽的身體換成將來不朽的身體，而且不經死亡，就是他所說的“赤身”（第3節）。那些“在耶穌裡睡了的”人和“活著還存留的”將在復活之日同時接受不朽的身體（帖前4:14-17；參林前15:51-54；提後4:6-8）。保羅更喜歡不經死亡而變化。
2.en:
**We groan.** The future life was so real to Paul that he looked anxiously forward to the time when he might exchange this life for it. He knew that a glorious body awaited him, and he groaned with ardent longing to take possession of it (Rom. 7:24; 8:23–25).
**To be clothed.** Gr. ependuō, “to put on over.” Paul now blends the figure of a tent or house with that of clothing. His absolute confidence in the resurrection and in the promises of God makes the future life appear incomparably preferable to this one. Paul would have been happy to exchange his mortal body for his future immortal body without experiencing death, which he describes as being “found naked” (v. 3). Those who “sleep in Jesus” and those who “are alive and remain” all receive their immortal bodies at the same time, the resurrection day (1 Thess. 4:14–17; cf. 1 Cor. 15:51–54; 2 Tim. 4:6–8). Paul would have preferred translation without seeing death.
**From heaven.** See on v. 1.

3.zh:
倘若穿上，被遇見的時候就不至於赤身了。

**穿上。**要麼穿上屬世必朽的身體，要麼穿上屬天不朽的身體。
**赤身。**既不是“地上的房屋”（第1節），也不是“從天上來的房屋”（第2節）。若有可能，保羅想不經死亡而變化。他希望加入特選的以諾和以利亞隊伍，就是不經死亡而進入天家的行列（創5:24；王下2:11）。如果這種既不擁有屬地身體，也不擁有屬天身體的中間狀態能提供在上帝面前無實體的快樂的話，保羅就不會那麼渴望躲避它了（林後5:2-4）。如果這種快樂的狀態是可能的，為什麼使徒還這麼熱切地希望得到另一個身體，即便是屬天的身體呢？見第4節註釋。
3.en:
**Being clothed.** That is, either with the earthly, mortal body, or with the heavenly, immortal body.
**Found naked.** That is, with neither an “earthly house” (v. 1) nor a “house … from heaven” (v. 2). If possible, Paul chose to be translated without seeing death. He would join the elect company of Enoch and Elijah, who were translated to heaven without seeing death (Gen. 5:24; 2 Kings 2:11). Had this intermediate state, in which he would have neither an earthly nor a heavenly body, offered the prospect of a state of disembodied bliss in the presence of God, Paul would not have so earnestly desired to avoid it (2 Cor. 5:2–4). If such a state of bliss were possible, why would the apostle so ardently desire to be cumbered with another body, even though it were a heavenly body? See on v. 4.

4.zh:
我們在這帳棚裡歎息勞苦，並非願意脫下這個，乃是願意穿上那個，好叫這必死的被生命吞滅了。

**嘆息。**見林後5:2註釋；參羅8:20-23。
**勞苦。**保羅十分了解這個必朽帳棚的脆弱，遲早會被拆毀（見林後4:7-12）。他渴望擺脫今生的一切軟弱和痛苦。他最近在以弗所的經歷和他為哥林多教會的擔憂幾乎是人所無法忍受的（見林後1:8,9；2:13；11:23-28註釋）。
**脫下。**就是沒有穿上必朽的或不朽的身體。
**被生命吞滅了。**從第4節可以看出，直到“穿上”“從天上來的房屋”（第2節），必朽的才變為不朽的。保羅在這裡並沒有支持那種沒有聖經根據的教訓，就是人在死亡，即“赤身”時，就進入了一種不朽的狀態（見林前15:51-54；帖前4:15-17；提後4:6-8註釋）。
4.en:
**Do groan.** See on 2 Cor. 5:2; cf. Rom. 8:20–23.
**Being burdened.** Paul is fully aware of the frailty of the mortal tent, which must sooner or later be dissolved (see ch. 4:7–12). He longs to be released from all the frailties and sufferings of this present life. His recent experience at Ephesus and his anxiety for the church at Corinth had been almost beyond human endurance (see on chs. 1:8, 9; 2:13; 11:23–28).
**Unclothed.** That is, without either a mortal or an immortal body.
**Swallowed up of life.** It is plain from v. 4 that mortality is not exchanged for immortality until one is “clothed” with the “house … from heaven” (v. 2). Paul here gives no support to the unscriptural teaching that at death, when one is “unclothed,” he enters upon an immortal state of existence (see on 1 Cor. 15:51–54; 1 Thess. 4:15–17; 2 Tim. 4:6–8).

5.zh:
為此，培植我們的就是神，他又賜給我們聖靈作憑據（原文是質）。

**為此。**指必朽的變為不朽的。基督徒是世界上最能滿足的人，也是從世界最少得到滿足的人。他像一個旅行者，只滿足於客棧本身，始終嚮往著家。他渴望永恆的現實，而不是地上暫時的事。肉體的思想只滿足於眼睛所看得見的；基督徒的思想則嚮往那看不見的事（見林後4:18）。熱切盼望公義和永恆世界，而不是今生的過眼雲煙，乃是基督徒真悔改和成熟的證據（見太5:48註釋）。
**培植。**katergazomai，“執行”，“完成”，“成就”，“預備”。福音工作能使人獲得“生命”（見弗2:10；彼前5:10）。
**憑據。**見林後1:22註釋。
5.en:
**Wrought.** Gr. katergazomai, “to perform,” “to accomplish,” “to achieve,” “to prepare.” It is the work of the gospel to qualify men to receive “life” (see Eph. 2:10; 1 Peter 5:10).
**Selfsame thing.** That is, the exchange of mortality for immortality. The Christian is the most contented man in the world; he is also the least contented with the world. He is like a traveler—perfectly satisfied with the inn as an inn, but having his desires ever in the direction of home. His longing is for the eternal realities, not the transient things of earth. The carnal mind is satisfied with what the eyes can see; the mind of the Christian, with things that are invisible (see ch. 4:18). The earnest longing for righteousness and for the eternal world—in preference to the baubles of this world—is evidence of genuine conversion and Christian maturity (see on Matt. 5:48).
**Earnest.** See on ch. 1:22.

6.zh:
所以，我們時常坦然無懼，並且曉得我們住在身內，便與主相離。

**時常坦然無懼。**保羅對復活的確定性沒有絲毫懷疑（見14節註釋）。
**身。**或“地上的房屋”（見第1節註釋）。
**與主相離。**指不在祂面前，還沒有“穿上”“從天上來的房屋”（第2節），不能“面對面”見祂（林前13:12；參約叄14）。見第8節註釋。
6.en:
**Always confident.** There was never the least doubt in Paul’s mind concerning the certainty of the resurrection (see on v. 14).
**The body.** Or, the “earthly house” (see on v. 1).
**Absent from the Lord.** That is, not in His immediate presence, not yet “clothed upon” with the “house which is from heaven” (v. 2), not able to see Him “face to face” (1 Cor. 13:12; cf. 3 John 14). See on v. 8.

8.zh:
我們坦然無懼，是更願意離開身體與主同住。

**離開身體。**就是離開現實世界的生活。
**與主同住。**一些人根據6-8節從的字面，認為基督徒的靈魂在死時就立即“與主同住”；保羅既渴望與主同住（第2節），就歡迎死亡的到來。但在第3,4節中，保羅把死說成是“赤身” 或“脫下”的狀態。若有可能，他希望避免這種中間狀態，而渴望“穿上”他“從天上來的房屋”。換言之，他希望不經歷死亡就改變（見2-4節註釋）。保羅在其他地方說明（見林前15:51-54；帖前4:15-17；提後4:6-8等），人在死時並沒有個別地“穿上”不朽，而是在義人復活時同時穿上的。
或者這樣說：保羅在林後5:2-4提到了“生命”，顯然指不朽的生命，在復活時“穿上”“從天上來的房屋”時臨到（見第4節註釋），而不是“赤身的”或“脫下”的死亡狀態。他在第8節中表示希望“離開身體”“與主同住”，但顯然“離開身體”並不是說沒有實體（“赤身”，或“脫下”）了，因為他在2-4節已經說明他不要這種中間狀態，而要儘量避免它。要有“生命”（第4節），“與主同住”（第8節），就需要擁有“天上來的房屋”（第2節）。所以仔細研究保羅的論述，就很明確地排除了一種死亡和復活之間的狀態；在這種狀態中，無實體（“赤身”或“脫下”）的靈“與主同住”。參羅8:22,23；見腓1:21-23註釋。
聖經說死亡只是睡覺。在第一次復活時，信徒將被喚醒（約11:11-14,25,26；林前15:20,51-54；帖前4:14-17；5:10）。那時，活著的和復活的聖徒都將要“與主同住”（見帖前4:16-18註釋），沒有誰先誰後（參來11:39,40）。
8.en:
**Absent from the body.** That is, from life in the present world.
**Present with the Lord.** From a superficial reading of vs. 6–8 some have concluded that at death the soul of the Christian goes immediately to be “present with the Lord,” and that Paul, ardently desiring to be with the Lord (v. 2), welcomed death. But in vs. 3, 4 Paul describes death as a state of being “naked,” or “unclothed.” He hopes, if at all possible, to avoid this intermediate state, and ardently desires to be “clothed” with his “house … from heaven.” In other words, he hopes to be translated without seeing death (see on vs. 2–4). Elsewhere (see on 1 Cor. 15:51–54; 1 Thess. 4:15–17; 2 Tim. 4:6–8; etc.) Paul makes it certain that men are not “clothed” with immortality individually at death, but simultaneously at the resurrection of the just.
Or, to restate it in this way: In 2 Cor. 5:2–4 Paul has already declared that “life,” obviously meaning immortal life, comes when one is “clothed upon” with his “house … from heaven” at the resurrection (see on v. 4), not in the “naked,” or “unclothed,” state of death. In v. 8 he expresses the desire to be “absent from the body” and “present with the Lord,” but it is obvious that being “absent from the body” does not mean being disembodied (“naked,” or “unclothed”), for in vs. 2–4 he has stated clearly that he does not desire this intermediate state and would avoid it if at all possible. To have “life” (v. 4) and to be “present with the Lord” (v. 8) thus requires possession of the “house … from heaven” (v. 2). Careful scrutiny of Paul’s statements thus clearly and decisively rules out any possibility of a state between death and the resurrection in which, as disembodied (“naked,” or “unclothed”) spirits, men go to be “present with the Lord.” Compare Rom. 8:22, 23; see on Phil. 1:21–23.
The Bible declares death to be but a sleep from which believers will be awakened at the first resurrection (John 11:11–14, 25, 26; 1 Cor. 15:20, 51–54; 1 Thess. 4:14–17; 5:10). It is not until then that both the living and the resurrected saints will be with the Lord (see on 1 Thess. 4:16–18). Neither group precedes the other (cf. Heb. 11:39, 40).

9.zh:
所以，無論是住在身內，離開身外，我們立了志向，要得主的喜悅。

**所以。**鑑於保羅對復活和來生的信心（6-8節）。
**無論是住在身內，離開身外。**見第6,8節註釋。
**立了志向。**philotimeomai，“出於被愛榮譽之心”，“為……而努力奮鬥”（參羅15:20；帖前4:11）。在可能打倒他的試煉面前（參林後4:7-18），激勵保羅前進的動機，就是他和他的信徒復活與活著變化的光榮前景。保羅希望當站在“基督臺前”時，他個人的努力會得到悅納（5:10）。他立了志向，不是為了在上帝面前賺取功勞，也不是為了彌補自己的罪惡，替基督所賜的義加添什麼，而是為了在拯救同胞的工作中與基督合作（林前15:9,10；西1:29）。他立了志向，要讓自己生活中的一切都反照基督，因為他知道這是在主眼前是蒙喜悅和接納的。真假信徒的區別在於追求上帝的悅納還是人的悅納。決心不為自己而活，卻為基督而活的人，不會把時間花在安逸閒懶或追求屬世的娛樂上（加1:10）。
據說古時的鍊金者會盯著坩堝中融化的金屬看，直到他看見自己的容貌在金屬上反映出來，從而知道這是純金。基督也是這樣，祂希望我們身上反映祂的形象（參伯23:10）。我們有權利與基督相像。聖經說祂“不求自己的喜悅”（羅15:3；參來11:5）。行義僅僅是為了它是義或出於上帝的要求，和行義是為了因基督的緣故而做所得的快樂，兩者之間有很大的區別。出於責任心行義是值得讚許的，而出於對主的熱愛而行義則更值得讚許。基督的愛激勵保羅過他所過的生活（林後5:14）。遵守上帝誡命的擔子，會因愛的動機而變得輕省（見太22:28-30註釋；參羅8:1-4）。誠心求上帝悅納的心，會使基督徒準確無誤地識別何為惡，何為善（見羅8:5-8註釋）。
**得主的喜悅。**保羅最關心的不是他是否能活下去，或他在地上的勞苦是否結束。他所關心的只是無論發生什麼，他的生活都應蒙上帝悅納（見提後4:6-8；見太25:21；路19:17註釋）。
9.en:
**Wherefore.** That is, in view of Paul’s confidence in the resurrection and the future life (vs. 6–8).
**Labour.** Gr. philotimeomai, “to be actuated by a love of honor,” “to strive earnestly for” (cf. Rom. 15:20; 1 Thess. 4:11). The motive that ever spurred Paul onward, in spite of the trials that beat down upon him (cf. 2 Cor. 4:7–18), was the glorious prospect of the resurrection, or of translation without death, both for himself and for his converts. Paul personally strove to be “accepted” when he should stand before “the judgment seat of Christ” (ch. 5:10). He labored, not to earn merit before God, not to atone for his sins, not to add something to the gift of Christ’s righteousness, but to cooperate with Christ in the task of saving his fellow men (1 Cor. 15:9, 10; Col. 1:29). He labored, as well, to make everything in his own life a reflection of Christ, for he knew this would be pleasing and acceptable in the sight of the Lord. The difference between the sincere and the insincere believer is that one seeks the approbation of God and the other the approbation of man. He who resolves to live, not for himself, but for Christ, will not spend his time in ease and idleness or in the pursuit of worldly pleasure (Gal. 1:10).
It is said that in ancient times a refiner of gold gazed intently at the molten metal in his crucible until he could see his own face mirrored in it. Then he knew that it was pure. Thus it is with Christ, who looks for His own reflection in us (cf. Job 23:10). It is our privilege to become like Christ, of whom it is said that He “pleased not himself” (Rom. 15:3; cf. Heb. 11:5). There is all the difference in the world between doing right only because it is right and because God requires it, and doing it for the joy that comes when it is done for Christ’s sake. Laudable as it may be to do right from a sense of duty, how much better to do it from a heart overflowing with love for the Master. It was the love of Christ that constrained Paul to live as he did (2 Cor. 5:14). The burden of obedience to God’s commandments becomes light when it is motivated by love (see on Matt. 22:28–30; cf. Rom. 8:1–4). The sincere desire to please Christ enables the Christian to discern, with unerring accuracy, between that which is evil and that which is good (see on Rom. 8:5–8).
**Whether present or absent.** See on vs. 6, 8.
**Accepted of him.** The great concern was not whether Paul should live on, or whether his earthly labors should be brought to a close. His concern was only that, whatever might happen, his life should be such that it would meet the approval of God (see 2 Tim. 4:6–8; see on Matt. 25:21; Luke 19:17).

11.zh:
我們既知道主是可畏的，所以勸人。但我們在神面前是顯明的，盼望在你們的良心裡也是顯明的。

**可畏的。**phobos，在《新約》其他地方譯為“害怕”。這種“害怕”與淪喪的罪人將來所要經歷的恐怖大不一樣。虔誠的敬畏是智慧的開端（詩111:10；箴9:10），與以賽亞在上帝面前所感受的深深敬畏意義相同（賽6:5），是依據對上帝的品格、威權和偉大的認識，以及感覺自己的不配。這是真虔誠的根源和主要動力。它阻止驕傲（見箴26:12），威懾罪惡（代下19:7；伯1:1,8；28:28；箴8:13；徒5:5），消除其他一切的恐懼（箴14:26,27；19:23）。敬畏上帝的人能擺脫一切的憂慮。敬畏主就是崇敬，順服慈愛的天父（詩103:11；參詩111:10）。見詩19:9註釋。
**勸人。**見20節註釋。
**我們在上帝面前是顯明的。**我們是什麼樣的，上帝很瞭解，正如原文所暗示的，祂是一直都清楚的。更重要的是，上帝完全知道保羅討祂喜歡的崇高目的。保羅相信哥林多信徒現在也因此被說服了。他們當中即使不是很多，總有些人受到試探懷疑他美好的信心。他呼籲他們以良心來判斷，渴望他們能認清事實。他作為基督使者的真正品格（20節）在眾人面前是昭然若揭的。
11.en:
**Terror.** Gr. phobos, elsewhere in the NT always translated “fear.” This fear is something far different from the terror that lost sinners will one day experience. Godly fear is the beginning of wisdom (Ps. 111:10; Prov. 9:10). It is synonymous with profound reverence such as Isaiah felt when in God’s presence (Isa. 6:5), and is based on a realization of the character, majesty, and greatness of God, and of one’s own unworthiness. It is the root and mainspring of true piety. It prevents conceit (see Prov. 26:12), and is a deterrent to sin (2 Chron. 19:7; Job 1:1, 8; 28:28; Prov. 8:13; Acts 5:5). It gives release from all other fears (Prov. 14:26, 27; 19:23). He who stands in awe of God can be free of all anxiety. The fear of the Lord is reverent adoration and obedient respect for a loving heavenly Father (Ps. 103:11; cf. Ps. 111:10). See on Ps. 19:9.
**Persuade men.** See on v. 20.
**We are made manifest.** What we are is known to God, and as the Greek implies, has been known to Him all along.
