His only thought was for the well-being of the Corinthians as individuals and as a church.
**Heaviness.** Gr. lupē, “sorrow,” “pain,” “grief.”

2.zh:
倘若我叫你們憂愁，除了我叫那憂愁的人以外，誰能叫我快樂呢？

**叫……憂愁。**lupeo，“使……悲傷”，“使……痛苦”。保羅為教會中罪惡的泛濫而憂愁，他前一封責備的信無疑使教會中真誠的人傷心，也使另一些人生氣（參林後10:9,10）。在這種情況下，再次訪問無論對於他和他們來說都是痛苦的，會加重所有相關者的憂傷。但是如果他的信能先達到預期的效果，再次的訪問對彼此來說就都是快樂的。
2.en: **Make … sorry.** Gr. lupeō, “to make sad,” “to cause grief.” Paul was grieved by evils rampant in the church, and his previous letter of reproof had no doubt saddened the sincerehearted members of the church, as it had angered others (cf. ch. 10:9, 10). Under such circumstances a second visit would have been painful both to him and to them. This would compound the sadness for all concerned. But if his letter could first accomplish its intended result, another visit would prove mutually joyful.

3.zh:
我曾把這事寫給你們，恐怕我到的時候，應該叫我快樂的那些人，反倒叫我憂愁。我也深信，你們眾人都以我的快樂為自己的快樂。

我曾……寫……。保羅在這裡可能是指《哥林多前書》，但也可能指林前5:9中所提到的信。那些認為這裡的上下文（林後2:3,4）和7:8-12排除了指《哥林多前書》可能性的論據，是沒有說服力的（見本卷註釋822頁；林前3-6章）。
**把這事寫給你們。**touto auto，可譯為“這事”，也可譯為“因此”。保羅寫了前一封信的責備和勸戒，希望他們能悔改（見第2節註釋）。
**應該……快樂。**保羅最高興的就是看到男男女女經歷了新生並在基督裡成長。他的快樂取決於他們的屬靈健康狀況。當他們軟弱不前時，保羅是不可能快樂的。福音執事的工作就是散佈喜樂而不是憂愁。基督希望祂自己的喜樂能在祂門徒的內心和生活中得到反映（約17:13）。
**你們眾人。**保羅相信給他帶來快樂的事，也會給他們帶來快樂。
3.en:
**I wrote.** Paul here probably refers to 1 Corinthians, though possibly to the letter mentioned in 1 Cor. 5:9. Arguments to the effect that the context here (2 Cor. 2:3, 4) and in ch. 7:8–12 precludes the possibility of reference to 1 Corinthians are not convincing (see p. 822; 1 Cor. 3 to 6).
**This same unto you.** Gr. touto auto, which should probably be translated “this very thing,” though possibly, “for this very reason.” Paul had written that previous letter of censure and admonition in the hope that it might effect a reformation (see on v. 2).
**Ought to rejoice.** Paul’s supreme joy was that of seeing men and women experience the new birth and grow up into Christ. His happiness depended upon their spiritual state of health. Paul could not be happy while they were weak or downcast. The work of the gospel minister is to dispense joy, not sorrow. Christ desired His own joy to be reflected in the hearts and lives of His disciples (John 17:13).
**Of you all.** Paul believed that what brought joy to him would also bring joy to them.

4.zh:
我先前心裡難過痛苦，多多的流淚，寫信給你們，不是叫你們憂愁，乃是叫你們知道我格外的疼愛你們。

**痛苦。**sunoche，“悲痛”，“傷心”，直譯為“擠在一起”，指緊張。意思是內心受到很大的壓力。這種壓力而產生悲痛。
**多多地流淚。**保羅曾嚴厲地責備教訓他們，不是因為生氣，而是因為憂傷。基督在憐憫祂的子民時也曾哭了（太23:37,38）。要挽回犯錯的人，責備不可抱著粗暴傲慢的態度，而要以極大的溫柔和同情。保羅在危險、迫害和死亡面前有著無限的勇氣，但他在被迫責備在基督裡的弟兄時卻哭了（見徒20:31；腓3:18）。
成功地挽回犯罪的人，不是靠嚴厲的指責，嘲笑，諷刺，或公開他們的罪。這些鋒利的武器所不能成就的，藉著深切的關懷，“多多地流淚”卻能奏效。教會成員陷入罪惡的不幸景況，引起了每一個真基督徒的痛苦傷心。神聖的關懷和基督化的愛把教會團結在一起，並防止因受懲戒的人而意見分歧。
傳道工作需要不遮掩罪惡，不為罪惡尋找藉口，毫不畏懼地譴責罪惡的人（參結9:4）。他們被基督的愛所激勵，勇敢地對付教會里的罪惡（林後5:14）。從特殊的意義上說，他們是修補“破口”，重修“路徑與人居住的”人（賽58:12；見來13:7,17）。忽略罪惡從來就不是愛的表現。有時愛需要嚴厲。教會中的愛並不是意味著同情和忍耐頑固不化的成員，以犧牲教會的完美和其他信徒的安全為代價。認為愛總是不必要的遷就，就等於說它是軟弱，缺乏主動，力量和勇氣。傳道人對信徒的愛不只是溫柔地同情他們，還要不斷地關懷他的們的屬靈利益，為他們的屬靈進步而高興，為他們的罪惡而憂傷，有堅定的領導才能，在想企圖驅散羊群的人類仇敵面前表現出堅強不屈的勇氣。保羅作為永遠福音的執事，為了別人的得救，準備經受任何艱難，即使犧牲性命，也在所不惜。他的愛絕無軟弱。耶穌和保羅都沒有在愛中注入病態的情感。他們都不斷表現出獲得高尚艱難成就的能力，和戰勝魔鬼的力量，不管魔鬼是以什麼樣的偽裝來攻擊教會。見太5:43,44註釋。
**我……寫信。**見第3節註釋。
**知道……疼愛。**保羅寫信的目的不是要引起人憂愁，而是要表達真誠的愛，這愛指導使徒處理與他們的一切關係（見林後5:14註釋）。他們如果首先認識到他所說的都是出於愛，就會獲得更大的益處。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第300頁；《服務真詮》第166頁。
4.en:
**Anguish.** Gr. sunochē, “distress,” “anguish,” literally, “a holding together,” that is, a tenseness. The thought is that the heart seems to be under great pressure, and that the pressure produces grief.
**I wrote.** See on v. 3.
**Many tears.** Paul had administered stern reproof and discipline, not in anger but in sorrow. Christ wept as He yearned for His people (Matt. 23:37, 38). Reproof intended to win back the erring must never be done in harshness or with an overbearing attitude, but with great tenderness and compassion. Paul possessed boundless courage in the face of danger, persecution, and death, but he wept when compelled to censure his brethren in Christ (see Acts 20:31; Phil. 3:18).
Successful dealing with sinners is not achieved by bitter denunciation, by ridicule or sarcasm, by making public their sins. What these harsh weapons cannot accomplish may be done by affectionate concern, with “many tears.” The unfortunate spectacle of a church member falling into sin awakens anguish and distress in the mind of every true follower of Christ. Godly concern and Christlike love unite the church and prevent differences of opinion concerning those disciplined.
The ministry needs men who will not palliate or excuse sin, nor shrink from rebuking evil (cf. Eze. 9:4). They are men who, while dealing courageously with evil in the church, are constrained by the love of Christ (2 Cor. 5:14). They are, in a special sense, repairers of the “breach” and restorers of “paths to dwell in” (Isa. 58:12; see Heb. 13:7, 17). It is never a demonstration of love to pass by sin. Sometimes love must needs be severe. Love in the church does not mean the display of pity and long-suffering toward obdurate members at the expense of the integrity of the church or the safety of other members. To consider love as something always necessarily flaccid is to identify it with weakness, lack of initiative, forcefulness, and courage. The minister’s love for his people means more than a feeling of tender emotion for them, it means also a continuous attitude of concern for their well-being, joy in their spiritual growth, sadness over their sins, strong leadership, and firm, unyielding courage when the enemy of souls seeks to scatter the flock. Paul, as a minister of the everlasting gospel, was prepared to go through any amount of suffering, even to the sacrifice of life itself, for the salvation of others. There was nothing weak or effeminate about his love. Neither Jesus nor Paul invest love with sickly sentimentality. Both continually reveal the capacity for noble and difficult accomplishments and strength to overcome the devil in whatever guise he may appear to attack the church. See on Matt. 5:43, 44.
**Know the love.** Paul’s purpose in writing was not to cause sorrow, but to express, if possible, the ardent love that guided the apostle in all his relations with them (see on ch. 5:14). If they could first realize that all he said was spoken in love they would be able the better to profit by it.

5.zh:
若有叫人憂愁的，他不但叫我憂愁，也是叫你們眾人有幾分憂愁。我說幾分，恐怕說得太重。

**叫人憂愁。**有人認為保羅在這裡是指林前5:1淫亂的人，也有人認為是指反對他的首領。兩種見解的理由都沒有充分的說服力。但由於聖經沒有特指反對的首領或淫亂的人，本註釋假定保羅指的是淫亂的人。從《哥林多前書》中可以看出，這種道德的淪喪已成為哥林多教會最嚴重的問題。由於公開容忍這個犯罪的人，在一段時間裡固執地拒絕有效地處理這個問題，情況更加惡化了。這段經文（林後2:5-11）表明教會已經按照保羅的指示，開除了那個犯罪的人。這個措施顯然使他真心悔改。保羅在這裡提議讓那個人重新回到教會。
保羅處理犯錯信徒的方法為今天解決類似問題提供了範例。保羅對待堅持不改的人是堅決而嚴厲的。但那人一旦悔改了，保羅就非常溫柔地對待他。保羅現在設法減輕悔改的人負罪愧疚的重擔，使他重新為弟兄們所接納。保羅沒有一次提犯罪者的名字，只是謹慎地說“這樣的人”。不要無謂地反覆提說一個人的罪，傷害他的感情。至今他的名字也只有上帝知道。這是基督處理此類問題的精神和方法（見約8:10,11；見太18:1-35註釋）。與那些公開犯錯之人的名字，不必要地傷害和侮辱他們的做法是多麼不同啊！只要真心悔改，就了結此事，不要再提，而是全心全意地接受已被寬恕的人。
**不但叫我憂愁。**保羅所建議的嚴厲措施不帶任何個人動機。他為教會所遭遇的痛苦和困惑而憂愁。
**有幾分。**本節後半部分可以更明確地譯為：“但在一定的程度上對你們所有人──免得我[對那悔改的罪人]過於嚴歷”。罪行主要是針對整個哥林多教會，而不是針對保羅的。
**說得太重。**epibareo，“加重擔於”。問題既已解決，保羅就刻意避免誇大罪行而傷害犯錯的人。
5.en:
**Caused grief.** There is a difference of opinion as to whether Paul here refers to the incestuous person of 1 Cor. 5:1 or to the ringleader of opposition to him. Reasons set forth for both are inconclusive. However, because there is no specific reference in Scripture to the ringleader, as there is to the incestuous person, this commentary assumes that Paul refers to the latter. From the first epistle it appears that this case of immorality had been the most acute problem in the Corinthian church. The case had been aggravated by the open toleration of this offender and by the stubborn refusal, for a time, to deal effectively with it. This passage (2 Cor. 2:5–11) reveals that the church had by now complied with Paul’s instructions and had disfellowshiped the offender. This course of action had evidently led him to genuine repentance. Paul here counsels his restoration and reinstatement in the church.
Paul’s method of dealing with an erring member provides a commendable example for similar cases today. Paul’s firmness and severity toward the man while he remained unrepentant gave way to great tenderness once he had repented. Paul now sought to mitigate the contrite man’s burden of guilt and condemnation, and to restore him to favor with his brethren. Never once does he mention the man’s name, but considerately speaks of him as “such a one” (v. 7). There is no needless repetition of the man’s sins to wound his feelings. Today his name is known only to God. This is the spirit and method of Christ in dealing with such cases (see John 8:10, 11; see on Matt. 18:1–35). How different from those who would publicize the names of offenders and thereby crush them with unnecessary pain and dishonor! Where there is genuine repentance the case should be brought to a close, with no further reference to the incident and with wholehearted acceptance of the forgiven person.
**Not grieved me.** No personal motives had been involved in the stern measures recommended by Paul. His grief had been over the distress and confusion that had come to the church.
**But in part.** The latter part of the verse may be rendered more clearly, “but to some extent all of you—lest I be too severe [toward the repentant offender].” The offense was not so much against Paul as against the entire Corinthian church.
**Overcharge.** Gr. epibareō, “to put a burden upon.” Now that the case had been settled, Paul deliberately avoided wounding the offender by appearing to magnify the offense.

6.zh:
這樣的人受了眾人的責罰也就夠了，

**眾人的。**指多數人。在這件事上教會接受了保羅的建議，但不是一致作出決定。少數不同意的人，無疑包括那些在道德上放縱自己的人，猶太化的派別，和一些反對保羅干預此事的人。他們挑戰他的權威，或不贊成這麼嚴厲的懲罰。挽救性的懲戒和處罰性的懲戒不同，需要耐心和體諒。在這件事上，它成了整個教會的責任（見林前12:20-27）。保羅本來可以把少數不同意之人的反對視為對他個人的攻擊，回應他們惡意的曲解和批評，但他沒有這樣做。
**責罰。**或“處罰”，意為應受的懲罰。
**夠了。**教會懲戒的目的已經達到；犯罪的人已經悔改了。現在是讓他重獲弟兄們的信任，恢復交往的時候了。基督教的懲戒是愛的舉措。其目的是挽救，而非報復。要高舉上帝的誡命，維持教會的秩序。要保護教會其他信徒的利益和教會的名譽，但也要儘可能引導罪人悔改。它要成為潛犯罪者警告，和重犯此罪的威懾。
6.en:
**Sufficient.** The objective of church discipline had been accomplished; the offender had repented, and it was now time to restore him to the confidence and fellowship of his brethren. Christian discipline is a work of love, not of vengeance. Its objective is not revenge, but restoration. It must uphold the commandments of God and maintain church order. It must safeguard the other members of the church and protect the good name of the church, but it should also, wherever possible, lead the sinner to repentance. It must serve as a warning to other potential offenders and a deterrent to a repetition of the offense.
**Punishment.** Or, “penalty,” implying a merited judgment.
**Of many.** That is, by the majority. The church had complied with Paul’s recommendation in the case, but the decision had not been unanimous. The dissenting minority doubtless included some who tended to be lax in morals themselves, members of the Judaizing faction, and a few who resented Paul’s interference in the case, challenged his authority, or objected to so severe a penalty. Remedial discipline—as contrasted with punitive discipline—requires patience and understanding. In this instance it had become the responsibility of the whole church (see 1 Cor. 12:20–27). Paul might have taken the opposition of the dissident minority as a personal affront and responded to its misrepresentation and criticism in a spirit of bitterness and vindictiveness, but he did not.

7.zh:
倒不如赦免他，安慰他，免得他憂愁太過，甚至沉淪了。

**倒不如。**外科醫生切開口病灶完成了手術之後，就要縫合傷口，使病人恢復健康。哥林多犯罪的人已被大多數信徒開除出教。但現在他已悔改，繼續懲戒就顯得是報復性和懲罰性的了，有可能使他灰心，不能忠於新立的志向。
**安慰他。**單赦免還不夠。教會要接受回來的弟兄，就像上帝悅納悔改的罪人一樣。罪行要赦免和遺忘。教會有責任仁慈地對待每一個真心悔改的人（見路15:7；弗4:32註釋）。
**沉淪。**或“淹沒”，如溺水。聖經常常把過度悲傷或災難比作洪水（見詩69:1；124:2-5；賽8:7,8）。我們常說被悲傷所淹沒。保羅真誠地關心悔改之人的心靈。教會的信徒不可繼續棄絕或輕視犯罪的人，免得過度的悲傷淹沒他，把他趕回到罪惡之中。
7.en:
**So that contrariwise.** Having made an incision and accomplished his purpose, a surgeon binds up the wound and seeks to restore his patient to health. The offender at Corinth had been deprived of Christian fellowship by the majority of the church members. But now that he had repented, further discipline would be vindictive and punitive, and would tend to discourage him from being loyal to his new resolve.
**Comfort him.** Forgiveness was not enough. The church was to receive this returning brother as God receives a penitent sinner into His favor. The offense should be forgiven and forgotten. It is the duty of the church to treat every true penitent with kindness (see on Luke 15:7; Eph. 4:32).
**Swallowed up.** Or, “overwhelmed,” as if drowning. Excessive sorrow or calamity is often compared to floodwaters (see Ps. 69:1; 124:2–5; Isa. 8:7, 8). We commonly speak of being overwhelmed with grief or drowned in sorrow. Paul was genuinely concerned for the repentant man’s soul. There must be no evidence of continued rejection or disdain by church members, lest excessive grief overwhelm him and drive him back into sin.

8.zh:
所以我勸你們，要向他顯出堅定不移的愛心來。

**顯出堅定不移的。**kuroo，“批准”，“確認”，“重申”（參加3:15）。這個法律術語用來指批准一個協議。這裡是指教會通過教令或表決批准或確認（見太18:18註釋）。教會作為一個團體，撤消原來的決議，恢復那個人信徒的身份。懲戒是教會通過正式的決議實施的，恢復教籍也當公開正式地進行。那個人得到了在教會里受弟兄接納的充分保證，今後就不會對他恢復教籍的有效性置疑 了。
8.en: **Confirm.** Gr. kuroō, “to ratify,” “to confirm,” “to reaffirm” (cf. Gal. 3:15). It was a legal term used of validating an agreement. Here it means to ratify or confirm by decree or vote of the church (see on Matt. 18:18). Acting in its corporate capacity, the church should revoke its former action and restore the man to fellowship. Discipline had been administered by a formal action on the part of the church; restoration to fellowship should be no less public and official. The man was to have full assurance of the favor of his brethren in the church. Thus, in the future, no question as to the validity of his reinstatement could arise.

9.zh:
為此我先前也寫信給你們，要試驗你們，看你們凡事順從不順從。

**寫信。**見第3節註釋。
**試驗。**保羅在《哥林多前書》中就教會中犯罪的人發出指示的另一個原因，就是希望考驗他們的順服與忠誠。他們已忠實地處理了教會里的罪惡，經受住了考驗。但是這個考驗與其說涉及對保羅權威的順服，倒不如說是對基督權威的順服。他們順服保羅，以他為使徒，為耶穌基督的直接代表，為主所說“聽從你們的，就是聽從我”（路10:16）的人。
9.en:
**Did I write.** See on v. 3.
**The proof.** Another reason for Paul’s instruction regarding the church offender in his former epistle was his desire to test their obedience and loyalty. Events had now proved them loyal. They had measured up to the test by dealing faithfully with sin in the church. This test, however, was not so much one of obedience to Paul’s authority as to that of Christ. They submitted to Paul as an apostle, a direct representative of Jesus Christ, and as one to whom the Lord said: “He that heareth you heareth me” (Luke 10:16).

10.zh:
你們赦免誰，我也赦免誰。我若有所赦免的，是在基督面前為你們赦免的；

**你們赦免誰。**由於哥林多教會已提供了充分的證據表明他們忠於原則，現在保羅與信徒們一起對此表示信任。他充分認識到教會在基督引導下處理自身問題的權威，（見太16:19；18:17,18；約20:23）。基督已將權柄賜給整個教會，讓他們在聖靈的引導和管理下行動。
各位學者都注意到，這是《新約》中唯一記載行使保留或赦免罪惡之權威的事例。在這裡行使這一權柄的是保羅而不是彼得。這個權柄是基督授予全體使徒的；他們是基督教會的代表（見約20:23）。
**在基督面前。**沒有依據可以得出結論說，使徒或教會有權免除人在上帝面前的罪責。只有上帝擁有這樣的權利（見可2:7-11）。如果人真心悔改了，上帝根據自己的應許就已赦免了他（耶31:34；約一1:9）。保羅所說的赦免只是人承認上帝已經赦免他而已（見太16:19註釋）。上帝授權給祂在地上的代表確認上天對每一個悔改之人的赦免。
10.en:
**Whom ye forgive.** Because the Corinthian church had given full proof of its loyalty to principle, Paul now unites with its members in the proposed vote of confidence. He fully recognizes the authority of the church, under Christ, to deal with its own problems (see Matt. 16:19; 18:17, 18; John 20:23). Christ has delegated authority to the church as a corporate body, acting under the direction and presidency, as it were, of the Holy Spirit.
Various scholars have noted that this is the only specific instance on record in the NT of the exercise of ecclesiastical authority to retain and remit sins, and that here it is exercised by Paul, not by Peter. This power was given by Christ to the apostles collectively and as representatives of the Christian church (see John 20:23).
**Person of Christ.** Rather, “presence of Christ,” or “before Christ.” There is no basis for concluding that either the apostle or the church had power to release the man from accountability for his sins before God. None but God could do that (see Mark 2:7–11). If the man had sincerely repented, God, according to His promise, had already forgiven him (Jer. 31:34; 1 John 1:9). Paul’s vote to forgive was simply the human acknowledgment that God had already pardoned him (see on Matt. 16:19). God has authorized His representatives on earth to assure the forgiveness of Heaven to every repentant soul.

11.zh:
免得撒但趁著機會勝過我們，因我們並非不曉得他的詭計。

**免得撒但。**保羅曾指示哥林多信徒將犯罪的人“交給撒但”（林前5:4,5），為了他最終的得救。但是如果教會沒有赦免和重新接納悔改的罪人，撒但就會得勢。撒但不僅在引誘人犯罪上得勢，也因我們不寬恕悔改的罪人而得勢。
**詭計。**或“計謀”。撒但不斷設法傷害毀滅人的心靈。他的詭計特別針對教會和渴望跟隨基督的人。他有時成功地使個人甚至教會最好最純潔的計劃和努力轉入歧途。當人看不到個人的得救時，心靈就會痛苦或絕望；憤怒和分裂將會危害教會。
撒但的詭計藉著教會信徒冒失又被誤導的熱情而實現。他們尖酸刻薄，吹毛求疵，表現出批評挑剔的精神，對人類命運的漠不關心；將薄荷，茴香，芹菜獻上十分之一，倒不行那律法上更重要的事──公義，憐憫和信實（太23:23）。上帝的品格就這樣被歪曲醜化；祂的聖工遭到羞辱；教會的立場受到嚴重破壞。
基督徒不只要應付在判斷和行為方面犯錯的弟兄（見太4:1註釋），還要應付一個有位格的仇敵。在曠野試探我們主的是一個有位格的魔鬼（太4:1-11）。保羅曾遭到“撒但的差役”的攻擊（林後12:7），親身接觸到與他所必須面對的那種仇敵。他認識魔鬼的真面目。他清晰的屬靈洞察力能識透撒但的偽裝。他用上帝的道，聖靈的寶劍，戰勝了惡者（弗6:16,17；約壹2:14）。“要穿戴上帝所賜的全副軍裝，就能抵擋魔鬼的詭計”（弗6:11）。我們遵從這樣的勸勉，就能戰勝敵人。參《善惡之爭》516頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第516頁；《先知與君王》第654頁；《證言》卷一第211，304，707頁；《證言》卷二第143，313頁；《證言》卷三第476頁；《證言》卷六第446頁。
11.en:
**Lest Satan.** Paul had instructed the Corinthians to deliver the sinner “unto Satan” (1 Cor. 5:4, 5), with a view to his ultimate salvation. But if the church failed to forgive and restore the repentant offender, Satan would still gain an advantage. He gains an advantage not only by leading people into sin but also by our failure to forgive them when they repent.
**Devices.** Or, “designs.” Satan is constantly seeking to injure and destroy the souls of men. His designs are directed particularly against the church and against individuals who aspire to follow Christ. He sometimes succeeds in perverting even the best and purest plans and efforts of individuals, and even of the church. Where the salvation of the individual is lost sight of, hearts will be embittered or driven to despair, and irritation and division will injure the church.
Satan’s designs are accomplished in rash and misguided zeal of church members, by harsh and rigid pretensions at perfection, by a critical and censorious spirit, by cold indifference to the fate of men, by tithing mint and anise and cummin and omitting the weightier matters of the law—justice, mercy, and faith (Matt. 23:23). God’s character is thus maligned and misunderstood, His cause is dishonored, and the standing of the church is seriously impaired.
The Christian deals not simply with some error of judgment and conduct in an offending brother but with a personal foe (see on Matt. 4:1). It was a personal devil that tempted our Lord in the wilderness (Matt. 4:1–11). Paul had been buffeted by a “messenger of Satan” (2 Cor. 12:7), and knew from experience the kind of adversary he had to face. He recognized the devil for what he is. His clear spiritual perception pierced the disguise used by Satan, and he overcame him by the sword of the Spirit, the Word of God (Eph. 6:16, 17; 1 John 2:14). Victory over our adversary comes by following the admonition to “put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil” (Eph. 6:11). Compare GC 516.

12.zh:
我從前為基督的福音到了特羅亞，主也給我開了門。

**基督的福音。**就是來自基督的福音。保羅離開以弗所後，打算化一段時間在特羅亞傳道。
**到了特羅亞。**12,13節表達了保羅對哥林多信徒深厚的個人感情，以及他始終關心他們的利益。他顯然曾派提多前往哥林多做和睦的工作，並獲得有關教會情況以及他們如何對待他責備信息的詳情（參《使徒行述》323頁）。他們似乎說好了在特羅亞會面，提多大概受到阻撓未能赴約。保羅想像他對哥林多教會最大的擔心已變為現實，心中不勝憂慮。這種想法妨礙他在特羅亞有效地開展工作。關於特羅亞市和保羅以前訪問那裡，見徒16:8-11註釋。保羅在從哥林多返回前往耶路撒冷的路上，再次訪問了特羅亞（徒20:6-12）。他第一次在羅馬被囚獲釋後也訪問過特羅亞（見提後4:13註釋）。
**門。**保羅在特羅亞的傳道顯然有所回應。用門來比喻機會，還出現在林前16:9（見啟3:8註釋）中。上帝的天意為保羅開了許多門，包括死裡逃生的門（見林後1:8-11）。在光明和黑暗，陽光和風雨中，保羅都看到上帝的手。他甚至看見上帝的手將他“肉體”的“刺”變為好事（參林後12:7）。基督徒用始終關注上帝在他道路上的天意安排──殷勤看守，耐心等待，樂意順從，感恩喜樂。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–13節）**。《使徒行述》第323頁。
12.en:
**Came to Troas.** Verses 12, 13 reveal Paul’s deep personal affection for the Corinthian believers and his unabated interest in their welfare. He had apparently dispatched Titus to Corinth to work for the restoration of harmony and to obtain a full report of conditions and of how the Corinthians received his letter of reproof (cf. AA 323). It seems that they had agreed to meet each other at Troas, but Titus had apparently been prevented from keeping that appointment. Anxiety overwhelmed Paul as he imagined that his worst fears about the Corinthian church had come true. This frame of mind made it impossible for him to labor effectively at Troas. Concerning the city of Troas and Paul’s previous visit there see on Acts 16:8–11. Paul again visited Troas on his return from Corinth, en route to Jerusalem (Acts 20:6–12), and also after his release from his first imprisonment at Rome (see on 2 Tim. 4:13).
**Christ’s gospel.** That is, the gospel that proceeds from Christ. Upon leaving Ephesus, Paul had intended to devote some considerable time to evangelistic labors at Troas.
**A door.** Apparently there was a ready response to Paul’s preaching at Troas. The figure of a door to represent opportunity appears elsewhere in 1 Cor. 16:9 (see on Rev. 3:8). Divine providence had opened many doors for Paul, including the door of escape from death (see 2 Cor. 1:8–10). Paul saw God’s hand in the light and in the darkness, in sunshine and in rain. He even saw God’s hand turning the “thorn” in his “flesh” to a good purpose (ch. 12:7). The Christian must ever be alert for the providence of God upon his pathway—earnestly watching, patiently waiting, promptly obeying, and thankfully rejoicing.

13.zh:
那時，因為沒有遇見兄弟提多，我心裡不安，便辭別那裡的人往馬其頓去了。

**不安。**保羅的憂慮一直延續到他在馬其頓遇見提多。他極為憂慮，以致不能留在特羅亞講道，儘管那裡的前景很光明。這證明保羅對他的信徒有著強烈的個人感情。聖經其他地方沒有記載保羅轉離一個“開了門”的地方。上帝最成功的工人也會受到強烈情緒的影響，在一段時間內不能繼續工作。當基督的工作在哥林多遇到危機的時候，保羅既不能安心，也無法集中精力做其他工作。
**往馬其頓去。**馬其頓在前往哥林多的路上，保羅希望在那裡比在特羅亞更早會見提多。
13.en:
**No rest.** Paul’s state of anxiety continued until he finally met Titus in Macedonia. So overwhelming was his anxiety that he could not tarry to preach in Troas, even though the prospects there were bright. Here is evidence of Paul’s intense personal interest in his converts. We have no other record of Paul’s turning away from “an open door.” The most successful worker for God is not always above deep emotion that may unsettle him and render it impossible for him to continue his work for a time. While crisis confronted the work of Christ at Corinth, Paul could neither rest nor concentrate his faculties on other activities.
**Into Macedonia.** Macedonia lay on the way to Corinth, and there Paul could expect to meet Titus sooner than at Troas.

14.zh:
感謝神！常帥領我們在基督裡誇勝，並藉著我們在各處顯揚那因認識基督而有的香氣。

**感謝上帝。**保羅到達馬其頓遇見提多，無法抑制的憂愁頓時化為無限的快樂。保羅從本節開始，長篇論述他自己的生活所體現福音事工的動機和屬靈能力。這是本書信直至林後7:4的主題。聖經中沒有其他章節如此逼真和深刻地描寫了基督真使者的內心經歷（見林後5:20）。
率領……誇勝。thriambeuo，“凱旋”，指慶祝勝利或率領凱旋的隊伍。保羅在西2:15中用了該動詞的這個意義。在紙莎草文獻中該詞也是這樣使用的。誇勝的不是保羅和他的同工。他們作為主耶穌基督的俘虜，在祂的率領下勝利地前進，走遍世界宣揚福音，成為祂戰勝黑暗權勢的活範例（西2:15）。
Thriambeuo一詞與thriambos有關係。Thriambos是指慶祝偉大軍事勝利的隊伍所唱的讚歌。著名的羅馬凱旋儀式就是羅馬元老院授予勝利的將軍，慶祝傑出軍事勝利的。凱旋的將軍在首都城門口受到政府官員的歡迎。凱旋的遊行開始了。走最前面的是一批官員，接著的元老院議員，後面是號手，作為勝利者的先導。然後是一長列滿載著戰利品的車輛，展示琳琅滿目的貴重珍稀之品。還有準備獻為祭的白色公牛和母牛。持香者四處揮舞著香，香氣飄溢於空氣中。從被征服地帶來的獅子、老虎、大象及其他珍禽異獸也出現在遊行隊伍裡。後面是戴著鐐銬的被俘的國王、王子，將領，及大批較低級別的戰俘。接著是偉大的征服者自己，站立華麗的戰車上，頭戴桂冠或是金冠冕。一隻手拿著象徵勝利的桂樹枝，一隻手拿著他的權杖。在他後面的是眾多跟隨他征戰的軍官，騎兵和步兵。每一個人都手持裝飾著桂枝的矛。隊伍在擁擠的大街，沿著聖路，經過凱旋門到達卡皮託利尼山（見462頁的地圖）。隊伍在那裡停下，有些俘虜被殘忍地處死，或被扔進監獄等待在羅馬大圓形劇場執行死刑。還有一些被視為可以赦免。將獲得釋放。祭牲要獻給羅馬諸神，慶祝勝利的宴會開始了。
保羅想像基督是偉大的勝利者，率領得勝的隊伍，帶著被征服者回來。保羅，他的同工和所有他們為基督所贏得的人，都是上帝凱旋大軍中的俘虜。保羅沒有說自己是上帝軍隊勝利的統帥，卻將一切榮耀都歸給上帝。保羅以自己為凱旋隊伍中上帝恩典的戰利品；這與他一貫的態度和觀念是一致的（見林前4:9,10；林後4:10；11:23；西1:24）。這裡他強調了上帝成功地使用他作為傳道者。上帝正率領他和他的同工勝利地前進。福音在各地都獲得了像在哥林多那樣的勝利。所有的真基督徒都是上帝的僕人（見羅6:16），是救贖主與罪惡作戰的戰利品。看到保羅作為一個俘虜被捆在基督的戰車上，就可以看出基督為墮落的人所能成就的。上帝正在帶領他前往世界各地，作為祂勝利大能和無比恩典的典範。最偉大的勝利就是靠著基督的能力戰勝罪惡。戰勝道德和屬靈的仇敵，遠比在戰場上戰勝敵軍輝煌（參箴16:32）。
**在各處。**指保羅所去過的地方。基督釘十字架後不到35年，福音就傳遍了地中海世界（見徒19:10,26,27；羅1:8；15:18,19）。
**認識。**原文該詞是“香氣”的同位語。認識基督就這樣成了保羅所說的香氣。這種屬靈的香氣藉著保羅和他同工的服務，藉著基督徒生活中所彰顯基督的義，這種屬靈的香氣在各處、在哥林多、實際上也在整個亞該亞的教會中顯揚。
**香氣。**是指持香者在遊行的途中所散發的香氣。團團香氣從路邊的祭壇上升，從香爐和敞開的殿宇中飄出。整座城市都充滿祭牲的煙，鮮花和薰香的香氣。保羅視自己為基督凱旋隊伍中的持香者。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–15節）**。《餘民教會》61頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–16節）**。《使徒行述》第326頁；《證言》卷六第316頁。
14.en:
**Thanks be unto God.** Irrepressible anxiety gives way to exuberant joy when Paul reaches Macedonia and meets Titus. Paul here begins a lengthy exposition on the motives and spiritual power of the gospel minister as exemplified in his own life. This is the theme of his letter through ch. 7:4. No passage in the Scriptures gives so earnest and impassioned a portrayal of the inner experience of a true ambassador for Christ (see ch. 5:20).
**Causeth … to triumph.** Gr. thriambeuō, “to triumph,” that is, to celebrate a triumph or to lead in a triumphal procession, the sense in which Paul uses this verb in Col. 2:15 and the sense in which it is always used in the papyri. The translation here should probably be “leads … in triumph.” It is not Paul and his co-workers who triumph, rather, they, as captives of the Lord Jesus Christ, are led by Him in triumphal procession as they go through the world proclaiming the gospel, living examples of His triumph over the powers of darkness (Col. 2:15).
Thriambeuō is related to thriambos, a hymn sung in connection with processions celebrating great military victories. The famous Roman triumph was conferred on successful generals by the Roman Senate, in celebration of some outstanding military victory or campaign. A victorious general was welcomed by government officials at the gates of the imperial city, where the triumphal march began. First came the Senators, preceded by a body of magistrates. After the Senators came trumpeters, heralding the approach of the victor. Then followed a long train of carts laden with the spoils of war. Articles of great value, rarity, or beauty were fully exposed to view. There were also white bulls and oxen destined for sacrifice. Here and there incense bearers waved their censers to and fro, perfuming the air. Lions, tigers, elephants, and other strange animals from the captive lands often appeared in the procession. After these came the captive kings, princes, or generals, and a long train of inferior captives, bound and fettered. Next came the great conqueror himself, standing in a splendid chariot. A crown of laurel or gold was upon his head. In one hand he held a branch of laurel, the emblem of victory, and in the other his truncheon or staff of authority. Following him marched many of those who had fought under him—officers, horse soldiers, foot soldiers—each holding aloft a spear adorned with laurel boughs. The procession moved on through the crowded streets, along the Via Sacra, through the Triumphal Arch to the Capitoline hill (see Paul at Rome). There it halted, and some of the captives were executed in cold blood or thrown into prison to await death in the Colosseum. Others, considered worthy of pardon, were set free. Animal sacrifices were offered to the Roman gods, and the triumphal feast began.
Paul envisions Christ as a great conqueror, leading the conquered in a triumphal procession. Paul, his co-workers, and all those won to Christ by them are captives in God’s great triumph. Paul does not speak of himself as the triumphant commander of God’s army, but gives God all the glory. For Paul to be led in triumph as a trophy of divine grace accords with his habitual attitude and feelings (see 1 Cor. 4:9, 10; 2 Cor. 4:10; 11:23; Col. 1:24). He here emphasizes God’s successful use of him as an evangelist. God is leading him and his fellow workers about in triumph. Everywhere the gospel was gaining such victories and triumphs as had been won in the Corinthian church. All true Christians are God’s slaves (see Rom. 6:16), trophies of the Redeemer’s victorious campaign against sin. To see Paul, a captive chained to the chariot of Christ, was to see what Christ could do for reprobate men. God was leading him up and down the world, an example of His conquering power and matchless grace. The grandest of all victories is the victory over sin through the power of Christ. He who conquers the moral and spiritual foes of the soul achieves a far grander triumph than he who conquers an opposing army upon the battlefield (cf. Prov. 16:32).
**The savour.** That is, fragrance scattered by the incense bearers along the route of the procession. Clouds of incense rose from wayside altars and were wafted from censers and from open temples. The entire city was filled with the smoke of sacrifices and the fragrance of flowers and incense. Paul thinks of himself as an incense bearer in the triumphal procession of Christ.
**Knowledge.** In the Greek this word stands in apposition to “savour.” Thus the knowledge of Christ becomes the fragrance of which Paul speaks. Through Paul’s ministry and that of his fellow workers, through the righteousness of Christ manifest in the lives of His followers, this spiritual savor is manifested in every place, in the church at Corinth, in fact, throughout Achaia.
**In every place.** That is, wherever Paul had been. Less than 35 years after the crucifixion the gospel had been extensively preached throughout the Mediterranean world (see Acts 19:10, 26, 27; Rom. 1:8; 15:18, 19).

15.zh:
因為我們在神面前，無論在得救的人身上或滅亡的人身上，都有基督馨香之氣。

**得救的。**得救的人靠的是基督的恩典。滅亡的人要為自己的淪喪負責。
現在回到羅馬凱旋儀式的比喻。一些遊行隊伍裡的人是要去接受死刑，其他人則要獲得釋放或慶祝勝利。兩等人在前進的路上都聞到了香氣，讓一等人想到了死，讓另一等人想到了生。福音也是這樣。對於接受的人，它是美好將來的保證，對於拒絕的人，它是死亡的警告。福音的傳播決不是要讓人保持在原來的狀態。它要麼引人進入永生，要麼使硬著心拒絕生命（見16節註釋）。或使人順從，或使人悖逆，或使人疏遠，或使人和好。福音並不改變。“在得救的人”，它始終是“上帝的大能”（羅1:16）。但拒絕福音的人要被福音定罪（見太7:21-27；可16:16；約3:17-21註釋）。基督來，要成為人生命中的房角石，但在拒絕的人，祂將變成了“絆腳的石頭”（彼前2:8）。
**馨香之氣。**Euōdia來自“好”和“氣味”兩個詞，指上帝所悅納的人或物（見弗5:2；腓4:18），在七十士譯本中指會幕中的香氣（見出29:18；利1:9；2:2等）。
保羅仍然想到在舉行凱旋儀式時羅馬街頭所瀰漫的香氣，只是對比喻稍作變動。林後2:14中的香氣指認識上帝的知識，藉著人間的代表傳播出去。在15節中，保羅和他的同工就是基督的香氣。基督是上帝傳播天上知識的主要媒介；保羅和他的同工是次要媒介。他們與基督聯為一體。祂住在他們中間（加2:20），藉著他們顯揚屬靈的香氣。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–17節）**。《證言》卷二第706頁。
15.en:
**Sweet savour.** Euōdia, from two words meaning “good” and “smell.” Euōdia is applied to persons or things well pleasing to God (see Eph. 5:2; Phil. 4:18). In the LXX it is used of the incense in the tabernacle (see Ex. 29:18; Lev. 1:9; 2:2; etc.).
Paul is still thinking of the aroma of incense in the streets of Rome during a triumph, but the figure changes slightly. In 2 Cor. 2:14 the odor represents the knowledge of God, diffused through human representatives. In v. 15 Paul and his fellow ministers constitute the odor of Christ. Christ is the primary medium through which God diffuses the knowledge that is from above; Paul and his fellow ministers are the secondary medium. They become one with Christ, who lives in them (Gal. 2:20) and manifests the fragrance of spiritual things through them.
**Are saved.** Literally, “are being saved.” Those who are being saved are saved by the grace of Christ; those who are lost are responsible for the loss of their own souls.
To return to the figure of the Roman triumph. Some who marched in the procession were on their way to execution, others to release or triumph. Both groups breathed the perfume as they marched along. To one it was a reminder of death, to the other a reminder of life. So it is with the gospel. To those who accept it, it becomes the pledge of a happy future, but to those who reject it, it becomes a warning of death. The preaching of the gospel never leaves a man in the same state in which it finds him. It either leads him on to eternal life or hardens him so that he rejects life (see on v. 16). It either subdues or hardens, alienates or reconciles. The gospel changes not, it is always the “power of God unto salvation” (Rom. 1:16), but those who reject it are condemned by it (see on Matt. 7:21–27; Mark 16:16; John 3:17–21). He who came to be the chief cornerstone of men’s lives becomes “a stone of stumbling” to those who reject Him (1 Peter 2:8).

16.zh:
在這等人，就作了死的香氣叫他死；在那等人，就作了活的香氣叫他活。這事誰能當得起呢？

**在這等人。**基督對拒絕祂意味著死；對接受祂的人意味著生。這是必然的，因為只有祂是生命的源泉。任何人一旦面對基督裡的真理，就必須作出選擇。《新約》中經常提到福音拯救和定罪兩種不同的功能（見約3:19；15:22；林前1:18,23,24）。太陽給種在好土裡的樹木帶來生命，也會使拔出來拋在地上的樹腐爛毀壞。陽光使蠟融化，也使泥土堅硬，其區別在於物質本身。人心也是如此。一些是柔軟的，一些卻是剛硬的，取決與他們個人對福音的反應。
誰能當得起呢？這是一個反問句。保羅意識到身上所負救靈職責的嚴肅性。這種責任感是他成功的重要因素，使他深切關心哥林多的事態（見13節註釋）。這種關懷出於對任務的重要性和靈魂價值的深刻認識。真正相信聖經的真理，尤其的涉及末日將近之真理的傳道人，對於淪喪的人決不會冷若冰霜。
傳福音的人要對自己的生活，所講的道，以及他的忠實宣講信息負責。上帝使者的職責超過其他任何職業。基督的使者只有成為他所傳信息的典範，在生活中不斷接觸他所代表的主，才能“當得起” “這事”。
16.en:
**To the one.** Christ is life or death to men as they accept or reject Him. This is inevitably so because He is the one and only source of life. Once confronted by truth as it is in Christ, no man can avoid making a decision. This contrast between the intended saving effect of the gospel and its opposite effect of condemnation is often alluded to in the NT (see John 3:19; 15:22; 1 Cor. 1:18, 23, 24). The sun, which imparts life to a tree that is planted in good soil, decomposes and destroys it if it is plucked up and exposed on the surface of the ground. Sunlight melts wax, but hardens clay. The difference is in the substances themselves. Even so with human hearts, some are melted, some hardened, depending on their individual response to the gospel.
**Who is sufficient?** The question is rhetorical. Paul senses the solemnity of the responsibility resting upon him for the salvation of men. This sense of responsibility was an important contributing factor to his success. It was this that had made him feel so deeply concerned over the state of affairs in Corinth (see on v. 13). This feeling of concern grows out of a deep sense of the importance of the task and of the value of souls. The minister who truly believes the truths of God’s Word, particularly those that have to do with the nearness of the end of time, cannot be indifferent toward lost men and women.
The minister of the gospel is responsible for how he lives, for what he preaches, and for the faithful delivery of his message. The responsibility of being an ambassador for God surpasses that of any other calling. Only as the ambassador for Christ is a living example of the message he proclaims, and as he lives in uninterrupted contact with the One whom he represents, can he expect to be “sufficient for these things.”

17.zh:
我們不像那許多人，為利混亂神的道；乃是由於誠實，由於神，在神面前憑著基督講道。

**許多人。**就是反對保羅的人。哥林多教會的不少信徒顯然認為“許多人”是不會錯的。他們唯一關心的是，哪一邊人多？
**混亂。**直譯是“零售商”，“小販”，“小商人”，“精明的商人”。該詞這樣翻譯常帶貶義，例如指經銷葡萄酒的人，在酒中摻水或其他劣質混合物，以謀取更高的利潤。該詞也用於文化含義。柏拉圖用它指根據自己的思維方式給真哲學摻假的哲學家
保羅現在說到那些在上帝的道中摻假行騙的人。哥林多的“許多人”就像不誠實的旅店老闆或獸酒商，用人的理論和遺傳混亂福音。根據啟17:2，背道的教會要讓地上的居民喝淫亂的酒，就是摻了假酒，即假道。假師傅們滿足於贗品，廉價的替代品，表面的順從，並企圖靠行為成義。他們銷售上帝的道為個人的利益。買方只需付出很少的個人犧牲。聖經經常提到這些推銷宗教的人所用的方法和教訓（賽50:11；林後10:12,13；11:13-15；提後4:3；彼後2:1-18）。
當一個人將上帝的道主要視為謀生的手段，削弱其精髓或嚴肅性，放鬆對基督徒的崇高要求，傳講自己，自己的聰明或學問時，他就是混亂上帝的道。他就是這樣使這道為他效勞，而不是他為這道效勞。
**誠實。**一個成功的傳道人知道是上帝差派了他，上帝會看見他，基督的靈在他裡面。真正的傳道人不追求個人的利益，沒有狡詐，偽善和卑鄙的動機，不追求名望。他必以基督為中心，傳上帝的道。
17.en:
**Many.** Literally, “the many,” that is, those who opposed Paul. Apparently a large number of church members in Corinth had concluded that “the many” could not be wrong. To them the only important question was, Which is the popular side?
**Which corrupt.** Literally, “retailers,” “peddlers,” “hucksters,” “sharp dealers.” The word thus translated is always used in an uncomplimentary sense. It was used, for instance, of a retailer of wine, or vintner, who adulterated his wine by adding either water or some other inferior mixture, in order to make a greater profit. It came also to be used in an intellectual sense. Plato thus refers to philosophers who, according to his way of thinking, adulterated true philosophy.
Paul now speaks of those who adulterate, or deal deceitfully with, the Word of God. “The many” at Corinth were like dishonest tavernkeepers and wine peddlers, dispensing a gospel corrupted with human theories and traditions. According to Rev. 17:2 the apostate church makes the inhabitants of the earth drunk with the wine of her fornication, that is, the wine of adulterated, false doctrines. False teachers are content with a counterfeit, with a cheap substitute, with superficial obedience, with trying to achieve righteousness by works. They sell the Word for personal profit, at a low price of personal sacrifice on the part of the buyer. The methods and teachings of such hucksters of religion are often alluded to in Scripture (Isa. 50:11; 2 Cor. 10:12, 13; 11:13–15; 2 Tim. 4:3; 2 Peter 2:1–18).
A man corrupts the Word of God when he considers it primarily as a means of making a livelihood, when he tempers either its goodness or its severity, when he eases the high requirements it makes of Christians, or when he preaches himself, his cleverness, or his own learning. Thus he makes the Word minister to him, instead of ministering the Word.
**As of sincerity.** The successful minister of the gospel is conscious that God has sent him, conscious that God sees him, conscious of the spirit of Christ within him. The true preacher will be free from all self-seeking, all duplicity and hypocrisy, all sordid motives, all cravings for popularity and fame. He will preach the Word, with Christ as its center.

1.zh:
我們既然蒙憐憫，受了這職分，就不喪膽，

**這職分。**指“新約”的職分。人們因此而擺脫律法“字句”的捆綁（見林後3:6,17註釋），將律法的原則刻在心版上（第3節）。這“屬靈”的職分（6節），因信“稱義”的職分（9節），“新約”的職分（6節），真正“自由”的職分（17節），幫助信徒恢復基督的樣式。這榮耀的職分一直支持著信徒和使者們經歷一切試煉和患難，更促進了上帝的榮耀。
**喪膽。**egkakeo，“疲倦”，“灰心”，“喪志”。保羅十分相信自己信息的真實性和價值。上帝曾大大祝福他的工作。他自己是完全不配的。他曾是一個迫害者和褻瀆者。他視自己是罪人中的“罪魁”（提前1:15），但他“蒙了憐憫”。他將自己傳福音的職分完全歸功於上帝的恩典（林前7:25；15:9,10；加1:15,16；提前1:12-16）。沒有什麼比誠實地回顧自己的生活更能使人放棄驕傲、狂妄和自負。保羅的悔改和從事福音聖工是出於上帝的恩典（提前1:13,14）。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–6節）**。《使徒行述》第329頁；《基督教育原理》第476頁。
1.en:
**This ministry.** That is, the ministry of the “new testament,” by which men are freed from bondage to the “letter” of the law (see on ch. 3:6, 17), and have its principles engraved on the heart (v. 3). This ministry of the “spirit” (v. 6), of “righteousness” by faith (v. 9), of the “new testament” (v. 6), of true “liberty” (v. 17), restores the believer to the likeness of Christ. This glorious ministry ever sustains its adherents and its ambassadors through every trial and every suffering, and even these redound to the glory of God.
**Faint.** Gr. egkakeō, “to be weary,” “to lose courage,” “to lose heart.” Paul had supreme confidence in the integrity and value of his message, and God had greatly blessed his ministry. He was altogether unworthy. He had been a persecutor and a blasphemer. He considered himself the “chief” of all sinners (1 Tim. 1:15). But he had “received mercy.” He owed his ordination as a minister of the gospel entirely to the grace of God (1 Cor. 7:25; 15:9, 10; Gal. 1:15, 16; 1 Tim. 1:12–16). Nothing subdues pride, conceit, and self-confidence like an honest retrospect of one’s own life. Paul’s conversion and commission to the gospel ministry were due to divine favor (1 Tim. 1:13, 14).

2.zh:
乃將那些闇昧可恥的事棄絕了；不行詭詐，不謬講神的道理，只將真理表明出來，好在神面前把自己薦與各人的良心。

**可恥的事。**aischune。基督徒的職分要求生活和品格光明磊落。人們什麼時候懷疑領袖的生活有什麼經不起仔細審查的事，他的工作就結束了。對真執事的第一項條件就是完全拋棄所有可能給上帝的聖工帶來羞恥的事。真宗教是光明之路，而非黑暗之路（見羅13:12；林前4:5；弗5:8；參約壹1:5），因為它不僅涉及每一行動，更涉及每一動機。
**棄絕。**保羅在悔改的時候，棄絕了一切與他的新信仰不一致的做法。他在接受福音執事的使命時，棄絕了反對他的人所隨便使用的一切錯誤的方法。
**不行詭詐。**即沒有欺騙。保羅決心表裡如一（參路20:23）。反對他的人為達目的可以採用一切欺騙的手段。
**謬講。**保羅宣講完整的真理絕不摻假。給上帝的道摻假包括：將個人的觀點說成是有聖經依據的，斷章取義，用人的遺傳代替“耶和華如此說”，曲解聖經明白的意思為犯罪找藉口，用神秘或象徵性的方式解釋聖經直接的教訓以削弱其力量，或把真理與謬論混合起來（見林後11:3；12:16；弗4:14；帖前2:3,4）。
**表明。**該詞在這封書信中以一種或另一種形式多次出現（2:14；3:3；4:10；5:11；11:6等），是隱瞞或狡猾的反義詞。真理只要求簡單明瞭的講述。傳道人或自稱為基督徒的人決不可使這種明顯的真理晦澀不明。
**在上帝面前。**上帝知道保羅內心的真誠。保羅似乎在呼籲上帝為他現在所寫的真理作證。
**把自己薦與。**哥林多的反對者稱保羅的假使徒（見林後3:1註釋）。現在保羅為自己的使徒身份辯護，通過展示他生活和傳道工作的某些方面，以向他們舉薦自己是一個真使徒。
**良心。**有關保羅重視清潔的良心，見徒23:1註釋。保羅認為每一個人都有道德判斷的能力和與生俱來對道德律法的認識（見羅2:13-15）。領受保羅所“表現”的真理，不僅需要人的理智，也需要人的良知（參約8:9；羅2:15）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第331頁；《證言》卷一第337頁。
2.en:
**Have renounced.** Literally, “have renounced [once for all].” At conversion Paul had renounced every practice that was inconsistent with his new-found faith, and upon receiving his commission as a gospel minister he had renounced questionable methods such as his opponents felt free to use.
**Dishonesty.** Gr. aischunē, “shameful [things].” The Christian ministry demands transparency of life and character. The moment men begin to suspect that there are things in a leader’s life that will not bear scrutiny, his work is over. The first requirement of a true minister is that he renounce completely all things that might bring shame to the cause of God. True religion is a way of light and never of darkness (see Rom. 13:12; 1 Cor. 4:5; Eph. 5:8; cf. 1 John 1:5), for it is concerned, not only with every act, but even more, with the motive that prompts the act.
**Not walking in craftiness.** That is, not practicing deception. Paul aspired to be what he appeared to be (cf. Luke 20:23). His opponents would resort to any deception in order to secure their objectives.
**Deceitfully.** Paul proclaimed the whole truth without adulterating it. Adulteration of the Word of God consists of preaching personal opinions as if they had the sanction of Scripture, of removing texts from their context, of substituting human traditions for a “Thus saith the Lord,” of explaining away the plain meaning of Scripture in order to excuse sin, of interpreting its literal teachings in a mystical or symbolic way so as to vitiate their force, or of presenting an admixture of error with truth (see 2 Cor. 11:3; 12:16; Eph. 4:14; 1 Thess. 2:3, 4).
**Manifestation.** In one form or another the word “manifest” appears repeatedly in this epistle (chs. 2:14; 3:3; 4:10; 5:11; 11:6; etc.). It stands for the opposite of concealment and craftiness. All that truth requires is a simple, clear statement. Nothing in the minister or the professed Christian must be allowed to obscure this open manifestation.
**Commending ourselves.** Opponents at Corinth have branded Paul a false apostle (see on ch. 3:1). He now proceeds to defend his apostleship by setting forth certain aspects of his life and ministry that should commend him to them as a genuine apostle.
**Conscience.** For the importance Paul attached to a clear conscience see on Acts 23:1. Paul credits every man with the capacity for moral judgment and for an inborn knowledge of the moral law (see Rom. 2:13–15). Paul’s “manifestation” of the truth appealed not only to men’s intellect, but also to their conscience (cf. John 8:9; Rom. 2:15).
**In the sight of God.** God knows the integrity of Paul’s heart, and Paul, as it were, calls God to testify to the truth of what he now writes.

3.zh:
如果我們的福音矇蔽，就是矇蔽在滅亡的人身上。

**矇蔽。**或“遮蓋”，“隱藏”。保羅這裡指第3章中的“帕子”（見13-16節）。保羅時代的情形與摩西的時代一樣，對許多人而言，真理依然是矇蔽的。這不是因為福音本身不明確，而是因聽福音之人的思想態度。
**滅亡的人。**保羅無疑想到哥林多少數堅持隨從他們中間假師傅的人。他們有可能悔改。但是隻要福音對他們依然矇蔽，他們就仍處在滅亡之中。對他們而言，只有“帕子”除去，才能得救（見太18:11；路15:4,6,24,31,32；19:10）。
人不能為自己提供光明，但能因閉目不看光明而使自己陷於黑暗之中了。太陽不論多麼明亮，瞎子還是看不到它的光明。保羅講到那些因內心的黑暗而拒絕福音亮光的人。他們自己得為此而負責（見何4:6註釋）。有些情況會矇蔽福音拯救的大能。如在哥林多教會，有些人生活中所表顯的結黨精神、敵對，爭競，淫亂，驕傲和自私，對他們矇蔽了福音。明朗的福音必須由開明的心靈來領受（約8:47；約壹4:6）。
對屬靈事物的冷漠和非屬靈思想的先入之見也象帕子一樣（見路21:34；見太6:24-34註釋）。地上合法的職業可能使人全神貫注，以致沒有時間也沒有願望追求屬天的亮光。人們拒絕真理不是因為缺乏證據。他們可能確信成千件證據少得多的事。他們拒絕真理是因為真理譴責了他們，責備了他們的罪惡，使他們良心不安。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–4節）**。《基督比喻實訓》第106頁；《證言》卷一第338頁；《證言》卷四第586頁。
3.en:
**Be hid.** Or, “be veiled,” or “remains veiled.” Paul here alludes to the “vail” of ch. 3 (see vs. 13–16). In Paul’s day the situation was the same as it had been in the days of Moses—for many, truth still remained hidden. This situation was not due to lack of clearness in the gospel itself, but to the attitude of the minds and hearts to which it was addressed.
**Are lost.** Literally, “are being lost.” Paul is thinking, no doubt, of the Corinthian minority that persists in following the false apostles among them. They may yet repent, but so long as the gospel remains veiled to them, they remain in a lost condition. For them, salvation will be possible when the “vail” is removed (see Matt. 18:11; Luke 15:4, 6, 24, 31, 32; 19:10).
Man cannot provide himself with light, but he can make darkness for himself by closing his eyes to the light. However bright the sun, its beams are veiled to the blind. Paul speaks of those who refused the light of the gospel because of inward darkness for which they themselves were responsible (see on Hosea 4:6). Certain conditions may veil the saving power of the gospel. In the Corinthian church, for instance, party spirit, rivalry, contention, immorality, pride, and selfishness in the lives of some hid the gospel from them. The open gospel must be met by open minds and hearts (John 8:47; 1 John 4:6).
Indifference to spiritual things and preoccupation with nonspiritual things also draw the veil (see Luke 21:34; see on Matt. 6:24–34). Legitimate earthly occupations may swallow up a man until he has neither time nor the desire for heavenly light. Men do not reject the truth because of lack of evidence. They may, indeed, believe a thousand things on the basis of far less evidence. They reject the truth because it condemns them; it reproves their sins and disturbs their conscience.

4.zh:
此等不信之人被這世界的神弄瞎了心眼，不叫基督榮耀福音的光照著他們。基督本是神的像。

**不信。**屬靈的盲目不只是撒但的責任，也是那些選擇“不信”之人的責任。他們已經被帶到上帝真理的亮光面前，但他們心靈的反應是盲目而消極的。他們不重視基督教信仰最基本的道理。但他們要為自己負責，因為他們故意轉離真理。他們有眼睛卻看不見（賽6:9；太13:14,15；約12:40；羅11:8-10）。他們看不出主的僕人有什麼佳形美容值得他們羨慕（賽53:2）。
**這世界的神。**就是撒但。保羅在這裡解釋為什麼榮耀的福音對許多人是矇蔽的。撒但是有位格的（見太4:1註釋）。他不論以什麼形式或通過什麼媒介出現，我們都必須識破。“這世界的神”這個稱呼暗示撒但企圖篡奪上帝對這個世界的主權。魔鬼自稱是這個世界的神（太4:8,9；約壹5:19）。他曾是地上許多偉大王國和帝國看不見的統治者。他被稱為“這世界的神”是因為他的目的就是完全控制這個世界及其居民。他是“這世界的神”，因為世界大部分都在他的控制之下。他在世界大多數居民的心中掌權（參弗2:1,2）。世界服從他的命令，屈從他的誘惑，參與他的陰謀詭計。他是所有罪惡的創始者和策動者，是罪惡的化身。頑梗的罪人要交給撒但（林前5:5；參提前1:20）。他是“這世界的神”，因為他在一定程度上控制了海、陸、空中自然的力量。
說撒但是“這世界的神”，並不意味著上帝已放棄了世界的主權。撒但的能力和控制權是受嚴格限制的。只有在全智上帝許可的範圍裡，撒但才可以在罪惡永遠而有效地消滅之前運用他的權力（林前15:24-28；啟12:12）。
**心眼。**noēmata，“洞察力”。基督和撒但在爭奪人心（羅7:23,25；12:2；林後3:14；11:3；腓2:5；4:7,8）。撒但的主要工作就是矇蔽或弄瞎人的心眼。為此他叫人不學習上帝的道，過度消耗體力精力，使人心緒混亂，用今生的事物充滿人的心，使人追求驕傲和自高。
**光。**phōtismos，“光照”，“啟發”，源於一個表示“發光”，“照亮”的動詞。參表示“光”的常用詞phōs（見約1:7,9註釋）。Phōtismos在這裡指福音，要照亮每一顆真誠敞開的心。但許多人雖然有充足的福音亮光照耀在他們黑暗的心靈上，他們依然是盲目的。他們就像在黑暗的房間裡的人故意將光明拒之門外。他們使福音的光不能上升到他們生活的高空（見箴4:18）。
這是光明與黑暗之爭。撒但最多隻能弄瞎人的心眼。他不能遮暗福音的亮光，卻能把人心包圍在黑暗之中。即使福音照亮周圍所有的人，他也能讓帕子矇住他們的眼睛。
撒但的國度是黑暗的國度（見賽60:2；太8:12；路22:53；彼後2:4；猶6；啟16:10），因此魔鬼仇恨福音的亮光。他希望有其他東西代替福音發光，如知識，文化，道德，教育，財富以及人的智慧。他全力以赴地阻撓福音真光的傳播。只有福音的真光才能拯救人類（徒4:12）。只有福音才能揭露撒但的陰謀詭計，使人看見從黑暗到光明的道路。見約1:4,5,9,14註釋。
**照著。**保羅在這裡是指福音救恩知識的亮光透入人的心中。
**像。**eikōn，“形象”。 創1:26的七十士譯本用了該詞。該詞還出現在林前11:7；西1:15；3:10；來10:1中。基督是聖父的真像，因為兩者在品格、特徵和完美方面都是一樣的。父上帝與耶穌相象（約12:45；14:9；腓2:6）。亞當和夏娃原來也是照著上帝的形像造的。救贖計劃的目的就是在人身上恢復上帝的形像。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給管家的勉言》第209頁；《歷代願望》第19頁；《佈道論》第610頁；《善惡之爭》第508頁；《先知與君王》第682頁；《先祖與先知》第67，442頁；《證言》卷一第476頁；《證言》卷二第397頁；《證言》卷三第250頁；《證言》卷四第44頁；《證言》卷五第742頁。
4.en:
**God of this world.** That is, Satan. Paul here explains why the glorious gospel is veiled to many men. Satan is a personal being (see on Matt. 4:1), and it is imperative that we recognize him when he comes in any form or through any medium. The title “god of this world” alludes to Satan’s attempt to usurp God’s sovereignty over this world. The devil claims to be the god of this world (Matt. 4:8, 9; 1 John 5:19). He has been the invisible ruler of many of the great kingdoms and empires of earth. He is called “the god of this world” because it is his purpose to secure complete control of this world and its inhabitants. He is “the god of this world” because the world is largely under his control. He rules in the hearts of most of its inhabitants (cf. Eph. 2:1, 2). The world obeys his dictates, yields to his temptations, takes part in his wicked ways and abominations. He is the author and instigator of all sin, and the very embodiment of it. Willful sinners are said to be given over to Satan (1 Cor. 5:5; cf. 1 Tim. 1:20). He is the “god of this world” because of his control, even though limited, of the forces of nature, the elements of earth, sea, and sky.
To speak of Satan as “god of this world” does not mean that God has abdicated sovereignty over the world. Satan’s power and control are strictly limited. He exercises what power he has only by permission of an all-wise God, and only so long as may be necessary for the effective and eternal destruction of sin (1 Cor. 15:24–28; Rev. 12:12).
**Minds.** Gr. noēmata, “perceptive faculties.” The battle between Christ and Satan is a battle for the minds of men (Rom. 7:23, 25; 12:2; 2 Cor. 3:14; 11:3; Phil. 2:5; 4:7, 8). Satan’s principal work is to blind or darken men’s minds. He does this by keeping them from the study of God’s Word, by deranging the powers of the mind through excesses of body and soul, by wholly occupying the mind with things of this life, and by appealing to pride and self-exaltation.
**Believe not.** The responsibility for spiritual blindness rests not only with Satan but also with those who choose to “believe not.” They have been brought to the light of God’s truth, yet their mental and spiritual reactions are blind and negative. The great fundamental doctrines of the Christian faith appear to them to have no value. But they themselves are responsible, for they have knowingly turned away from the truth. They have eyes but see not (Isa. 6:9; Matt. 13:14, 15; John 12:40; Rom. 11:8–10). They see no beauty in the Lord’s Servant, that they should desire Him (Isa. 53:2).
**Light.** Gr. phōtismos, “enlightenment,” “illumination,” from a verb meaning “to give light,” “to illuminate.” Compare phōs, the usual word for “light” (see on John 1:7, 9). Phōtismos is here used of the gospel, which will enlighten every sincere and open mind. Many, nevertheless, remain blind, even when the full light of the gospel shines into their darkened minds. They are like men in a dark room who deliberately keep out the light. They keep the light of the gospel from rising and ascending to the zenith of their lives (see Prov. 4:18).
The issue is one between light and darkness. The most that Satan can do is to blind the minds of men. He cannot darken the light of the gospel; but he can envelop human minds in darkness. He can cause a veil to cover their eyes, even though the gospel enlightens others all around them.
Satan’s kingdom is the kingdom of darkness (see Isa. 60:2; Matt. 8:12; Luke 22:53; 2 Peter 2:4; Jude 6; Rev. 16:10), and it is for this reason that the devil hates the light of the gospel. He is willing that the light of any substitute for the gospel should shine—the light of knowledge, of culture, of morality, of education, of wealth, and of human wisdom. But his whole effort is turned against the spread of the gospel light, which alone can save men (Acts 4:12). The gospel is the only means by which Satan’s diabolical schemes and deceptions can be exposed, and by which men can see the way from darkness to light. See on John 1:4, 5, 9, 14.
**Image.** Gr. eikōn, “image,” “figure,” “likeness.” This word is used in the LXX of Gen. 1:26, and also in 1 Cor. 11:7; Col. 1:15; 3:10; Heb. 10:1. Christ is the express image of the Father, in that the character, attributes, and perfection of both are the same. God the Father is like Jesus (John 12:45; 14:9; Phil. 2:6). Adam and Eve were originally made in that image, and it is the objective of the plan of salvation to restore that image in mankind.
**Should shine.** Paul here refers to the penetration of the human soul by the light of the saving knowledge of the gospel.

5.zh:
我們原不是傳自己，乃是傳基督耶穌為主，並且自己因耶穌作你們的僕人。

**我們原不是傳自己。**有人指控保羅傳道以自我為中心。他堅決駁斥這一指控。人若以自私的利益為動機，追求人的稱讚，企圖展示自己的才能，宣揚自己的觀點和遺傳，以及人的教訓，與上帝的道相反，為利益，生計，聲望和名譽而傳道時，他們就會傳自己。
**基督耶穌為主。**見太1:1；約1:38註釋。傳基督就是傳永遠的福音。
**僕人。**douloi，“奴隸”。保羅在其他地方稱自己是基督的僕人（羅1:1；腓1:1；參太20:28）。所以他無權轄制上帝的產業。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–6節）**。《使徒行述》第208頁；《證言》卷三第31頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–7節）**。《餘民教會》61頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–10節）**。《證言》卷二第550頁。
5.en:
**We preach.** Paul had been charged with being self-centered in his preaching, but he flatly repudiates the charge. Men preach themselves when they are motivated by self-interest, when they seek the applause of men, when they are ambitious to display their own talents, when they proclaim their own opinions and the traditions and teachings of men in preference for, and in contradiction to, the Word of God, and when they are motivated to preach for gain, for a livelihood, or for prestige and popularity.
**Christ Jesus the Lord.** See on Matt. 1:1; John 1:38. To preach Christ means to preach the everlasting gospel.
**Servants.** Gr. douloi, “slaves,” “bond servants.” Elsewhere, Paul speaks of himself as a servant of Christ (Rom. 1:1; Phil. 1:1; cf. Matt. 20:28), and as such he has no right to lord it over God’s heritage.

6.zh:
那吩咐光從黑暗裡照出來的神，已經照在我們心裡，叫我們得知神榮耀的光顯在耶穌基督的面上。

**吩咐光。**上帝用一道命令使光產生（見創1:3；詩33:6,9註釋）。聖經最初的記載是在完全黑暗之處出現了光（創1:2）。上帝不僅創造了自然界的光，還差遣祂的兒子成為“世界的光”（約8:12）。所有體力，智力，道德和屬靈的光都是從眾光之父而來的（雅1:17）。祂“披上亮光，如披外袍”（詩104:2）。上帝的本性就是光（雅1:17；參約1:4,5）。見約1:4,5,9,14註釋。
**照。**lampo，創造太陽照亮世界最初黑暗的主，也用真理的光照亮黑暗的心（詩119:105）。正如上帝口中所說的話給黑暗的世界帶來光明，聖經所展示的生命之道，命令天上的光照入黑暗的心靈。這光遠非人的能力、技術和智慧所能產生。
原文動詞的形式暗示，保羅可能指他過去悔改的特別經歷。那時他看見基督榮耀的形象。基督面上的光照耀他。後來有鱗片從他的眼睛和心頭掉了下去（徒9:3-18）。這是基督第一次作為救主和上帝向他顯現。他成為一個改變了的人。他心靈中的黑暗被驅散了（徒9:17,18；26:16-18）。
叫……光。根據本段的原文結構，上帝將光照入人心是為了給人帶來光明，使他們認識上帝的榮耀，其目的就是讓他們得救。
**在耶穌基督的面上。**摩西臉上反映的榮光不久前顯在基督臉上（見太17:2；路2:48；約1:14；彼後1:17,18註釋）。基督是祂父榮耀的完全展示，是一切神聖美德的化身。其他所有的啟示都是部分或不完全的。人在基督面上能看見上帝純潔完美的榮光。
保羅承認上帝創造和律法中的榮耀，但他現在看到耶穌基督面上和身上上帝榮耀的完美表現。他的心因此而感服，並決定終身事奉。人只有在耶穌基督裡並藉著祂才能與上帝的性情，就是上帝的榮耀有份。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第149，415，421頁；《歷代願望》第19，282，464頁；《教育論》第22，28，30頁；《佈道論》第284頁；《服務真詮》第464頁；《先知與君王》第717頁；《證言》卷八第46，256，322頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（6–10節）**。《使徒行述》第510頁；《早期著作》第28頁；《救贖的故事》第317頁。
6.en:
**Commanded the light.** God spoke the light into existence by a single command (see on Gen. 1:3; Ps. 33:6, 9). His first recorded words brought forth light where there had been only darkness (Gen. 1:2). Not only did God create natural light, He sent His Son to be “the light of the world” (John 8:12). All physical, intellectual, moral, and spiritual light have their origin in the Father of light (James 1:17). He clothed Himself “with light as with a garment” (Ps. 104:2). By very nature God is light (James 1:17; cf. John 1:4, 5). See on John 1:4, 5, 9, 14.
**Shined.** Gr. lampō, “to shine.” The very One who created the sun to illuminate the primeval darkness of this world also provides the light of truth to enlighten benighted minds (Ps. 119:105). As the spoken word of God brought light to a dark world, the living Word, as set forth in the written Word, commands the light of heaven to shine into darkened souls. It is beyond the power, skill, and wisdom of man to produce such light.
The form of the verb in Greek suggests that Paul may refer to a particular experience in the past—his own conversion. Paul then beheld Christ in His glorified form, and light from the face of Christ shone upon him. Later, the scales fell from his eyes and from his mind (Acts 9:3–18). For the first time Christ appeared to him as He truly was, Saviour and Lord, and he became a transformed man. The darkness of his own soul and mind was dispelled (Acts 9:17, 18; 26:16–18).
**To give the light.** According to the Greek construction of this passage, the purpose of God’s shining into men’s hearts is to give light, the purpose of the light is to acquaint them with the knowledge of the divine glory, and the purpose of the knowledge of the divine glory is to save them.
**In the face.** The same glory that had been reflected on the face of Moses had more recently been seen on the face of Christ (see on Matt. 17:2; Luke 2:48; John 1:14; 2 Peter 1:17, 18). Christ is the complete revelation of His Father’s glory, the incarnation of every divine excellence. All other revelations have either been partial or imperfect. In the face of Jesus Christ men may see the whole, pure, perfect light of God.
Paul acknowledged God’s glory in creation and in the law, but now he perceived the perfect exhibition of divine glory in the face and person of Jesus Christ. This is what won his heart and lifelong devotion. It is only in and through Jesus Christ that man becomes a partaker of the divine nature, and thus of the divine glory.

7.zh:
我們有這寶貝放在瓦器裡，要顯明這莫大的能力是出於神，不是出於我們。

**這寶貝。**就是“得知上帝榮耀的光現在耶穌基督的面上”（第6節）。保羅在7-18節中敘述了這種認識如何給他帶來力量，作上帝的“奴僕”，忍受了他傳道過程中幾乎無法克服的困難。要不是這種認識和能力，軟弱人性的器皿就要崩潰（見第1節）。
**瓦器。**ostrakinoi，原指用貝殼或烘過的泥製作的容器。這種器皿脆弱易碎，也不美觀，只有簡單的用途，沒有什麼價值。這裡將人的器皿與上帝永恆的寶貝進行對比。但上帝的計劃是讓這軟弱的瓦器容納和保存最大的寶貝。傳道人和信徒要被稱為瓦器，其崇高的目的是為了容納上帝偉大的寶貝。保羅也有可能想到了古時為了安全而把財寶藏在大瓦罐裡的做法。
人只是存放珠寶的盒子。這珠寶就是基督的義，是賜給每一位信徒的（見太13:45,46註釋）。人自己是一無所有的，直到他被天上的財寶所充實。基督所救贖的人都擁有這種財寶。有的人多一些，有的人少一些，根據各人憑著信心對它的領受。對於穿越沙漠的人，水是最寶貴的；對於生活在黑暗中的人，光明是最寶貴的；對於面臨死亡的人，生命是最寶貴的。對於必死的人類，福音的寶貝就是生命之水，世界之光，永遠的生命。
**出於上帝。**人喜歡用貴重的器皿存放自己的財寶。但上帝在實施祂計劃的時候，往往揀選最卑微的人，免得他們歸功於自己（林前1:28,29）。人把拯救自己或同胞的功勞歸於自己並沒有什麼好處。對於傳道人或信徒的生命來說，沒有什麼比驕傲更大的障礙了。重要的不是器皿本身，而是器皿中所裝的東西。傳道人和他的信息也是如此。上帝原可委託天使去做祂交託給軟弱人類的工作。但祂沒有這樣做，為了證明救贖的工作不是出於人，而是出於祂自己。器皿或工具本身並沒有什麼價值（參提後2:19,20）。只有上帝的臨格和能力才能確定其價值。哪裡有人因強調人的智慧，能力或口才而矇蔽了上帝的工作，哪裡福音的傳播就受到阻礙。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第297頁；《給傳道人的證言》第54，154，404頁；《證言》卷四第529頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–10節）**。《使徒行述》第330頁。
7.en:
**This treasure.** That is, “the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (v. 6). In vs. 7–18 Paul dwells on the way in which this knowledge has given him the power to endure, as a “slave” of God, the almost insuperable difficulties that have confronted him in his ministry. Except for this knowledge and power the weak human vessel would have collapsed (see v. 1).
**Earthen vessels.** Gr. ostrakinoi, originally, hollow receptacles made of shell or of baked clay. Such utensils were frail and fragile, unimposing, of brief usefulness, and of little value. Such is the human vessel in contrast with the eternal treasure of God. Yet it is God’s plan to make this weak vessel the recipient and retainer of the greatest of treasures. The minister and the believer are declared to be but earthen jars for the supreme purpose of containing God’s great treasure. Perhaps Paul is thinking of the ancient practice of storing treasure in great earthen jars for safekeeping.
Man is but the casket that contains the jewel of Christ’s righteousness, which is imputed and imparted to every believer (see on Matt. 13:45, 46). By himself, man is in a state of abject poverty. He remains in that state until he is enriched by this heavenly treasure. All who are redeemed by Christ have this treasure, some more than others, according to their own reception of it by faith. To those crossing the desert, water is of supreme value. To those living in darkness, light is of supreme value. To those facing death, life is of supreme value. To mortal man, the gospel treasure is all of these—living water, the light of the world, eternal life.
**Of God.** Men would be inclined to use valuable containers for storing their treasures. But in the working out of His plan God often chooses the humblest of men, lest they take credit to themselves (1 Cor. 1:28, 29). It is not for man’s good that he should receive credit for saving himself or his fellow men. There is no greater hindrance to the life of the minister or the believer than pride. It is not the containers, but their contents, that are important; thus with the minister and his message. God might have commissioned angels to do the work He has committed to frail men, but in doing so He works in such a way as to make it evident that the work of redemption is of God and not of man. The vessel or instrument has no value of itself (cf. 2 Tim. 2:19, 20); His presence and power alone determine its value. The spread of the gospel is always hindered where men obscure the work of God by emphasis upon human wisdom, ability, or eloquence.

8.zh:
我們四面受敵，卻不被困住；心裡作難，卻不至失望；

**四面受敵。**8-10節有四組對比。一方面說明瓦器的脆弱，另一方面說明無論容器如何脆弱，上帝大能的優越性。見林後1:4註釋。每一個基督徒，特別是傳道人，都在參加一場大戰，就是基督和撒但之間曠日持久的戰爭（弗6:10-17；啟12:7-12,17）。所以他無法躲避試煉和患難（約16:33；徒14:22；啟7:14）。然而在患難苦楚中伴隨著脆弱之人的成功，表明了上帝大能的存在（羅6:35-39）。因此沒有人能誇口，“只誇我們主耶穌基督的十字架”（加6:14）。靠著上帝的恩典得勝的人，能最明顯最有效地顯示基督。
**卻不被困住。**保羅不屈不撓的精神，鼓舞了無數基督的使者，在變幻莫測，失望困苦，迫害死亡的環境中，成為忠誠，勇敢，無畏的人。環境不能決定基督徒的心情。他忍耐是因為看到了那不能看見的主，並得到上帝恩典亮光的支持（見來11:27）。
**作難。**exaporeo，“處於疑惑之中”。在人看來，保羅經常走到山窮水盡的地步。但他在這樣的環境中學會了信靠等候上帝。
**失望。**exaporeo，“絕望”，“不知所措”。不論環境多麼惡劣，保羅已從經驗中學會信靠上帝尋找出路。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–9節）**。《使徒行述》第296頁。
8.en:
**Troubled on every side.** Verses 8–10 contain four pairs of contrasts. On the one side they illustrate the frailty of the earthen vessel, and on the other the excellency of the power of God despite this frailty. See on ch. 1:4. Every Christian, and particularly the Christian minister, finds himself in the midst of a great battle, the age-long warfare between Christ and Satan (Eph. 6:10–17; Rev. 12:7–12, 17). Consequently, he cannot escape trial and tribulation (John 16:33; Acts 14:22; Rev. 7:14). Yet the success that attends the efforts of the frail human instrument in the midst of tribulation and distress demonstrates the presence of divine power (Rom. 8:35–39). Therefore no man may “glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ” (Gal. 6:14). The clearest and most effective revelation of Christ is made in and through men and women who triumph by God’s grace.
**Yet not distressed.** The buoyancy of Paul’s indomitable spirit has inspired countless thousands of ambassadors for Christ to be loyal, brave, and courageous in the midst of uncertainty, disappointment, difficulty, persecution, and death. Circumstances do not determine the climate of the Christian soul. He endures because he sees his invisible Lord, and is sustained by the light of divine grace (see Heb. 11:27).
**Perplexed.** Gr. aporeō, “to be in doubt.” Paul had often found himself in situations where, from a human point of view, there was no way out. But he had learned, under such circumstances, to trust God and wait.
**In despair.** Gr. exaporeō, “to be in despair,” “to be utterly at a loss [to know what to do].” However forbidding the circumstances, Paul had learned by experience to trust God for a solution.

9.zh:
遭逼迫，卻不被丟棄；打倒了，卻不至死亡。

**遭逼迫。**見太5:10-12；10:17-23；約15:20註釋。一個接一個的對比都更加充分地顯示了患難和個人危險的嚴峻。保羅說到被敵對的勢力包圍，追逐，抓獲和打倒，似乎山窮水盡，必死無疑。
**卻不被丟棄。**保羅和他的同工在一切試煉中體驗了基督應許的實現，在生死關頭找到了逃生之路（見林前10:13；帖後1:4；來2:18；13:5）。對於處在試煉和迫害中的基督徒來說，一些上帝的真理是非常明顯的。他們無論遭遇多大的試煉，都不會無法忍受（申33:25；詩46:1）。基督徒不必灰心。即使被剝奪了地上的一切財產，他們最大的財寶還是安全的，是人和魔鬼所奪不走的（林後4:16；參詩23:3）。基督徒生活中所遇到的一切患難和試煉，只要正確地忍受，都會使他在基督的苦難中與祂有更加密切的交往（腓3:10）。保羅為基督的緣故所受的苦也許比其他基督徒蒙召所受的多。若是這樣，保羅就比別人更加理解與耶穌一同受苦的意義。在所有《新約》的作者中，沒有別人寫下那麼多有關十字架和與基督同死的話語。對保羅而言，即使是逼迫，試煉，犧牲，甚至捨命，也都成為光榮的經歷，因為它們在基督的苦難中使他與基督的關係更加密切了。
跟隨基督的人要通過苦難達到完美。基督的苦難提供了黑暗的背景，使祂的完美品格煥發出更加燦爛的光芒（來2:10）。祂的整個人生經歷了對自己死。沒有什麼比這更加清楚地彰顯祂和天父對罪人的愛了。同樣，基督徒生活中的試煉、患難和失望也提供了背景，彰顯神聖忍耐的美，基督化品格的芳香，以及安靜地順服上帝的旨意、堅定地信靠上帝的引導。上帝的光輝就這樣反映在基督徒的臉上。基督化的生活始終會遭遇黑暗之君隨從者的敵意和憎恨。但上帝的計劃並不是要基督徒以受苦本身為榮，也不要他們去招惹敵意和反對，讓人注意他們的自我犧牲和勇氣。
**打倒了。**kataballo，“打倒在地”，如在個人格鬥中被打倒。
**不至死亡。**保羅似乎多次不僅倒下，而且幾乎喪命。他承認多次被“打倒”，但他強調自己“不至死亡”。
9.en:
**Persecuted.** See on Matt. 5:10–12; 10:17–23; John 15:20. Each succeeding contrast reveals more fully the intensity of the suffering and personal peril. Paul speaks of being surrounded, pursued, caught, and thrown down by hostile forces. No way of escape seemed to remain, and death appeared to be inevitable.
**Not forsaken.** Through all his trials Paul and his fellow laborers experienced the fulfillment of Christ’s promise to be with them even to the point of death, and to provide a way of escape (see 1 Cor. 10:13; 2 Thess. 1:4; Heb. 2:18; 13:5). For the Christian in times of trial and persecution, certain divine truths are evident. However great the trials encountered, they are not beyond endurance (Deut. 33:25; Ps. 46:1). No Christian need be discouraged. Even when stripped of everything of earthly value his greatest treasure remains secure—beyond the reach of men and demons (2 Cor. 4:16; cf. Ps. 23:3). Rightly endured, all sufferings and trials that beset the life of the Christian serve only to bring him into closer fellowship with Christ in His sufferings (Phil. 3:10). Paul, perhaps, suffered more for Christ’s sake than any other Christian has been called upon to suffer. If so, Paul understood better than others what it meant to suffer with Jesus. Of all the NT writers, no other writes so much about the cross and about dying with Christ. With Paul, even persecution, trial, sacrifice, and life itself became experiences to glory in, because of the closer fellowship they brought with Christ in His sufferings.
Christ’s followers are to attain perfection through sufferings. Christ’s sufferings provided the dark background, as it were, against which His perfection of character shone forth with brighter luster (Heb. 2:10). His whole life was an experience of dying to self. Nothing tended to reveal more clearly His own love, and that of His Father, for sinners. Similarly, for the Christian the trials, sufferings, and disappointments of the Christian life provide a background for the beauty of divine patience, the fragrance of a Christlike character, quiet submission to the will of God, firm trust in God’s guidance. Thus the light of God is reflected upon the Christian’s countenance. Christlike living will always be met by hostility and hatred from the followers of the prince of darkness. But it is not God’s plan for the Christian to glory in suffering for its own sake, to court hostility and opposition so as to call attention to one’s self-sacrifice and courage.
**Cast down.** Gr. kataballō, “to cast down [to the ground],” “to lay prostrate,” as a man worsted in personal combat.
**Not destroyed.** Again and again it may have appeared that Paul was not only “down” but also “out.” He admits that he has repeatedly been “cast down,” but emphatically declares that he was never “destroyed.”

10.zh:
身上常帶著耶穌的死，使耶穌的生也顯明在我們身上。

**身上……帶著。**保羅無疑身上傷痕累累。這是他為基督受苦的無聲見證。
**死。**保羅經常冒著死亡的危險，所以天天要經歷死亡（羅8:36；林前15:31；提後2:11）。保羅用這個比喻表達了他在患難中與基督的親密關係。這種患難是他經常蒙召去忍受的。這是福音大能給世界的重要證據。猶太派人士沒有這樣的證據。他們傳講沒有生命的律法主義福音來逃避逼迫（見加6:12）。
**耶穌的生也顯明在我們身上。**保羅身上的傷疤證明他離死亡是多麼近；同樣他依然活著，雄辯地證明了基督拯救他脫離死亡的能力。保羅的生還證明了基督的能力能救人脫離罪惡，並把他們變成基督的樣式（見加2:20）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第251，297頁；《給傳道人的證言》第388頁；《證言》卷二第343頁。
10.en:
**Bearing about in the body.** Here and there on Paul’s body there were doubtless many scars that bore mute testimony to his sufferings for Christ.
**The dying.** Literally, “the death.” For Paul this was a perpetual, daily dying, made real by his own constant exposure to death (Rom. 8:36; 1 Cor. 15:31; 2 Tim. 2:11). By this figure of speech Paul expresses his intimate fellowship with Christ in the sufferings he is continually called upon to endure. This constituted a vital testimony to the world concerning the power of the gospel. The Judaizers, who escaped persecution by preaching a lifeless, legal gospel, could offer no such evidence (see Gal. 6:12).
**Life also of Jesus.** As his scars testified of how close Paul had come to death, the fact that he still lived bore eloquent testimony to the power of Christ to deliver him from death. Also, Paul’s life testified to the power of Christ to deliver men from sin and to transform them into His likeness (see Gal. 2:20).

11.zh:
因為我們這活著的人是常為耶穌被交於死地，使耶穌的生在我們這必死的身上顯明出來。

**我們這活著的人。**保羅在本節進一步肯定了他在第10節中所說的話。就當時的福音使者而言，生與死總是相距不遠的。
**常。**該詞原文處於強調的位置。保羅的生與死很近（見林前15:29註釋）。
**生。**基督的傳道士雖然經常被交付死地，但他依然活著，因為基督將自己的生命賜給必死必朽的人（約3:36；14:6；約一5:11,12）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《福山寶訓》第78頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–14節）**。《使徒行述》第331頁。
11.en:
**We which live.** Paul here amplifies and confirms what he has already stated in v. 10. For the ambassador of the gospel in those days, life and death were never far apart.
**Alway.** In the Greek this word is in the emphatic position. Paul lived intimately with death (see on 1 Cor. 15:29).
**That the life.** Though permanently handed over to death, the Christian missionary lives on, for Christ communicates His own life to that which is essentially mortal and corruptible (John 3:36; 14:6; 1 John 5:11, 12).

12.zh:
這樣看來，死是在我們身上發動，生卻在你們身上發動。

保羅現在進一步將生與死進行對比。雖然福音使者經常面臨死亡的威脅，但他的目的卻是要將生命帶給那些註定因罪死亡的人。這裡的“生”用於更高的屬靈意義。保羅帶領的信徒雖然沒有經歷過像他那樣的生死搏鬥，上帝卻使用他將生命帶給他們。基督的能力蘊藏在卑微的瓦器，就是保羅自己的生命中，將新生命分給哥林多人。
12.en: **Death worketh.** Paul now proceeds a step further in the contrast between life and death. While death is ever a present prospect for the gospel messenger, his objective is to bring life to those who are doomed to death because of sin. Here the term “life” is used in its higher spiritual sense. Although Paul’s converts have experienced little or nothing of a life-and-death conflict comparable to his, nevertheless God has used him to minister life to them. From the lowly earthenware vessel, which was Paul’s own life, proceeds the power of Christ to impart new life to the Corinthians.

13.zh:
但我們既有信心，正如經上記著說：我因信，所以如此說話。我們也信，所以也說話。

**信心。**即《舊約》的引文所表達的那種信心：“我因信，所以如此說話”。保羅給哥林多人寫信，深深相信並誠摯希望他們會聽他的勸。
**經上記著說。**引自詩116:10。這首詩顯然是他的支柱和安慰。保羅和大衛都證明和相信上帝的良善和大愛。他們都經歷過試煉、患難和拯救，都能充滿把握地說話。與死亡接近並不妨礙活潑的信心所表達的快樂。聖經中所有偉人的生活都閃現這種勝利的精神，喜樂開朗的心情。他們即使是在迫害和損失中也表達對上帝的快樂感恩。所有體驗過上帝之愛的基督徒，都在生活中快樂地表達那種愛和能力。表達心中的認識和感受是非常自然和容易的。一個人講述他所不相信的事，那是偽善者；而他若不肯說出自己信仰，那就是懦夫。
13.en:
**Spirit of faith.** The same faith as that expressed in the OT quotation, “I believed, and therefore have I spoken.” Paul writes to the Corinthians with a profound sense of conviction and in earnest hope that they will heed his counsel.
**It is written.** The quotation is from Ps. 116:10. This psalm had evidently been his stay and comfort. Both Paul and David had proved, and thus were convinced of, the goodness and love of God. Both experienced trial, suffering, and deliverance, and both spoke with conviction. The nearness of death is no hindrance to the joyous expression of a living faith. The lives of all the great men and women of the Bible sparkle with this spirit of triumph, this mood of buoyancy and radiance. They express joyful gratitude to God even in the midst of loss and persecution. The lives of all Christians who have experienced the love of God become joyfully expressive of that love and power. It is natural and easy for the tongue to express what the mind knows and the heart feels. The man who speaks what he does not believe is a hypocrite, whereas the man who believes what he will not speak is a coward.

14.zh:
自己知道那叫主耶穌復活的，也必叫我們與耶穌一同復活，並且叫我們與你們一同站在他面前。

**叫主耶穌復活的。**保羅曾對哥林多信徒做過詳細的解釋（見林前15:13-23）。耶穌的復活是所有義人最後復活的絕對保證。
**叫我們……一同復活。**保羅對復活的堅定盼望，使他能平靜而勇敢地面對死亡。他與基督一同經歷了屬靈的復活（羅6:4）。這是他將來戰勝死亡的保證。他對永生有把握（羅8:11；林前15:12-22；提後4:8）。
**與耶穌。**保羅指的是我們主的復活。他覺得自己的復活是很有把握的。耶穌是贖民中首先復活的（啟1:5）。贖民包括使徒的所有信徒（林前15:20）。此外在末日基督會叫死人復活（約5:25-29）。
**叫我們一同與你們站在祂面前。**與基督一同得勝的人最快樂的時刻也許就是站在父上帝的面前。保羅驕傲地預見到把他的信徒呈獻給基督（11:2）。聖經多次提及基督徒被呈獻在上帝面前。他們為辯護和稱義來到基督的審判臺前（羅14:10-12；林後5:10）。在羔羊的婚宴上他們將作為羔羊的新娘被帶到上帝面前（啟19:7-9），並住在祂面前（啟21:3）。
本節的文字似乎表明，保羅期待在他的主來到之前去世，與復活有份。
14.en:
**Raised up the Lord.** As Paul had already explained to the Corinthians at length (see 1 Cor. 15:13–23), the resurrection of Jesus stood as an absolute guarantee of the eventual resurrection of all the righteous.
**Raise up us.** It is Paul’s confident hope of the resurrection that enables him to face death with calm and courage. He has already experienced a spiritual resurrection with Christ (Rom. 6:4), and this is his assurance of future triumph over death. He is sure of eternal life (Rom. 8:11; 1 Cor. 15:12–22; 2 Tim. 4:8).
**By Jesus.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the reading “with Jesus.” Paul refers to the resurrection of our Lord. He feels that his own resurrection is fully as certain. Jesus was raised up as the first of a redeemed race (Rev. 1:5), which would include all of the apostle’s converts (1 Cor. 15:20). Furthermore, it is Christ who will bring the dead to life at the last day (John 5:25–29).
**Present us.** Perhaps the greatest moment of joy for those who triumph with Christ will be their presentation before God the Father. Paul anticipates with pride presenting his converts to Christ (ch. 11:2). The Scriptures refer several times to Christians being presented, or simply being present, before God. They appear before Christ at His judgment seat, for vindication and justification (Rom. 14:10–12; 2 Cor. 5:10). They will be presented before God at the marriage supper of the Lamb, as the bride of the Lamb (Rev. 19:7–9), and will dwell in His presence (ch. 21:3).
It may be noted in passing that the language of this verse seems to intimate that Paul expected to die before the return of his Lord, and to have a part in the resurrection.

15.zh:
凡事都是為你們，好叫恩惠因人多越發加增，感謝格外顯多，以致榮耀歸與神。

**凡事。**就是保羅作為基督的使者所遭遇的一切事情（7-12節）。參林前3:22,23；提後2:10。
**恩惠……加增。**指使罪人得救蒙贖的上帝恩典（約1:14,16,17；徒20:24,32；羅4:16；5:20等）。
**感謝格外顯多。**保羅預見上帝所得的榮耀將越來越多，因為藉著他的服務而歸向基督的人越多，上帝聖名所得的榮耀也就越多（參9:11,12）。正如雨水使土地結出果實，上帝豐盛的恩典也使人有感恩的反應（參弗2:6-8）。這種反應是對上帝良善、恩慈、仁愛和能力的自然承認。感謝讚美上帝，表明人與上帝已恢復了正常的關係。這是福音的主要目的。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第288，550頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–18節）**。《使徒行述》第332頁。
15.en:
**All things.** That is, all of the things Paul has suffered as an ambassador for Christ (vs. 7–12). Compare 1 Cor. 3:22, 23; 2 Tim. 2:10.
**Abundant grace.** That is, the grace of God that makes possible the salvation and redemption of the sinner (John 1:14, 16, 17; Acts 20:24, 32; Rom. 4:16; 5:20; etc.).
**Thanksgiving of many.** Paul foresees increasing glory being given to God, for the more people he turns to Christ through his ministry, the more there will be to ascribe glory to God’s holy name (cf. ch. 9:11, 12). As the rain brings forth the fruits of the earth, so the abundant grace of God leads men to respond with thanksgiving (cf. Eph. 2:6–8). This response comes as the spontaneous acknowledgement of God’s goodness, mercy, love, and power. The rendering of thanks and praise to God indicates the restoration of right relations between God and man, and this is the principal aim of the gospel.

16.zh:
所以，我們不喪膽。外體雖然毀壞，內心卻一天新似一天。

**所以。**將來喜樂和榮耀的前景，使保羅安靜耐心地面對他工作中所遇到的試煉與磨難（參來12:2）。福音的使者忍受地上的變遷，因為他們每天活著都像“看見那不能看見的主”（來11:27）。他們堅信將來的榮耀；今生的一切經歷都只是增進他們的盼望、喜樂和信心。
**外體。**就是身體，人體看得見的部分，會隨著生活的磨礪而衰殘。在另一方面，“內心”指人經過重生的屬靈本性，是上帝的靈所天天更新的（羅7:22；弗3:16；4:24；西3:9,10；彼前3:4）。更新的過程不斷進行，使人與上帝聯合起來。保羅經常提到這種更新（羅12:2；弗4:23；多3:5）。聖靈工作的一個方面就是不斷提供屬靈的生命，力量，勇氣和信心，使信徒得到更新。
聖靈在人生命中每天的更新工作，使上帝的形象在人心中得到完全的恢復。雖然外體會隨著年歲變老朽壞，但只要一息尚存，內心就會繼續在恩典中成長。保羅能平靜地看待生活中的試煉，時光的流逝，年齡的衰老，痛苦和患難，以及死亡本身。同時聖靈帶給他永生的保證，是在復活之日領受的禮物（提後4:8）。
每一個基督徒如果不願使他與上帝的關係變得冷淡和形式化，他每天就都需要得到更新。屬靈的更新帶來上帝之道的新亮光，恩典的新經歷，好與他人分享，以及心靈重新得到潔淨。相比之下，未經更新的生命常為與外體有關的事而憂慮，比如吃什麼，穿什麼，享受什麼。見太6:24-34註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–18節）**。《餘民教會》61頁。
16.en:
**For which cause.** It is the prospect of future joy and glory that leads Paul to face with equanimity and patience the trials and tribulations attending his ministry (cf. Heb. 12:2). Ambassadors of the gospel endure the vicissitudes of this earth, for they live daily “as seeing him who is invisible” (Heb. 11:27). They are so confident of the glorious of the future that all the experiences of this life simply inspire added hope, joy, and faithfulness.
**Outward man.** That is, the body, the visible part of man, which decays under the wear and tear of life. The “inward man,” on the other hand, denotes man’s regenerate, spiritual nature, which has been and is daily being renewed by the Spirit of God (Rom. 7:22; Eph. 3:16; 4:24; Col. 3:9, 10; 1 Peter 3:4). The process of renewal goes forward constantly and keeps him united to God. Paul makes constant reference to this renewal (Rom. 12:2; Eph. 4:23; Titus 3:5). One aspect of the Holy Spirit’s work is the renewing of the believer with new supplies of spiritual life, energy, courage, and faith.
It is the daily renewing work of the Spirit in the life that brings about the complete restoration of the image of God in the soul of man. Thus, though the outward man may grow old and decay with the years, the inward man continues to grow in grace as long as life lasts. Paul could look calmly on the trials of life, on the flight of time, on the advance of age, on pain and suffering, on death itself. At the same time the Holy Spirit brought to him the assurance of immortality, a gift to be received on the resurrection day (2 Tim. 4:8).
Every Christian needs this daily renewal if his experience with God is not to become callous and formal. Spiritual renewal brings new light from God’s Word, new experiences of grace, to share with others, new cleansing of heart and mind. In contrast, the unregenerate are usually anxious about those things that pertain to the outer man, what to eat, what to wear, and what to enjoy. See on Matt. 6:24–34.

17.zh:
我們這至暫至輕的苦楚，要為我們成就極重無比、永遠的榮耀。

**至暫。**parautika，“暫時”，“立即”。與永恆相比，片刻算不得什麼。基督徒一想到永生，就足以忍受任何短暫的痛苦。
很少有人像保羅那樣為基督經受那麼多的苦難（林後11:23-30）。他走到哪裡，苦難就天天跟到哪裡。他的苦楚本身是夠重的，但與永遠的喜樂、將來的榮耀相比，就顯得十分短暫。參羅8:18；腓1:29；來2:9,10。
**至輕的苦楚。**本採用最高級的詞語進行對比，是保羅著作中語氣最強的段落之一。使徒在這裡將眼前的事與將來的時事，暫時的事與永恆的事，痛苦與榮耀進行對比。
**無比。**保羅覺得“極重的榮耀”一詞不足以表達他所看到的苦難時期與永恆福樂之間的對比。他又加上一個最高級詞語（參約壹3:1）。這個希臘習語也許是他自己發明的。參保羅在羅7:13；林前12:31；林後1:8和加1:13中所用的其他最高級詞語。
苦難能潔淨，純煉和提高品格，從而增進永遠的榮耀（詩94:12；賽48:10；來12:5-11；雅1:2-4,12；彼前1:7）。它培養對上帝的信心和依靠（詩34:19；賽63:9；何5:15；拿2:2），發揮感服人心的影響，降伏驕傲，征服自我，常常使信徒的意願與上帝的旨意完全和諧。它還考驗信徒的信心，以及他們的基督徒信仰是否真誠（伯23:10；詩66:10）。它為信心的運用和完善提供機會。信心會越用越強。苦難幫助信徒看清事物的本質，把重要的事擺在首位。苦難就這樣造就基督徒配得榮耀。基督徒通過苦難的訓練排除了世俗的目標，將更容易將自己的情感寄託在屬天的事上（西3:1,2；提後4:5）。苦難置人於困境，摧毀了人的智慧，使人感到無助而需要上帝（詩107:39）。它能潔淨人際關係。沒有什麼比憂愁、試煉和苦難更有助於我們理解同胞，並對他們懷有溫情。
**榮耀。**doxa（見約1:14；羅3:23註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第560頁；《給管家的勉言》第26頁；《佈道論》第244頁；《早期著作》第17，66頁；《善惡之爭》第351，460頁；《傳道良助》第18頁；《福山寶訓》第30頁；《今日的生活》第338頁；《先祖與先知》第127，476頁；《成聖的人生》第76頁；《證言》卷一第61，126，544，657頁；《證言》卷二第38，40，44，101，275，286，358頁；《證言》卷三第481頁；《證言》卷四第526頁；《證言》卷五第260，309，351頁；《證言》卷六第156頁；《證言》卷七第29頁；《證言》卷八第131頁；《證言》卷九第49，115頁；《論福利工作》第317頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–18節）**。《使徒行述》第363頁；《早期著作》第14，28頁；《證言》卷一第706頁；《證言》卷三第98，115頁；《證言》卷五第745頁；《證言》卷八第125頁。
17.en:
**Light affliction.** This verse, with its paradoxical superlatives, is one of the most emphatic passages in all of Paul’s writings. Here the apostle contrasts things of the present with things to come, things of time with those of eternity, affliction with glory.
**For a moment.** Gr. parautika, “momentary,” “immediate.” Compared with eternity, a moment is nothing. In view of eternity the Christian can well afford to endure any affliction for the brief space of a moment.
Few men have suffered as much for Christ as Paul did (ch. 11:23–30). Affliction pursued him everywhere he went, and every day. Considered by themselves, his afflictions were heavy indeed. But when compared with the joys of eternity and the glory of the hereafter, they were but momentary. Compare Rom. 8:18; Phil. 1:29; Heb. 2:9, 10.
**Far more exceeding.** Paul finds the words “eternal weight of glory” altogether inadequate to express the contrast he sees between the afflictions of time and the bliss of eternity. He adds still another superlative (cf. 1 John 3:1), a Greek idiom which he himself perhaps coined. Compare other superlative expressions used by Paul in Rom. 7:13; 1 Cor. 12:31; 2 Cor. 1:8; Gal. 1:13.
Affliction contributes to eternal glory by purifying, refining, and elevating the character (Ps. 94:12; Isa. 48:10; Heb. 12:5–11; James 1:2–4, 12; 1 Peter 1:7). It cultivates trust in, and dependence upon, God (Ps. 34:19; Isa. 63:9; Hosea 5:15; Jonah 2:2). Affliction exerts a subduing influence upon the heart and mind. It prostrates pride, subdues self, and is often the means of bringing the will of the believer into more complete harmony with the will of God. It tests the believer’s faith and the genuineness of his profession as a Christian (Job 23:10; Ps. 66:10). It gives occasion for the exercise and perfection of faith. Faith is strengthened by exercise. It helps the believer to see things in their true perspective, and to put first things first. Affliction thus creates in Christians a suitableness for glory. When worldly objectives are removed through the discipline of suffering, the Christian finds it easier to set his affection on heavenly things (Col. 3:1, 2; 2 Tim. 4:5). It proves the bankruptcy of human wisdom by placing the believer in difficult positions, where his own helplessness and need of God becomes apparent (Ps. 107:39). It sanctifies human relationships. Nothing contributes more to understanding our fellow men and having a feeling of kindness toward them than do sorrow, trial, and suffering.
**Glory.** Gr. doxa (see on John 1:14; Rom. 3:23).

18.zh:
原來我們不是顧念所見的，乃是顧念所不見的；因為所見的是暫時的，所不見的是永遠的。

保羅現在解釋為什麼能看清今生苦難真正性質，並視之為暫時的。他的目光注視永恆國度的榮耀（參來12:2）。人所關注的任何對象，將決定人如何忍受試煉，是帶著希望和忍耐，還是帶著不滿和苦毒。前者來自默想永恆世界看不見的事物（腓4:8），和基督的屬靈現實；後者來自關注看得見的暫時事物，如財富，快樂和名聲（見太6:24-34註釋）。我們關注基督的生活和品格，就會變得像祂（參來11:10,26,27,39,40；彼前1:11）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第412，662頁；《教育論》第183，296頁；《福山寶訓》第32頁；《服務真詮》第37頁；《先知與君王》第548頁；《證言》卷四第345頁；《證言》卷七第143頁。
