18.en: **While we look.** Paul now explains how it is possible to see the afflictions of this life in their true perspective and to view them as of only momentary consequence. His gaze was fixed upon the glories of the eternal kingdom (cf. Heb. 12:2). Whatever gains the fixed attention of the mind determines how one will endure trial, whether with hope and patience or with dissatisfaction and bitterness. The former comes from contemplating the unseen things of the eternal world (Phil. 4:8), the spiritual realities of Christ; the latter from looking at such visible, transitory things as wealth, pleasure, and fame (see on Matt. 6:24–34). By fixing the mind upon the character and life of Christ we become like Him (cf. Heb. 11:10, 26, 27, 39, 40; 1 Peter 1:11).

1.zh:
弟兄們，我把神賜給馬其頓眾教會的恩告訴你們，

**弟兄們。**第8章和第9章組成一個新的部分，涉及為猶大的窮人募捐（見林前16:1註釋）。“弟兄們”一詞為這個部分定下了基調。基督徒之間的弟兄之愛給施捨和分享提供了真正的動機。保羅在林後8:1-5呼籲哥林多信徒注意馬其頓各教會所樹立的慷慨榜樣。保羅為此寫了這封書信。
保羅以前曾把接濟猶大的問題和有關大捐獻的計劃告訴哥林多信徒（林前16:1-4；參2:9,10）。保羅在大約一年前第一次提出這個計劃時（林後8:10），他們曾表現出極大的熱情。後來保羅為此對別人誇獎了他們（林後9:3,4）。但是他們的熱情消退了。保羅寫這封書信時，他們在履行行善的承諾方面已大大落後（林後9:4,5）。這可能是因為他們處於屬靈的衰退時期。但是他們現在已經完全悔改了。他們的悔改是真誠的。保羅正確地推定他們會急於用實際方式證明他們的愛。真悔改的標誌之一就是樂意為需要的人作出個人的犧牲。
**我把……告訴你們。**一種禮貌的古老表達方式，意為“我們想告訴你們”。
**上帝……的恩。**馬其頓教會雖然“極窮”，卻很慷慨（第2節），這就證明“上帝……的恩”在他們心中工作。保羅追溯了他們慷慨的真正根源，向哥林多信徒指出，上帝的恩典激發了慷慨捨己的捐獻。基督徒被稱為“上帝百般恩賜的好管家”（彼前4:10）。況且基督徒要靠著上帝的恩典，管理他所擁有的一切。樂善好施的性情是上帝所激發的才能，所以是上帝恩典的特別證據。慷慨的精神自然表現在慈善之舉中，無須催促。
**馬其頓眾教會。**保羅稱讚這些教會值得效法。這些教會都是他所建立的──腓立比，帖撒羅尼迦，庇哩亞，也許還有其他教會。腓立比教會在慷慨捐助方面特別突出，是唯一記錄下來幫助保羅作為自養傳道人個人需要的教會（林後11:9；參腓4:10,11,14-18）。他沒有接受耶路撒冷教會或安提阿教會的經濟支援（林前9:4-7,14,15）。庇哩亞教會也有很高尚的品質（徒17:10-12）。慷慨的捐助來自馬其頓和亞該亞（羅15:26）。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–5節）**。《使徒行述》第343頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–6節）**。《證言》卷六第271頁。
1.en:
**Brethren.** Chapters 8 and 9 constitute a new section, which deals with the collection for the poor in Judea (see on 1 Cor. 16:1). The word “brethren” strikes the keynote of the new section. Brotherly love among Christians provides the true motive for giving and sharing. In 2 Cor. 8:1–5 Paul calls to the attention of the Corinthians the example of generosity set by the churches of Macedonia, whence Paul writes this epistle.
Paul had previously acquainted the Corinthians with the relief problem in Judea and his plan concerning the great collection (1 Cor. 16:1–4; cf. Gal. 2:9, 10). When Paul had first introduced the proposal, about a year earlier (2 Cor. 8:10), they had manifested great zeal, of which Paul later boasted to others (ch. 9:3, 4). But their zeal had waned, and at the time Paul wrote this epistle they were far behind in making good on their promises (ch. 9:4, 5). This had probably been due to the period of spiritual declension, but now they had made full repentance. Their conversion being genuine, Paul rightly assumed that they would be eager to demonstrate their love in a practical way. One mark of genuine conversion is a willingness to make personal sacrifices for others who may be in need.
**We do you to wit.** A polite, archaic expression meaning, “we wish to make known to you.”
**Grace of God.** The liberality of the Macedonian churches came about in spite of their “deep poverty” (v. 2), and this testified to “the grace of God” at work in their hearts. Paul traces their generosity to its true source, and points out to the Corinthians that it is divine grace that inspires generous and sacrificial giving. Christians are said to be “stewards of the manifold grace of God” (1 Peter 4:10). Furthermore, by the grace of God, Christians are stewards of the things they possess. The disposition to give to others is a divinely inspired talent, and thus a special evidence of divine grace. A liberal spirit seeks spontaneously for an outlet in acts of benevolence. It does not need urging.
**Churches of Macedonia.** Paul exalted these as worthy of emulation. They were all founded by him—Philippi, Thessalonica, Beroea, and perhaps others. The church at Philippi was particularly noteworthy for its generosity. It was the only church on record that contributed to Paul’s personal needs as a self-supporting missionary (2 Cor. 11:9; cf. Phil. 4:10, 11, 14–18). He received no financial support from either the church at Jerusalem or the one at Antioch (1 Cor. 9:4–7, 14, 15). The church at Beroea was also of a high and noble character (Acts 17:10–12). Liberal contributions came from Macedonia and Achaia (Rom. 15:26).

2.zh:
就是他們在患難中受大試煉的時候，仍有滿足的快樂，在極窮之間還格外顯出他們樂捐的厚恩。

**試煉。**或“試驗”。該詞特別用來指測試金屬的品質。馬其頓的基督徒遭受非凡的患難。但他們的信心和經驗證明是真實的。他們遭受了嚴重的迫害（徒17:5-9；帖前1:6-8；2:14；3:3-5；帖後1:4-6）。得勝的基督徒經驗的重大證據之一，就是患難中享受喜樂、平安和仁愛（太5:11,12；羅5:3；12:12；彼前2:20,21）。
**滿足的快樂。**逼迫和貧窮都可能壓制慷慨的精神和行動。但他們極窮之中的滿足快樂表現在鼓舞人心的慷慨之舉上。這就是早期教會的精神（徒4:32-37）。
**極窮。**馬其頓人的貧窮，就好比是要刮淨幾乎是空了的桶底。但他們雖然極窮，卻充滿了幫助其他窮人的深情。保羅稱讚馬其頓的基督徒，不是為他們捐獻的實際數量，儘管這是無疑是可觀的。保羅所指出值得效法的，是促使他們施捨的精神（見可12:41-44註釋）。
馬其頓信徒這時的極度貧困有若干因素。三次戰亂使這個地區幾近荒蕪：第一次是尤里烏斯·凱撒與龐培；第二次是暗殺凱撒之後的三人執政官與布魯特斯和卡修斯；第三次是奧古斯都與安東尼（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷六，28,35,37頁）。馬其頓人的境況非常窘迫，所以他們曾向提庇留皇帝請求減稅。此外，大多數早期的基督徒都來自貧困的社會階層。
**樂捐。**haplotēs，“（內心）單純”，“真誠”，“沒有偽裝”（林後11:3；弗6:5；西3:22等）。這裡指在極大的慷慨中所表現出來的開闊胸襟。它不是指捐獻的數量，而是指作為一切真捐獻基礎的心態。這種心態會導致自發為他人的利益而自我犧牲。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷三第413頁；《論福利工作》第205頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–5節）**。《證言》卷五第734頁。
2.en:
**Trial.** Or, “test.” The word is used especially of testing the quality of metals. The Macedonian Christians suffered more than ordinary affliction, yet their faith and experience proved genuine. They suffered severely from persecution (Acts 17:5–9; 1 Thess. 1:6–8; 2:14; 3:3–5; 2 Thess. 1:4–6). One of the great tests of a triumphant Christian experience is to know joy, peace, and love in the midst of affliction (Matt. 5:11, 12; Rom. 5:3; 12:12; 1 Peter 2:20, 21).
**Abundance of their joy.** Persecution and poverty would both tend to repress the spirit and practice of liberality, but the abundance of their joy combined with the depth of their poverty is represented as inspiring generosity. Such was the spirit of the early church (Acts 4:32–37).
**Deep poverty abounded.** Figuratively speaking, the poverty of the Macedonians was such that they had to scrape the bottom of a barrel that was all but empty. Yet in spite of utter destitution they overflowed abundantly with help for others in need. The measure of Paul’s praise of the Macedonian Christians was not for the actual amount given, though it was doubtless considerable. It was the spirit that prompted the giving to which Paul pointed as worthy of emulation (see on Mark 12:41–44).
The abysmal poverty of Macedonia at this time was due to various factors. Three wars had desolated the area: the first, between Julius Caesar and Pompey, the second, between the triumvirs and Brutus and Cassius following Caesar’s assassination, and the third, between Octavian and Antony (see Vol. V, p. 28, 35, 37). So desperate was the condition of the Macedonians that they had petitioned the emperor Tiberius for a reduction of taxes. Furthermore, most of the early Christians came from the poorer classes of society.
**Liberality.** Gr. haplotēs, “singleness [of heart],” “sincerity,” “freedom from pretense” (2 Cor. 11:3; Eph. 6:5; Col. 3:22; etc.). Here it denotes that openness of mind and heart which manifested itself in great liberality. It refers, not so much to what they gave, but to the quality of heart that is the basis of all true giving and that results in spontaneous self-sacrifice for the welfare of others.

3.zh:
我可以證明，他們是按著力量，而且也過了力量，自己甘心樂意的捐助，

原文3至6節是一個句子，進一步解釋了1,2節所說樂捐的性質。馬其頓人的捐獻超過了他們的能力。他們不希望捐得太少，而是要太多。他們的捐獻是自發的，沒有被人催促，也不需要提醒，象哥林多信徒現在似乎所需要的那樣。馬其頓信徒知道有需要就夠了。他們要求有權參加幫助耶路撒冷貧窮聖徒的工作。他們的精神體現了對聖工完全的自我奉獻和自我犧牲。
3.en: **To their power.** In the Greek vs. 3–6 constitute one sentence, which explains further the quality of liberality mentioned in vs. 1, 2. The Macedonians gave beyond their ability and means. Their tendency was not to give too little, but too much. They gave spontaneously and without being urged or even reminded, as it seemed the Corinthians now needed to be. It was sufficient that the Macedonians know of the need that existed. They requested the privilege of being allowed to share in the ministry of being allowed to share in the ministry to the poor saints at Jerusalem. Their spirit exhibited complete self-dedication and self-sacrifice to the work of the Lord.

4.zh:
再三的求我們，準他們在這供給聖徒的恩情上有分；

**再三地。**paraklēsis（見太5:4註釋）。
**有分。**馬其頓信徒視他們耶路撒冷弟兄的需要為自己的需要。馬其頓信徒認為，既加入基督徒大家庭，要與其他的基督徒一同犧牲，受苦，分擔貧困和幫助別人。不論是否力所能及，他們都樂意在凡事上共享，即便是貧窮（見徒2:44；4:32）。他們願與人分享自己屬靈，道德，社會和物質的資源，為共同的事業所用。實際上他們為有這樣的機會而感到榮幸。
4.en:
**Intreaty.** Gr. paraklēsis (see on Matt. 5:4).
**Fellowship.** The Macedonians considered the need of their brethren in Jerusalem as if it were their own. For the believers in Macedonia, to belong to the great Christian family meant to have common cause with their fellow Christians in sacrifice, in suffering, in sharing poverty, and in helping others. To the extent of their ability, and beyond, they were ready to have all things—even poverty—in common (see Acts 2:44; 4:32). Their spiritual, moral, social, and material resources were available to others, ready to be drawn upon in a common cause. In fact, they considered it a favor to be permitted to do so.

5.zh:
並且他們所做的，不但照我們所想望的，更照神的旨意先把自己獻給主，又歸附了我們。

**不但照我們所想望的。**他們超過了保羅的最高希望。他們認為捐獻不只是責任，更是特權。他們把這件事當作是自己的。
**上帝的旨意。**他們讓上帝指導他們的人生。祂的旨意成為他們的意願。這是徹底悔改的證據。
**把自己獻給。**馬其頓人的捐獻出於一顆奉獻的心。他們獻上自己，捐獻就自然隨之而來。他們藉著捐獻將自己獻上（參箴23:26）。把心獻給上帝的基督徒無所保留的。馬其頓人的榜樣對哥林多人和各時代的基督徒證明了一個偉大的真理：“沒有送禮者的禮物就是空的”。毫無保留地獻上自己的人，會毫不猶豫地奉獻他們的所有。
5.en:
**Not as we hoped.** Rather, they had exceeded Paul’s fondest expectations. They looked upon the collection, not as a duty, but as a privilege. They made the cause their own.
**Gave their own selves.** The Macedonian gift came from consecrated and devoted hearts. They gave themselves, and their gifts automatically followed. They gave themselves in their gifts (cf. Prov. 23:26). The Christian who gives God his heart keeps nothing back. The example of the Macedonians to the Corinthians and to Christians of all time illustrates the great truth that “the gift without the giver is bare.” He who gives himself without reservation will not hesitate to give his possessions also.
**Will of God.** They permitted God to direct their lives, and His will became theirs. Here was evidence of thorough conversion.

6.zh:
因此我勸提多，既然在你們中間開辦這慈惠的事，就當辦成了。

**勸。**parakaleo（見太5:4註釋）。提多是希臘人（加2:1,3），是保羅最信任的朋友之一（多1:4）。保羅曾派提多去處理哥林多的難題。他的使命出乎意料地成功了（見林後7:13註釋）。他贏得了哥林多信徒的信任，並開始在他們中間為猶大的窮人募捐。現在計劃讓他把這封書信帶回到哥林多完成募捐（見林後9:5；參12:18）。
**既然……開辦。**即提多既已開始正在哥林多進行的計劃。
**這慈惠的事。**就是募捐，反映了上帝的恩典運行在捐獻者的心中（見1,2節註釋）。
6.en:
**Desired.** Gr. parakaleō (see on Matt. 5:4). Titus was a Greek (Gal. 2:1, 3), and was one of Paul’s most trusted friends (Titus 1:4). Paul had sent Titus to deal with the difficult Corinthian problem, and his mission had proved successful beyond expectation (see on 2 Cor. 7:13). He had won the confidence of the Corinthian believers, and had begun a collection among them for the poor in Judea. The plan now was for him to return to Corinth with this epistle and to complete the collection (see ch. 9:5; cf. ch. 12:18).
**As he had begun.** That is, Titus had set in operation the plan now in progress at Corinth.
**The same grace.** That is, the collection, which reflected the grace of God operating in the hearts of the givers (see on vs. 1, 2).

7.zh:
你們既然在信心、口才、知識、熱心，和待我們的愛心上，都格外顯出滿足來，就當在這慈惠的事上也格外顯出滿足來。

**在信心、口才、知識、熱心，和待我們的愛心上。**一個均衡基督徒的經驗是在生命和服務上，在內在的美德及其外在的表現上和諧發展。基督徒生命任何一面的培養若是以犧牲其他方面為代價，就是有損的。參林前1:5。哥林多信徒在許多方面都很優秀。若在慈善上疏忽了，就會不協調。
**格外顯出滿足。**保羅在7至15節對哥林多信徒發出捐獻的指示。他提到基督徒的生命是豐盛的生命這項原則（約10:10）。
**這慈惠的事。**指捐獻（見1,2節註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第344頁；《醫療佈道論》第184頁；《證言》卷三第392頁；《證言》卷五第271頁。
7.en:
**Ye abound.** In vs. 7–15 Paul gives directions concerning the collection in Corinth. He appeals to the principle that the Christian life is an abundant life (John 10:10).
**In every thing.** A symmetrical Christian experience is a harmonious development of life and service, of inward graces and an outward expression of them. Any aspect of the Christian life cultivated at the expense of other aspects may become a blemish. Compare 1 Cor. 1:5. The Corinthians excelled in so many ways that it would be inconsistent to neglect the grace of charity.
**The grace.** That is, the collection (see on vs. 1, 2).

8.zh:
我說這話，不是吩咐你們，乃是藉著別人的熱心試驗你們愛心的實在。

**不是吩咐你們。**參林前7:6,12,25。捐獻要出於自願，不是因為保羅的要求。這樣的吩咐會顯出懷疑他們出於愛心之順從的誠意，破壞了只有自願奉獻才蒙上帝悅納的原則（見可12:41-44註釋）。
**別人的熱心。**指馬其頓信徒在非常貧窮時，響應捐助耶路撒冷窮人的呼籲。
**試驗。**馬其頓信徒高尚的榜樣成了上帝所指定試驗哥林多信徒的手段。保羅沒有用驕傲，虛榮，自私的感情或競爭的精神來促使哥林多信徒去做更高尚的動機無法使他們去做的事情。效法高尚的生活決不是叫人競爭，而是試驗人愛心和奉獻的深度和誠意。這種比較的高尚原則提供了有價值的屬靈訓練方法。
**你們愛心的實在。**見林後7:11,16註釋。保羅並沒有懷疑他們的誠意，而是認識到捐獻提供了良好的機會，證明他們愛心的真誠。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–9節）**。《給管家的勉言》第19頁。
8.en:
**Not by commandment.** Compare 1 Cor. 7:6, 12, 25. The collection is to be completed by their own free choice, not because Paul requires it of them. Such a command would have expressed doubt of their willingness to comply on the basis of love, and would have nullified the principle that only freewill offerings are acceptable to God (see on Mark 12:41–44).
**Forwardness of others.** That is, the readiness of the Macedonian believers, out of their comparative poverty, to respond to the plea to assist the needy at Jerusalem.
**To prove.** The noble example of the Macedonians becomes a divinely appointed test for the Corinthians. Paul did not appeal to pride, vanity, selfish feeling, or a spirit of rivalry and competition in order to urge the Corinthians to do something that more worthy motives would not lead them to do. The emulation of noble lives is never an appeal to rivalry, but it does test the depth and genuineness of one’s love and devotion. This elevated principle of comparison provides a valuable means of spiritual discipline.
**Sincerity of your love.** See on ch. 7:11, 16. Paul did not doubt their sincerity, but knew that the collection provided an ideal opportunity to demonstrate the genuineness of their love.

9.zh:
你們知道我們主耶穌基督的恩典：他本來富足，卻為你們成了貧窮，叫你們因他的貧窮，可以成為富足。

**你們知道。**保羅已對他們充分闡述了基督的恩典。原文暗示他們體驗了這恩典，而不只是作為一個信條。他們已經嘗過滋味，知道主是仁慈的。事實上他們自己已成了恩典的活證據。基督的恩典必須控制人的心靈和意志。如果只是作為頭腦的概念，就決無效果。就此而言，任何上帝的真理都不可能單憑理智就認識（見太16:17；約6:45；16:14；林前2:4；12:3）。只有受聖靈教導和感動的人，才會認識到上帝的道是真理。通過生命中屬靈的啟迪，基督的貧窮成為我們的富足。
**主耶穌基督。**見太1:1；約1:38註釋。
**恩典。**見羅3:24註釋。只有本節和羅5:15，加1:6把基督的高尚舉動，祂的道成肉身和釘十字架歸功於恩典。這些舉動是上帝慈愛和屈尊的最高表現。保羅在這裡將基督的崇高犧牲和人無比卑微的善行進行了對比。
**祂本來富足。**指基督道成肉身以前就已存在（見約17:5；見腓2:6,7註釋；見《約翰福音》第1 章補充註釋）。祂是創造主和君王，所以宇宙是祂的（約1:1,2；西1:15-17），但祂在地上的生活卻非常貧窮（太8:20）。祂的富足包括祂的神性和神的品質，數不清的星球，千萬天使的敬拜和忠誠。
**成了貧窮。**ptōcheuō，或“成為乞丐”。其相關名詞pto_chos見可12:42註釋。這裡所用的動詞時態指成為“貧窮”的舉動──道成肉身。基督完全倒空自己，一點兒也不保留原來的富足。祂披上人性並受制於人性的侷限性。祂貧窮到憑自己不能做什麼（約5:19,20；見卷五，917，918頁）。
**可以成為富足。**因著罪惡的入侵，人類失去了自己的家園，領土，品格，甚至是生命本身。現在人按本性是窮其一生來追求虛假的富足（見賽55:2；約6:27註釋）。永遠的貧窮正等待著那些沒有為自己積蓄財寶在天上的人（見太9:21；路12:21註釋）。基督來要救人脫離因尋求虛假的富足而來的貧窮（見《教會證言》卷三第401頁）。人只有在基督裡並通過基督，才能認識事物的真正價值，並接受在基督耶穌裡成為“富足”的權利。他們在祂裡面承受萬有（太6:20；羅8:17,32；林前1:5；弗1；3-5,10,11,18,19；2:6,7；見太6:33註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第71，332，341，519頁；《健康勉言》第318，320頁；《天路》第393頁；《給管家的勉言》第20，30，55，123，136，161，178，211，287頁；《基督教育之研究》第495頁；《歷代願望》第88，417頁；《佈道論》第240頁；《早期著作》第67頁；《福山寶訓》第83頁；《服務真詮》第105，501頁；《醫療佈道論》第19，321頁；《先知與君王》第652頁；《拾級就主》第79頁；《給傳道人的證言》第121，177頁；《證言》卷一第680頁；《證言》卷二第27，215，636，660頁；《證言》卷三第198，208，387，401，407，457，525，547頁；《證言》卷四第49，120，219，457，481，550，621，627頁；《證言》卷五第155，271，360，730頁；《證言》卷七第29，297頁；《證言》卷九第131，254頁；《論福利工作》第24頁。
9.en:
**Ye know.** Paul had fully declared to them the grace of Christ, and they knew it by experience with it, as the Greek makes evident, not simply as a tenet of belief. They had tasted, and thus they knew that the Lord is gracious. In fact, they themselves constituted living evidence of it. The grace of Christ must control the heart and will. It is never effective so long as it remains an intellectual concept only. For that matter, no divine truth is known merely by an intellectual understanding of it (see Matt. 16:17; John 6:45; 16:14; 1 Cor. 2:4; 12:3). The only man to whom the Word of God is truth is he who is taught and convinced by the Spirit. The riches we receive through the poverty of Christ come through spiritual illumination of the life.
**Grace.** See on Rom. 3:24. The supreme acts of Christ, His incarnation and crucifixion, are attributed to grace only here and in Rom. 5:15; Gal. 1:6. These acts constituted the supreme manifestations of divine love and condescension. Paul here contrasts the supreme sacrifice of Christ with man’s incomparably infinitesimal acts of charity.
**Lord Jesus Christ.** See on Matt. 1:1; John 1:38.
**He was rich.** An allusion to Christ’s preincarnate existence (see John 17:5; see on Phil. 2:6, 7; see Additional Note on John 1). Since He was Creator and King, the universe was His (John 1:1, 2; Col. 1:15–17), but His earthly life was ever one of extreme poverty (Matt. 8:20). His riches consisted of the nature and attributes of deity, of countless millions of worlds, of the adoration and loyalty of multitudes of angels.
**Became poor.** Gr. ptōcheuō, “to be [extremely] poor,” “to be a beggar.” For comment on ptōchos, the related noun, see on Mark 12:42. The verb tense here used points to the act of becoming “poor”—the incarnation. Christ so completely emptied Himself that He retained nothing of the riches that were once His. He took upon Himself human nature and became subject to the limitations of humanity. He became poor to the point where of Himself He could do nothing (John 5:19, 20; see Vol. V, pp. 917, 918).
**Might be rich.** With the coming of sin, man lost his home, his domain, his character, and even life itself. By nature, he now spends his life seeking false riches (see on Isa. 55:2; John 6:27). Eternal poverty awaits those who do not lay up treasure for themselves in heaven (see on Matt. 19:21; Luke 12:21). Christ came to deliver man from his poverty, which results from seeking false riches (see 3T 401). In and through Christ men are able to discern the true value of things, and receive the privilege of becoming “rich” in Christ Jesus. In Him they inherit all things (Matt. 6:20; Rom. 8:17, 32; 1 Cor. 1:5; Eph. 1:3–5, 10, 11, 18, 19; 2:6, 7; see on Matt. 6:33).

10.zh:
我在這事上把我的意見告訴你們，是於你們有益；因為你們下手辦這事，而且起此心意，已經有一年了，

**我的意見。**保羅沒有說“吩咐”他們（見第8節註釋）。他知道一個合理的判斷對於哥林多信徒來說，比強制性的命令更有分量。教會已經在進行捐獻，只需得到鼓勵實施其良好的意圖就行了。下命令是完全不合適的。
**是與你們有益。**保羅勸他們不要拖延完成他們一年前所開始的工作。為了他們自己的緣故，他們不該這樣做。拖延對於他們自己的基督徒經驗是有害的，並使他們受人批評。只要不涉及一個人基督徒的正直品格，對上帝所許的願就必須還（傳5:4-5）。
**已經有一年了。**自從哥林多的信徒開始為耶路撒冷教會募捐起，已過去一年了（林後9:2）。這項高尚的工作顯然因假使徒所引起的爭論和矛盾而中斷了。既然大多數人已重申對保羅的忠誠，這項工作就可以繼續了。見林後11:22註釋。
10.en:
**My advice.** Paul speaks not “by commandment” (see on v. 8). He knew that an expression of sound judgment would carry much more weight with the Corinthians than a peremptory order. The church had already committed itself to the offering, and needed only encouragement to revive and carry out its good intentions. A command would have been entirely out of place.
**This is expedient.** Paul’s counsel was that they should no longer delay completing what they had begun a year before. It was desirable for their own sake that they should not do so. To delay would be detrimental to their own Christian experience, and would leave them open to criticism. A vow made to God cannot be repudiated without involving a man’s Christian integrity (Eccl. 5:4–5).
**A year ago.** About a year had passed since the Corinthian believers had set out to raise funds for the church at Jerusalem (ch. 9:2). This noble project had evidently been interrupted by the contention and strife occasioned by the false apostles. Now that the majority had reaffirmed their loyalty to Paul the project could proceed once more. See on ch. 11:22.

11.zh:
如今就當辦成這事。既有願做的心，也當照你們所有的去辦成。

**辦成。**直譯是“完成”，就是完成他們所承諾的。
**願作的心。**樂意的心能使一點善行得蒙悅納。但是做力所不能及的事，就違背了樂意的精神。慷慨的意願本是好的，但還不夠。如果我們最好的願望和能力要用來鞏固和加強品格，這種意願就必須被體現在行動中。懷著慈善的理想是好的，但是理想必須得到實際的表達。信心和愛心若只是理想，那就決不能使飢餓的人飽足，赤身的人有衣穿（雅2:14-20）。所以“願作”是為上帝和同胞服務的自發傾向和思想態度，不需要別人強求或催促。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–12節）**。《使徒行述》第344頁。
11.en:
**Perform.** Literally, “complete,” that is, what they had already promised to do.
**Readiness to will.** A willing mind makes even a little acceptable, but to do less than one is able to do is a denial of willingness. A generous will is good in itself, but alone it is not enough. The will must be embodied in deeds, if our best desires and energies are to give solidity and strength to the character. It is good to cherish the ideal of charity, but the ideal must find practical expression. Faith and love, as ideals, never feed the hungry or clothe the naked (James 2:14–20). “Readiness,” then, is a spontaneous disposition and attitude of mind to serve God and one’s fellow men. It has no need of being urged or driven forward by the importunity of others.

12.zh:
因為人若有願做的心，必蒙悅納，乃是照他所有的，並不是照他所無的。

決定獻給上帝的禮物被接納的，是真誠樂意的心。上帝的問題是：你的心付出了多少。心如果沒有付出，手中所獻出的在上帝面前就沒有價值。上帝既不需要也不在乎我們的錢，錢對祂並無益處。一個人可能獻得很少一點，或者沒有，但是一顆樂意的心會使奉獻成聖。由於不可控制的環境，人最好的努力也可能失敗。他為上帝做工的心願可能因缺少機會而無法實現。但這並不會使他在天庭前受到指責。關於永遠獎賞的分配，見太20:1-16；25:14-46註釋。上帝所看重的，不是一個人擁有多少才幹，而是利用這些才幹時的獻身與忠誠。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第328頁；《給管家的勉言》第48，119頁；《今日的生活》第110頁；《給青年人的信息》第96頁；《論節制》第113頁；《證言》卷二第282，667頁；見徒16:14懷愛倫註釋。
12.en: **Willing mind.** It is the sincere willingness of the mind that determines the acceptableness of the gift to God. With God the question ever is, How much did your heart give? If the heart gives nothing, what the hands may offer is without value before God. God neither needs nor cares for our money, nor is He benefited by it. A man may have little or nothing to give, but a willing heart is what sanctifies the gift. A man’s best efforts may fail, due to circumstances beyond his control, or his desires to work for God may remain unfulfilled for lack of opportunity. But that need not cause him to stand condemned before Heaven. For comment on the basis upon which eternal rewards are to be meted out see on Matt. 20:1–16; 25:14–46. It is not the number of talents a man may have, but the devotion and faithfulness with which he improves them, that counts with God.

13.zh:
我原不是要別人輕省，你們受累，

保羅並不想讓要哥林多信徒承擔更多的擔子，以減輕其他教會的擔子。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一第178，179，205，324頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–15節）**。《先祖與先知》第295頁。
13.en: **Ye burdened.** Paul did not intend that the Corinthians should carry more than their share of the burden, to spare churches elsewhere the need of doing their fair share.

14.zh:
乃要均平，就是要你們的富餘，現在可以補他們的不足，使他們的富餘，將來也可以補你們的不足，這就均平了。

**均平。**保羅在這裡不是指財產或物品的平均，而是指付出相等的努力。哥林多信徒就其目前富裕的經濟狀況而言，能比貧困的馬其頓信徒做得更多（見1-5節註釋）。
**你們的不足。**哥林多信徒將來也可能遇到貧乏的日子，要讓其他人分擔大部分的擔子。聖經承認私有財產的權利和自願捐獻的權利，但也譴責對窮人自私冷漠的疏忽。即使有一位基督徒捐了大筆款，也不能免除其他人盡力捐獻的義務。世上財物不多的人沒有理由不履行他們相應的幫助別人的責任（參弗4:28；帖後3:12）。
14.en:
**An equality.** Paul does not here refer to an equality of property or goods, but to a proportionate equality of effort. In their present state of material prosperity the Corinthians were able to do much more than the Macedonians in their state of want (see on vs. 1–5).
**Your want.** There might come a time when the Corinthians would be in want and others would have to bear a larger share of the burden. The Scriptures recognize the right of private property and the right that all contributions shall be voluntary, but it also condemns the selfish and heartless neglect of the poor and needy. If one Christian gives a large sum, this does not relieve others from the obligation to contribute what they can. Those who have less of this earth’s goods are not to excuse themselves from doing their proportionate part to assist others (cf. Eph. 4:28; 2 Thess. 3:12).

15.zh:
如經上所記：多收的也沒有餘；少收的也沒有缺。

保羅引用在曠野中收嗎哪的故事（出16:17,18），來解釋14節所提出平均的原則。不管實際收穫多少，每一個人的需要都得到了滿足。基督教會也要實行這樣的原則，不是靠奇蹟的介入，而是靠對弟兄表現愛的精神。上帝的旨意是讓每一個人都得到生活所需的足夠物資。那些因自己的能力或機會收穫較多屬世財富的人，不應自私地享受自己富裕的財富，而要與貧乏的人分享（見路12:13-34註釋）。他們只是所擁有屬世財富的管家，而不是主人，應當用來為同胞服務（詩112:9；太25:14-46）。這樣就可以防止過多的財富或貧困所造成的罪惡。
15.en: **Gathered much.** To illustrate the principle of equalization set forth in v. 14, Paul alludes to the gathering of the manna in the wilderness (Ex. 16:17, 18). Irrespective of the amount actually gathered, each person had sufficient for his needs. The same principle is to operate in the Christian church, not by miraculous intervention but through the exercise of the spirit of love for one’s brethren. It is the will of God that each shall have a share of the material things of life adequate to his needs. It is also God’s will that those who, because of natural ability and opportunity, gather more of this world’s goods should not selfishly enjoy their superabundance, but share it with those in need (see on Luke 12:13–34). They are stewards, not outright owners, of the earthly benefits they have gathered, and are to use these for the welfare of their fellow men (Ps. 112:9; Matt. 25:14–46). In this way the evils that result from superabundant wealth and from poverty may both be prevented.

16.zh:
多謝神，感動提多的心，叫他待你們殷勤，像我一樣。

**多謝上帝。**保羅就這樣開始了書信的另一部分。他在1-15節向哥林多信徒提出了馬其頓信徒的高尚榜樣，闡述了基督徒慈善的真正原則。現在他開始解釋捐獻的實施細則。
**叫。**直譯為“給”，就是持續不斷地給。提多的熱心沒有衰退的危險。
**殷勤，像我一樣。**保羅首先對哥林多教會表揚提多，為提多參與他所提倡的捐獻而感恩。他們可以指望提多盡心盡意而殷勤地執行手頭的這項任務。
基督教的一個顯著特色，就是為人類實際和屬靈的福利而推進各項自我犧牲的事業。世界上慈善團體的工作，其根源和精神實際上都出於基督教。這種精神並不發源於人屬肉體的心，因為人心生來就是自私的。教會的偉大工作之一，將是讓人擺脫自我，並激勵他們真正關心別人的福利。基督徒當為教會而大大感謝上帝。教會不僅鼓舞信徒為其他人的貧乏而捐獻，也為他們的需要服務（太20:26,28）。提多在鼓勵哥林多人慷慨捐獻的事上，為他們做了真正的好事。哥林多人應當為這樣的機會感謝上帝，而不要設法規避為別人的得救和福利所發出的呼籲。
16.en:
**Thanks be to God.** Paul thus begins another section of his letter. In vs. 1–15 he has set before the Corinthians the noble example of the Macedonians and enunciated the true principles of Christian benevolence. He now proceeds to outline the practical details to be followed in completing the collection.
**Put.** Literally, “gives,” that is, keeps on giving, or continually gives. There is no danger that the zeal of Titus will wane.
**The same earnest care.** First, Paul commends Titus to the church at Corinth, expressing gratitude that Titus shares his own interest in the proposed collection. They can count on the diligent application of his mind and heart to the task at hand.
The impulse to self-sacrificing enterprises for the practical and spiritual welfare of humanity is pre-eminently Christian. The work of charity and philanthropy in the world is essentially Christian in its origin and spirit. Such a spirit does not originate in the human heart, for it is naturally selfish. It is part of the great work of the church to take men out of themselves and inspire them with a genuine concern for the welfare of others. Christians may well be grateful to God for the church, which inspires its members not merely to contribute to the needs of other members but also to minister to their needs (Matt. 20:26, 28). Titus would thus confer upon the Corinthians a true favor, in stimulating them to generous deeds. Instead of seeking to avoid appeals to give for the salvation and welfare of others, Christians should thank God for such opportunities.

17.zh:
他固然是聽了我的勸，但自己更是熱心，情願往你們那裡去。

**他固然是聽了我的勸。**提多欣然答應保羅的要求，前往哥林多教會，希望恢復教會從前的平安和睦的狀態。
**熱心。**保羅的話有雙重的意思。雖然捐獻是保羅發起的，但提多完全配合這項工作，與保羅一樣關心它的成功。這次催促不單出與保羅。提多顯然已表示自願參與哥林多的這項使命。
**往你們那裡去。**保羅說提多馬上就要前往哥林多，就像他已經去了──在讀這封書信的哥林多信徒看來。原文結構表明提多是《哥林多後書》的送信人。
17.en:
**He accepted the exhortation.** Titus had responded gladly to Paul’s appeal to go to Corinth in the hope of restoring the church to its former state of peace and unity.
**Forward.** Or, “earnest.” Paul’s words express a double meaning. Though the offering was initiated by Paul, Titus was fully in accord in this project and shared his concern for its success. The urging was not exclusively Paul’s. Evidently Titus had already volunteered to go on this mission to Corinth.
**He went.** Paul speaks of Titus’ impending departure for Corinth as if he had already gone—from the viewpoint of the Corinthians in reading this letter. This characteristic Greek mode of expression clearly points to Titus as the bearer of the second epistle.

18.zh:
我們還打發一位兄弟和他同去，這人在福音上得了眾教會的稱讚。

**還打發。**正要打發（見17節註釋）。
**一位弟兄。**保羅把亞該亞的募捐工作託付給三個人：提多和另外兩位沒有提到名字的弟兄。三位弟兄都是眾教會所信任的。這樣的安排是為了便於募捐，避免將捐款據為己用的猜疑。鑑於哥林多依然有少數人反對保羅，他沒有親自去募捐是明智的。無疑募集了相當一筆款項，因而要對教會作出完整的彙報，包括捐款的總數以及交給耶路撒冷的數目（見20,21節註釋）。保羅知道反對他的人會盡力找他麻煩。他特別勸勉福音傳道士在對待金錢的態度上要謹慎（提前3:3；彼前5:2）。
**這人在福音上得了眾教會的稱讚。**這位弟兄“在福音上”被證明是有效的工人，應該被尊為保羅和提多的同工。
18.en:
**Have sent.** That is, are sending (see on v. 17).
**The brother.** Paul entrusted the work of the collection in Achaia to three men, Titus and two others whose names are not given. All three enjoyed the confidence of the churches. This arrangement was designed to facilitate the collection and to protect all concerned with the collection against suspicion of appropriating funds thus collected to their own use. In view of the fact that a minority at Corinth still opposed Paul, it was better that he not collect the funds personally. Undoubtedly a considerable sum was collected, and a full report could thus be made back to the churches, both as to the amount given and as to its delivery at Jerusalem (see vs. 20, 21). Paul knew his opponents would find fault with him if they could. The minister of the gospel is specifically counseled to be discreet in his attitude toward money (1 Tim. 3:3; 1 Peter 5:2).
**Whose praise.** This brother had proved an effective laborer “in the gospel,” and should be respected as a worthy colaborer of Paul and Titus.

19.zh:
不但這樣，他也被眾教會挑選，和我們同行，把所託與我們的這捐貲送到了，可以榮耀主，又表明我們樂意的心。

**挑選。**cheirotoneo（見徒14:23註釋）。直譯是“伸手”，故有“選擇”之意，但沒有說明提多的這個同伴是如何任命的。
**行。**指耶路撒冷之行，與保羅等人一起把從馬其頓和希臘所募集的款項交給耶路撒冷的弟兄。
捐貨。如4-7節一樣，該詞在本節指幫助耶路撒冷窮人的慈善事業。這是上帝恩典的一種表現（第1節）。
**榮耀主。**所提倡的為耶路撒冷聖徒募捐能引人將榮耀歸給主。耶路撒冷的人將要稱頌上帝讓福音引導外邦人如此切實地關心他們的困境。外邦人也將從幫助基督徒同道需要的工作中得到喜樂。
**我們樂意的心。**有文本為“我們的熱心”。這項工作除了有利於耶路撒冷的窮苦聖徒，以及為他們提供幫助的外邦眾教會之外，還將向猶大地的猶太籍基督徒表明，保羅在為外邦人工作的同時並沒有忘記他們。這項工作將猶太人和外邦人的心連一起，使他們合為一體，有助於拆毀將他們分開的“中間隔斷的牆”（弗2:14）。
19.en:
**Chosen.** Gr. cheirotoneō (see on Acts 14:23). Although the word means, literally, “to stretch out the hand,” and thus “to elect,” its usage leaves uncertain the manner in which this companion of Titus was appointed.
**Travel.** That is, to Jerusalem, in company with Paul and others, to deliver to the brethren there the funds thus collected in Macedonia and in Greece.
**Grace.** As in vs. 4–7, the word here refers to the charitable enterprise of assisting the poor at Jerusalem, which was an expression of the grace of God (v. 1).
**To the glory.** The proposed collection for the saints at Jerusalem would lead men to glorify God. Those at Jerusalem would praise Him that the gospel had led the Gentiles to take so practical an interest in their needy condition, and the Gentiles would find joy in ministering to the needs of their fellow Christians.
**Your ready mind.** Textual evidence attests (cf. p. 10) the reading “our readiness of mind,” or “our zeal.” In addition to the good that would come to the poor saints at Jerusalem and to the Gentile churches in thus making provision for their needs, the project would also demonstrate to Jewish Christians in Judea that in his labors for the Gentiles Paul had not forgotten them. The project would bind the hearts of Jew and Gentile together and tend to unite them in one fellowship. This would help to break down “the middle wall of partition” (Eph. 2:14) that separated them.

20.zh:
這就免得有人因我們收的捐銀很多，就挑我們的不是。

**這就免得。**保羅要避免任何指控他從這項工作中謀取個人利益的把柄。在錢財的事務上，嚴格的誠實往往還不夠。最小的疏忽也可能成為批評的口實。基督的傳道人在處理錢財的問題時要特別謹慎（參提前3:3；彼前5:2）。
**很多。**或“慷慨”。鑑於保羅對比較富裕的哥林多教會的期望，這次募捐很有可能取得成功。哥林多人普遍被認為是富裕的，正如俗話所說：“不是每一個人都能假裝在哥林多生活。”
**挑我們的的不是。**或“責備”，暗示有人指控保羅在受託的資金上沒有實行嚴格的誠實。
20.en:
**Avoiding this.** Or, “taking precautions about this.” Paul sought to avoid any basis for the charge that he was making a personal profit from the project. Strict honesty may not always be sufficient in money matters, where the least carelessness may become the occasion for criticism. The Christian minister, especially, must exercise scrupulous care in handling money matters (cf. 1 Tim. 3:3; 1 Peter 5:2).
**Blame.** Or, “reproach,” here implying that someone might charge that Paul had not been strictly honest with the funds entrusted to him.
**Abundance.** Or, “liberality.” The collection had every appearance of proving successful, taking into account what Paul anticipated from the comparatively well-to-do Corinthian church. The Corinthians were popularly considered wealthy people, as reflected in the proverb, “Not every man can pretend to live in Corinth.”

21.zh:
我們留心行光明的事，不但在主面前，就在人面前也是這樣。

**光明的。**就是良善的，值得羨慕的，美麗的，名副其實的，值得尊敬的，在本節指擁有卓越愛心之人的行為。他們因此在別人面前享有良好的聲譽，由於他們令人羨慕的舉止而享有崇高的威望。基督徒不僅被稱為聖潔，誠實和純潔的，還要“在人前”被承認為擁有聖潔，誠實，純潔之美。真正的基督徒在上帝和人面前都要表現出美好的、吸引人的生活方式（羅12:17；腓4:8；彼前2:12）。本節引用了七十士譯本的箴3:4。
**懷愛倫註釋**。見羅12:17懷愛倫註釋。
21.en: **Honest.** That is, good, admirable, beautiful, meaning what looks and is honorable. Here it denotes the conduct of one who possesses the excellence of love and thus enjoys a good reputation before others, one held in high esteem for his admirable conduct. Christians are not only called to be holy, honest, and pure, but “also in the sight of men” are to be recognized as having the beauty of holiness, honesty, and purity. The true Christian is to exemplify before both God and man a beautiful and attractive way of life (Rom. 12:17; Phil. 4:8; 1 Peter 2:12). This verse is a quotation from the LXX translation of Prov. 3:4.

22.zh:
我們又打發一位兄弟同去；這人的熱心，我們在許多事上屢次試驗過。現在他因為深信你們，就更加熱心了。

提多的這個同伴和18節的那個人一樣無法辯明身份。但有人提出是推基古。他是陪保羅一同帶著捐獻上耶路撒冷的代表之一（徒20:4）。保羅在其他地方稱推基古為“所親愛忠心事奉主的兄弟”（弗6:21；西4:7）。保羅視推基古為他最信任的使者之一，後來派他執行許多重要的任務（提後4:12；多3:12）。
22.en: **Our brother.** It is no more possible to identify this companion of Titus than the one of v. 18. However, some have suggested Tychicus, who was a member of the delegation that accompanied Paul to Jerusalem with the contribution (Acts 20:4). Elsewhere Paul speaks of Tychicus as a “beloved brother and faithful minister” (Eph. 6:21; Col. 4:7). Paul considered Tychicus as one of his most trusted messengers, and later sent him upon various important missions (2 Tim. 4:12; Titus 3:12).

23.zh:
論到提多，他是我的同伴，一同為你們勞碌的。論到那兩位兄弟，他們是眾教會的使者，是基督的榮耀。

**提多。**保羅在這裡稱讚這三位蒙揀選指導募捐工作的人是他們所信任的勤勞的人。他全權委託他們，免得哥林多的任何派別質疑他們的動機。他們是完全值得信任的，應受到接納。提多最先提到，顯然是他們的組長的，和保羅的個人代表。提多後來在早期基督教會中擔任了重要的領導職位（多1:1-5；2:15）。
**使者。**直譯是“使徒”，或“奉差遣（執行使命）的人”。就這次募捐而言，這個稱呼授予他們與保羅自己同等的權威（林後1:1），但不一定賦予他們永久的使徒稱號和職分。
**基督的榮耀。**這三個人要被尊為基督個人的代表。他們的使命有利於基督的榮耀。保羅給了他們再高不過的評價。
23.en:
**Titus.** Paul here commends the three men chosen to direct the work of the collection as men of diligence in whom they may have confidence. He invests them with full authority, lest any of the factions at Corinth should be disposed to question their motives. They are all fully accredited and are to be so accepted. Titus is mentioned first, evidently as chairman of the group, and Paul’s personal representative. Titus later eventually filled an important post of leadership in the early Christian church (Titus 1:1–5; 2:15).
**Messengers.** Literally, “apostles,” or “ones dispatched [on a mission].” This designation invests them with authority equivalent to that of Paul himself (ch. 1:1), so far as the collection is concerned. It does not necessarily confer upon them the permanent title or office of apostle.
**Glory of Christ.** These three men are to be accorded the utmost respect as personal representatives of Christ. Their commission will redound to the glory of Christ. Paul could have given these men no higher commendation.

24.zh:
所以，你們務要在眾教會面前顯明你們愛心的憑據，並我所誇獎你們的憑據。

保羅要求哥林多信徒履行自己的職責，為其他地方的基督徒樹立一個值得效法的榜樣。他們所抱的態度，所作出的貢獻，對這些代表的接待，肯定會傳到其他教道。哥林多信徒在募捐事務上的表現是公開的。教會的名譽處在重要關頭。他們唯一合適的反應就是全心全意地配合基督的使者，慷慨地捐助猶大窮苦的基督徒。
地上的每一個教會都代表上帝的國，因此成了天使和人觀看的一臺戲（林前4:9）。上帝賜給這個國度每一個公民的恩典或福氣，決不單是為他們自己享用的，無論是真理，個人與基督交往的經歷，還是上帝所提供物質的福分。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給管家的勉言》第29頁。
24.en:
**Shew ye.** Paul challenges the Corinthians to measure up to their responsibility to set an example worthy of emulation by Christians elsewhere. The attitude they took, the contribution they made, the treatment they accorded these delegates, would inevitably become known to the other churches. The Corinthians were on public exhibition in this matter of the collection. Their honor as a church was at stake. The only proper response on their part would be one of wholehearted cooperation with the messengers of Christ and of generosity toward the poor Christians in Judea.
Every church on earth is representative of the kingdom of God, and thus a spectacle to angels and to men (1 Cor. 4:9). No subject of this kingdom has been entrusted with God’s gifts or blessings simply for his own use, whether it be truth, personal experience with Christ, or the material blessings of God’s providence.

0.zh:
**一、卷名**
寫於大約公元3世紀，現存最古的抄本中就有《哥林多後書》這一簡短的卷名。“保羅達哥林多人後書”這一較長的卷名是以後才有的。至於這封信是不是致哥林多教會的第二封信，為什麼用“後書”這樣的稱呼，見下文“歷史背景”項。原來的書信顯然沒有卷名。
**二、作者**
內證和外證都證明保羅是書信的作者。外證可以追溯到使徒以後的那個時代。早期教父常引用和提到這封書信，這充分證明了其真實性和完整性。距這封書信寫作約35年以後（公元95年），羅馬的克萊門特在寫給哥林多教會的信中談到了保羅所述及的同樣狀況（克萊門特致哥林多前書46章）。哥林多教會顯然沒有發生很大的變化，許多老的問題依然存在。士每拿主教波利卡普於公元155年寫給腓立比教會的信中，引用了林後8:21（6章）。里昂的主教伊裡奈烏於公元180年寫的文章《反異端論》中，引用和註釋了林後12:2-4保羅關於到第三層天中的歡樂。亞歷山大的克萊門特（公元200年）引用哥林多後書不少於20次（《雜記》卷一1.2章，卷二19:20章等）。所謂拉丁神學之父，迦太基的德爾圖良曾經多次引用哥林多後書（《駁馬西昂》5:11,12；《論肉身復活》40,43,44章；Scorpiace 13章）。
內證準確無誤地指證保羅為作者。書信的文體符合保羅的風格。書信多次提到保羅自己，提到他在哥林多的經歷和他致哥林多的前一封信。許多聖經學者認為這封書信最清楚，最完整地表現了保羅的氣質，個性和風格。記在這封書信中的經驗非常自然而真實。
**三、歷史背景**
保羅至少去過哥林多三次，寫了三封，也許是四封信。第一次訪問哥林多是在他的第二次傳道行程中，約於公元51年（徒18:11），在那裡工作了一年半，建立和組織了教會。以後他經常派代表繼續與哥林多教會保持聯繫（林後12:17）。在林前5:9中提到了他寫給哥林多教會的第一封信。這封信據說已失傳。他第三次外出傳道時在以弗所工作了兩年多快要結束時，寫了這封《哥林多前書》（16:8）。
一般認為，《哥林多前書》和《哥林多後書》相隔幾個星期。前書發自以弗所，後書發自馬其頓。保羅原想留在以弗所待到五旬節，再經馬其頓前往哥林多（徒19:21）。可是他比原來的打算早一些離開以弗所。這大部分是因為群眾的暴亂差點要了他的命（徒19:24-41）。他在以弗所時所遭遇的迫害使他負擔極重。他稱反對真理的人為“野獸”（林前15:32），說自己“被壓太重，力不能勝，甚至連活命的指望都沒有了”（林後1:8）。保羅就是在這種狀況下離開以弗所前往馬其頓的。
他來到了特羅亞，以便從這個港口出發前往馬其頓。他在特羅亞等候提多回來，以便了解哥林多教會對他前一封信的反應。可是提多沒有在他預計的時間裡回來。保羅心情焦慮，掛念著哥林多教會，以致無法利用敞開的門戶在特羅亞傳福音（林後2:13）。他趕往馬其頓，在腓立比遇見提多，聽到了提多帶來的的關於哥林多教會的好消息，便放了心，滿心高興。
有人認為保羅曾回到哥林多作第二次的訪問。他談到了前一次令人失望的訪問（見林後2:1；林後12:14；1林後3:1,2）。也許是這一次訪問進一步瞭解了哥林多令人難受的消息以後，他寫了一封責備和規勸的信（《哥林多前書》），並派提多去為他計劃中的下一次訪問作準備（林後8:6；林後13:1,2；參《使徒行述》301頁）。
在林後2:4中保羅提到寫前一封信時“心裡難過痛苦”，結果使哥林多信徒“憂愁”（林後7:8）。許多學者認為保羅在這些章節和其他章節所提到的不大可能指《哥林多前書》，因為他們主張上述說法與《哥林多前書》的精神和風格不符。於是他們說在新約的兩封致哥林多書信之間一定還有一封信。從這點出發，一些人認為該信已失傳，另一些人認為這就是哥林多後書10-13章。雙方都提出了似乎有理的理由，可是都缺乏客觀的證據。本註釋認為《哥林多後書》所提到的正是《哥林多前書》（參《使徒行述》324頁）。據林後2:13；林後7:5；林後8:1；林後9:2,4，顯然保羅是在馬其頓寫了這第二封書信，時間大約在公元57年。
保羅的書信和訪問至少暫時達到了目的。根據羅16:23，保羅得到了該教會一位主要成員的熱情接待。在加拉太書和羅馬書中進一步證實了哥林多教會所發生的變化。這兩封信是他在哥林多期間寫的，透露出他在特羅亞時哥林多的教會曾嚴重影響他的熱心，現在卻已從不安，憂慮和焦急中恢復過來（林後2:13；參林後7:6,13,14）。此外，哥林多教會為耶路撒冷聖徒的募捐也提供了一個很好的結論（羅15:26）。
保羅寫了《哥林多後書》，又訪問了哥林多以後。關於哥林多教會，我們只有零星的資料。然而，公元95年左右羅馬的克萊門特寫給哥林多的一封信，透露出至少有一部分舊惡習又死灰復燃了。克萊門特確實讚揚了該教會在許多方面值得效仿的行為，可他也責備了它結黨紛爭的精神。這是我們手頭有關使徒時代哥林多教會最後一點資料。
**四、主題**
提多從哥林多帶來鼓舞人心的消息，促使保羅寫這封信。信的前面部分講到哥林多教會如何接受他的前一封信，回顧了上一次所討論的若干問題。遵照保羅的指示，教會已經開除了亂倫的人（林前5:1-5；參林後2:6）。現在他指示如何得回犯錯的人。
信中強調了馬其頓和希臘各教會為窮人募集的捐款。保羅很關心這個計劃，因它會使外邦和猶太的基督徒團結在一起。外邦的信徒通過這個計劃會看到猶太基督徒為把福音傳給他們而作出的犧牲，而猶太信徒也會看到，這些奉獻無聲而有力的見證了弟兄相愛的精神。然而哥林多教會在這件募捐的工作上疏忽了，遠遠落後於馬其頓的各教會，也許是因為專注於份爭和不良行為的結果。在這封信保羅發出最後的呼籲，要求他們立即行動起來。
哥林多教會的大部分信徒，似乎都接受了保羅和他同工的勸告。他們伸開雙臂接待了提多。這個教會幾乎從開始就分了派。一些人擁護一位領袖，一些人擁護另一位領袖。由這種分派而造成的麻煩已經減輕了，可是，類似於加拉太所存在的那一派主張猶太化的人似乎仍在公開而惡毒地反對。他們的目的就是推翻保羅的工作、權威和使徒的身分。反對派指控保羅反覆無常，沒有如約前來哥林多。他們說他缺乏使徒的權威。他們說他是膽小鬼，企圖在遠方用書信來控制教會。他們說他不敢親自前來。
哥林多後書的前九章主要是感謝和稱讚，後四章則比較嚴肅地替自己辯護。有人說前幾章是寫給接受保羅規勸和責備的多數人，後幾章是寫給那些反對他在教會中恢復和睦精神的少數人。保羅千方百計地證實自己的權威，為自己在他們中間的做法辯解。為了證實自己的使徒身份，他談到了自己從主所領受的啟示和異象，他為主耶穌所受無比的苦楚，以及蓋在他工作成果上上帝悅納的印章。保羅在給哥林多教會的信中講到某些假使徒，也許就是教會中的少數成員時所用言辭之厲，至今仍有其影響力，這是在他給其他教會的書信中所沒有的。
這封信的內容與《哥林多前書》大不一樣。前書較為客觀和實際。後書則較主觀帶有個人風格。前書的語氣鎮定而謹慎，後書則反映了保羅急於盼待哥林多的消息，提多來到後給他帶來的寬慰和歡樂，以及他有效地處理教會中問題的堅定宗旨。前書反映了哥林多教會的情況，後書表現了使徒對教會的熱情。雖然後書的主要目的不是談論教義，象羅馬書和加拉太書那樣，但它仍闡明瞭一些重要的教會真理。

**1. Title.** Textual evidence attests (cf. p. 10) the brief title Pros Korinthious B, literally, “To the Corinthians 2.” This is the title that appears in the oldest extant manuscript of the epistle, dating from about the 3d century .. The longer title, “The Second Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians,” is not found until much later. For a discussion of this epistle as the “second” one to the Corinthians, and for the use of the word “second” in the title, see below under “3. Historical Setting.” Obviously the title was not a part of the original document.
**2. Authorship.** External and internal evidence conclusively attest Pauline authorship. The external evidence reaches back to the generation immediately following that of the apostles themselves. Quotations from, and references to, this epistle by many of the early Church Fathers and writers provide abundant testimony to its genuineness and integrity. In his letter to the Corinthians (c. .. 95), about 35 years after this epistle, Clement of Rome deals with the same conditions at Corinth as those here considered by Paul (First Epistle of Clement to the Corinthians 46). The Corinthian church had apparently not changed to any great extent, for many of the old problems still persisted. Writing to the Philippians, Polycarp (d. c. .. 155), bishop of Smyrna, quotes 2 Cor. 8:21 (Epistle 6). In his treatise Against Heresies ii. 30. 7 (c. .. 180), Irenaeus, bishop of Lyons, quotes and comments upon Paul’s account of his rapture to the third heaven in 2 Cor. 12:2–4. Clement of Alexandria (c. .. 200) quotes from 2 Corinthians not less than 20 times (see Stromata i. 1, 11; ii. 19, 20; etc.). Tertullian, of Carthage (c. .. 220), the so-called father of Latin theology, quotes frequently from it (Scorpiace 13; Against Marcion v. 11, 12 On the Resurrection of the Flesh 40, 43, 44).
Internal evidence points unmistakably to Paul as the author. Its style is that of Paul. The epistle abounds with references to Paul, to his experiences at Corinth, and to his first epistle to the church there. Many Biblical scholars consider that this epistle gives the clearest and most complete picture of Paul’s nature, personality, and disposition. The historical spontaneity of the experiences recorded in this epistle can be none other than genuine.
**3. Historical Setting.** Paul made at least three visits, and wrote three, perhaps four, epistles to the church at Corinth. The first visit, about .. 51, during the course of his Second Missionary Journey, continued for a year and a half (Acts 18:11). At this time Paul founded and organized the church. He continued to keep in touch with it from time to time through representatives (2 Cor. 12:17). His first written contact with it is mentioned in 1 Cor. 5:9. This document is now presumed lost. Toward the close of more than two years spent at Ephesus, on the third journey, he wrote what is now known as First Corinthians (ch. 16:8; see p. 103).
It is generally accepted that a period of several weeks probably elapsed between the writing of the two Corinthian epistles, the first from Ephesus and the second from Macedonia. Paul had intended to remain in Ephesus until Pentecost, and then to journey to Corinth by way of Macedonia (Acts 19:21). But he left Ephesus sooner than he had intended. This may have been due, in part at least, to the popular uprising that nearly cost him his life (vs. 24–41). The opposition he experienced while at Ephesus placed a great strain upon him. He referred to the opponents of truth as “beasts” (1 Cor. 15:32), and observed that he had been “pressed out of measure, above strength” and had “despaired even of life” (2 Cor. 1:8). It was in this condition that Paul left Ephesus for Macedonia.
He journeyed to Troas, the port of embarkation for Macedonia. Here he expected the return of Titus with a report of the response of the Corinthians to his previous epistle. But Titus did not arrive within the time expected, and Paul, finding no rest of spirit because of anxiety for the church at Corinth (ch. 2:13), was unable to take advantage of the open door to the preaching of the gospel at Troas. Pressing on into Macedonia, he met Titus at Philippi. With relief and joy Paul listened to the good news Titus brought from Corinth.
Some think that Paul had returned to Corinth for a second visit. He speaks of a previous visit that had been distressing and disappointing (see on chs. 2:1; 12:14; 13:1, 2). Probably following such a visit and the receipt of further disconcerting news from Corinth (1 Cor. 1:11), he dispatched a letter of reprimand and counsel (1 Corinthians), and sent Titus to prepare the way for a further visit he planned to make (2 Cor. 8:6; 13:1, 2; cf. AA 301).
In ch. 2:4 Paul refers to a former letter he had written to Corinth “out of much affliction and anguish of heart,” and which had made them “sorry” (ch. 7:8). Many scholars think that in these and others passages Paul can hardly refer to 1 Corinthians, since—as they affirm—these statements do not properly describe the spirit and nature of that epistle. Accordingly, they argue that he must have written a letter between the two that appear in the NT. Some who hold this view consider that this letter has been lost, but others think that it is preserved as chs. 10–13 of 2 Corinthians. Plausible reasons can be presented both for and against this theory, but objective proof is lacking for either. This commentary therefore assumes that 1 Corinthians is the letter to which Paul refers in 2 Corinthians (cf. AA 324). From chs. 2:13; 7:5; 8:1; 9:2, 4, it appears that Paul wrote this second epistle while in Macedonia. The date was about .. 57 (see pp. 102–104).
Temporarily, at least, Paul’s letters and visits seem to have accomplished their purpose. It is evident from Rom. 16:23 that Paul was hospitably received and entertained by one of the chief members of the church. The change in the church at Corinth is further corroborated by the fact that in the epistles to the Galatians and to the Romans, which were written during the course of his stay at Corinth, he gives evidence of having recovered from the state of restless anxiety and solicitude for the Corinthian church that distressed his ardent soul at Troas (2 Cor. 2:13; cf. ch. 7:6, 13, 14). Also, the collection in Corinth for the saints at Jerusalem came to a successful conclusion (Rom. 15:26).
After the writing of this second epistle and his next visit, we find only scattered references to the Corinthian church. However, an epistle to the Corinthians by Clement of Rome about .. 95 reveals that at least some of the old evils had reappeared. Clement does compliment the church for its exemplary conduct in many ways, but he also rebukes it for its strife and party spirit. This is the last information we have concerning the church at Corinth during the apostolic age.
**4. Theme.** The immediate occasion for the epistle was the encouraging report Titus had brought from Corinth. The first part of the letter deals with the reception the Corinthians had given Paul’s former epistle, and reviews some of the problems dealt with in it. Following Paul’s instructions the church had disfellowshiped the immoral offender of 1 Corinthians (1 Cor. 5:1–5; cf. 2 Cor. 2:6). Paul now advises how to win back the offender.
The contributions gathered among the churches of Macedonia and Greece for the poor are given special emphasis. This project lay close to Paul’s heart, for it would bind the hearts of Jewish and Gentile Christians together in a bond of fellowship and unity. On their part, the Gentile believers would be led to appreciate the sacrifices of Jewish Christians in bringing them a knowledge of the gospel. In turn, the Jews would be led to appreciate the spirit of fellowship to which the gifts bore mute, yet eloquent witness. But the church at Corinth had been delinquent in collecting their contribution, and far behind the churches of Macedonia, probably as a result of the strife and vice that had absorbed its attention. In this letter Paul makes a final appeal for promptness and diligence.
It seems that a majority of the Corinthian church members heartily accepted the counsel given by Paul and his colaborers. They had received Titus with open arms. Almost from the first there had been factions in the church, some favoring one leader and some another. Much of the trouble occasioned by this division of loyalty had been allayed, but open and malignant opposition, probably by a Judaizing faction similar to the one in Galatia, persisted. Its objective was to undermine Paul’s work, authority, and apostleship. Opponents charged Paul with fickleness for not coming to Corinth as he had originally promised. They argued that he lacked apostolic authority. They branded him a coward for attempting to control the church at a distance, by letter. This proved, they said, that he was afraid to appear in person.
The first nine chapters of 2 Corinthians are characterized by gratitude and appreciation; the last four, by marked severity and self-defense. It has been suggested that the former chapters were addressed to the majority, who had accepted Paul’s counsel and reproof, and the latter to a minority who persisted in opposing his efforts to restore the church to a spirit of harmony. At length, and in various ways, Paul essays to prove his authority and vindicate his conduct among them. For proof of his apostleship he appeals to his visions and revelations from the Lord, to his unparalleled sufferings for the Lord Jesus, and to the seal of divine approval evident in the fruitfulness of his labors. The severity of Paul’s words, addressed to the Corinthian church concerning certain false apostles and possibly a minority of its members still under their influence, is without parallel in his epistles to other churches.
This epistle differs materially from 1 Corinthians. The first epistle is objective and practical; the second, largely subjective and personal. The first is more calm and measured in tone; the second reflects Paul’s anxiety for news from Corinth, his relief and joy when Titus finally arrived, and his firm purpose to deal effectively with those who still troubled the church. The first reflects conditions in the Corinthian church; the second, the passion of the apostle himself for the church. Although the main concern of this second epistle is not doctrinal, as with Galatians and Romans, it does set forth important doctrinal truths.
**5. Outline.** I. Introduction, 1:1–11. A. Salutation, 1:1, 2. B. Thanksgiving in the midst of tribulation, 1:3–11. II. Recent Relations With the Church at Corinth, 1:12 to 7:16. A. An explanation of the change in travel plans, 1:12 to 2:4. B. Counsel for restoring the immoral offender to Christ, 2:5–11. C. Anxiety to have, and joy upon receiving, news from Corinth, 2:12–17. D. Apostolic credentials, 3:1–18. 1. Paul’s credentials as a genuine apostle, 3:1–6. 2. The glory of the apostolic commission, 3:7–18. E. The apostles sustained by divine power in their ministry, 4:1 to 5:10. 1. Strength to endure: an evidence of divine grace, 4:1–18. 2. Life and death in view of eternity, 5:1–10. F. The ministry of reconciliation, 5:11 to 6:10. 1. The apostle as an ambassador for Christ, 5:11–21. 2. The discipline essential to apostleship, 6:1–10. G. An appeal to the Corinthians to separate from evildoers, 6:11 to 7:1. H. Paul’s rejoicing at the warm response of the Corinthians, 7:2–16. III. The Collection for Needy Christians in Judea, 8:1 to 9:15. A. The exemplary liberality of the Macedonian churches, 8:1–6. B. The example of Jesus Christ, 8:7–15. C. The commission and commendation of Titus to receive the offering at Corinth, 8:16–24. D. An appeal to the Corinthians to do their part, 9:1–15. 1. An appeal to complete the collection of funds, 9:1–5. 2. An appeal to liberality, 9:6–15. IV. Paul’s Defense of His Apostleship; An Appeal to the Unrepentant, 10:1 to 13:10. A. A reply to those who have belittled Paul as an apostle, 10:1–12. B. Corinth within his appointed sphere of labor, 10:13–18. C. Marks of difference between true and false apostles, 11:1 to 12:18. 1. The subtlety of false apostles, 11:1–6. 2. Paul not dependent upon the Corinthians for support, 11:7–15. 3. His encounter with peril and privation, 11:16–33. 4. Paul the recipient of divine revelations, 12:1–5. 5. Paul humbled by “a thorn in the flesh,” 12:6–10. 6. Paul not enriched at their expense, 12:11–18. D. A final appeal to the unrepentant, 12:19 to 13:10. V. Conclusion, 13:11–14.
